unit: base part pipeline: §4 generation pipeline, §10 simulation and content, PART II, PART III
fields_note: items: id, kind, statement (our words, exact values), stated_in (every place in the unit, with line numbers), subject_owner (unit | base part | volume), owner_class, volumes (the volume subjects the item names), wiring (what it reads or is produced by; what reads, uses, renders, exports, tests or calls it; in-unit links by inventory id), decision_and_provenance_ids, restated_in_unit, note (flags). The unit is the base; "pipeline hook / Vxx" means the base carries the hook and the volume builds the other end.

items.statement: Generation is a fixed sequence of stages, each with typed inputs and outputs, its own random stream, its own time budget and a short fallback ladder; order: ground and water, demand, main roads between real places, side streets, districts typed before lanes are cut, wall traced from the stage it encloses, then blocks, plots, owners, buildings, fields, greenery, names
items.note: plain-words summary; normative content is 0002-0004

items.statement: Stage graph: S0 Blueprint → S1 Site → S2 Programme → S3 Siting, reservations, stage-1 boundary+trace → S4 Backbone → S5 stage k=1…K (S5a boundary+trace+gates; S5b main-road step; S5c secondary growth; S5d capacity check, one bounded top-up) → S6 Districts, quarters, field pass 1 → S7 wall strips + fortification lines → S7b Allocation + district claims → S12a Hinterland siting (no geometry) → S8 Infill per district → S9 Corridors (L2; districts + hinterland) → S10a Block allocation + field pass 2 → S10 (0) shared-edge bands (eager, both sides; margin bands 2 m a side on perimeter and shared reservation boundaries) → per district in the derivation pool and the hinterland unit on the generation worker, merged in lineage order: S10 Plots → S10b Placement → S11 Site plans + footprints → S12b Greenery (own faces only) → S12c Character (town-wide, after merge) → S13a Names + label candidates → S14 Display list → S15 Simulation (optional); S13b label placement is view data per zoom stop, never in the model

items.statement: Registration and order (COV-VG-VN-002): each stage registers a StageDecl (§4.12); the pipeline is the DAG the declared inputs/outputs induce, topologically sorted with stage id as deterministic tie-break; the base's registrations yield exactly the drawn order; a cycle is a registration error caught at load; a later product may register a stage the base lacks (village density stage before its network, palisade before roads) without editing the pipeline

wiring.read_by: PART III village stages; V07 village stages; §14 Stage extends StageDecl; §13.2 load test

items.statement: Each growth stage k runs S5a–S5d in order; the same S5 runs incrementally for an epoch (§4.11)

Op form (StageDecl.txForm, the transaction form of §3.3): callback for S5c, S8, S10 (ops read faces earlier ops made); declared for S3, S4, S5a, S5b, S7, S9, S11 and an edit's inserted feature; every other stage (S6, S7b, S12b, the hinterland unit's stages) registers callback, which is always safe

Why this order (a): water before roads — every carved water body (harbour basins, canals, castle and city moats, hinterland decoration ponds) enters L0 at S3 with the decks its crossings need, so no street is laid on ground that later becomes water and no route meets water without a deck (C12; GEO-19); the one later water body, an outer enceinte's moat, is carved by S5a through §4.11's carve path before that stage's secondaries grow, meeting only arterials through its gates

wiring.read_by: S4/S5 routing; §13.2 invariant no way on water without deck

items.statement: Why this order (b): programme before layout — buildings and people decided before geometry (FTG demand side); geometry answers with capacity (O7)

Why this order (c): large claims before streets — S3's reservations (§4.2 S3 (12)) enter L1 as barrier faces before S4 commits any way (MFP-3); claims larger than one block, large institutions among them, are cut out at S7b before S8 cuts lanes (§4.5 S7b (3); FTG-3)
items.note: earlier CF-PIPE-01 now resolved in text

items.statement: Why this order (d): walls before the streets they enclose — first enceinte is one construction at S3; each later stage's boundary and trace fixed in S5a, gates first, before its secondaries grow, so a secondary never crosses a wall except at a gate and intramural fabric inherits the wall's direction (GEO-18, MFP-2; J-P3)

Why this order (e): districts and field pass 1 before infill (infill block band is the district class's, J-2); S7's wall strips before S8 so no lane planned through a wall's band and setback; S12a before S10b so farms, mills, quarries have outside sites (FTG-7); greenery after site plans (reads yards and claims)

Laziness contract (LC-2, FTG-1; J-P9): a stage may run lazily for scope X (district, block, tile) only if its output for X is a pure function of eager upstream state and X's own sub-streams, reads no other scope's lazy output, writes nothing outside X

wiring.read_by: lazy derivation in viewer §8.6; §6.5 (9) derived-complete digest test; elaboration trigger policy (0032)

items.statement: Everything that decides the town's content is eager and town-wide: S2's roster, S3's reservations, S6's field bands, S7b's and S10a's allocations (S10a writes each district's band range, §4.5, item 72), S12a's hinterland siting, and S10's shared-edge step (0) (bands on L1 edges two face sets share; J-I9)

The per-district stages S10, S10b, S11, S12b (every district and the hinterland unit) may run lazily or in the pool; they read the eager records and their own sub-stream only and write only inside their own faces; S12b plants avenue and street-tree rows only in its own half-corridor strips; an edge orchard is a hinterland allocation row built by the hinterland unit, never by the district (§4.9); so any derivation order gives the same model (CI §6.5 (9))

S8 is eager: runs in the generation worker district by district in lineage order; its only writes outside a district's own faces are vertices where its lanes end on a bounding spine, each a baseLane portal in the shared Seam record (§4.6, II.1)

wiring.read_by: Seam record (II.1; model §2.5); stage-2 close-up V01

items.statement: S12c is eager and town-wide: runs on the generation worker after the pool's merge, reads every district's placements and buildings (the one-click path derives every district) and writes only the districts' derived character records (§4.5, item 72), so no derivation order changes it

items.statement: Transactions — one level per batch (§3.3), per stage: S1 L0 (arena outer ring = frame + context margin, one closed chain carrying structural margin role on the arena's Terrain entity, then water faces, shores, banks, islets, every crossing site's two pinned deck_end bank vertices); S3 L0 (harbour basins, canals, castle moat, city moat, decoration ponds, deck bank vertices of every carved channel) then L1 (map border = frame rectangle §3.2 (9), one closed chain with structural border role on arena Terrain entity, laid across land and water, no L0 edge added; land reservations as barrier faces, independent ops of one declared batch); S4 L0 only when F-ROUTE extra-bridge fires on standing water (two deck_end vertices by same-level shore splits, nothing cleared) then L1 arterial spines inserted once through deck ends (those bridges become built); S5 per k: k=1 S5a L1 S3's trace with gate vertices; k≥2 S5b L0 only for extra bridge, S5b L1 main roads (picked on boundary, data), S5a L1 trace with every arterial crossing as gate, then outer moat carve batches (L1 crossing made one straight edge between two deck bank vertices; L0 channel with those vertices as KernelTx.prepared); every k S5c L1 growth then L1 prune and trim; S5d top-up re-runs S5a arc and S5c on rim, each L1; S6 L1 perimeter chain then district owners and district_bound roles (one batch); S7 per enceinte L1 setback/glacis lines, intervallum, gate-plaza claims, castle paths and inner-ward trace, quays, piers, moles; S7b per district L1 claims (claimSubFace); S12a, S10a, S10b, S12c none (decisions and records; field pass 2 is a raster); S8 per district L1 lanes, rear lanes, through-alleys with T-junction ends; S9 L2 corridorUnion; S10 L3 step (0) eager shared-edge bands then per block in pool claims, plots, alleys-as-faces, residue; S11 per block L4 footprints and yard parts (party wall = plot's shared L3 side line with party_wall rows); S12b L3 park/grove layouts on own reserved green faces and residue then L4 yard-planting parts, tree rows write no plat edge (§2.7 Greenery.along); edits one batch per operator and level in §7.3 chain order, multi-level conversion a declared sequence of single-level batches, decks as §4.2 S1 (5)

items.statement: Every committed batch (generation or edit) whose commit record changes a footprint face's rings (e.g. a formal-garden grid line or orchard part edge ending on a house wall) is followed by §2.6's carry for that building before the next batch (J-P47)

Level writers: L0 by S1, S3, S4 and S5b (F-ROUTE extra bridge only) and S5a (outer moat carve); L1 by S3 (map border first), S4, S5, S6, S7, S7b and S8 in that order and by no generation stage after S9 (J-P46); S10 never writes L1 — a rear/back lane is decided by S8's deep-interior rule (§4.6), a lane a user adds later is a drawWay edit through §7.3's S5 operator whose tree scoping re-derives every finer level (GEO-25)

Static index partitions rebuilt as §3.3 states; S10's eager step (0) ends like a stage, rebuilding the L3 partitions it touched before the pool's freeze; work limits count kernel operations, never milliseconds (§5.1 (5))

Generation worker, derivation pool, hinterland unit (DEF-16; D-18): pipeline runs in one generation Web Worker (tile worker and main thread are §8.9's); primary configuration adds a derivation pool of up to three workers (min(3, hardwareConcurrency − 1)) for S10, S10b, S11, S12b after eager S10a and S10 (0); each district on its own copy-on-write overlay over a read-only arena copy frozen after those two eager steps (typed arrays, lookup tables, every non-empty level's static index partitions: L0–L3 at one-click freeze, L4 too after edits; every dynamic grid empty; partitions edits left dirty rebuilt first, §3.3 step 1; ≤ ≈15 MB at CITY); overlays merge in district lineage order with slot remap and index partitions (§3.3 merge); any write outside a district's face set is E_SCOPE; pool size 0 runs the same path in the generation worker
Derivation pool size = min(3, hardwareConcurrency − 1); frozen arena copy ≤ ≈15 MB at CITY
Addresses and lineage keys derive from lineage (§6.3), so no id ranges are reserved; the pool makes no shared-edge writes (district boundary edges belong to L1 and L2, committed before S10)

The hinterland unit: the hinterland pseudo-district's S10 (furlongs, outside lots, driveways, trails, woods, edge orchards), S10b (outside classes and, under §4.9 fill farm mode, farm households), S11 (farmstead and outside site plans), S12b (ring supply, ambient scatter, shoreline band) — runs on the generation worker while the pool runs the districts, on its own overlay over the same frozen arena; its faces are the hinterland's L2 blocks, disjoint from every district's; overlay merges with the districts' in lineage order under the pseudo-district's lineage; from freeze to merge no other writer touches the arena (J-P27); on the single-worker fallback the hinterland unit runs first, then districts in lineage order

items.statement: While a loaded document is verified (§2.9 step 3), every edit runs its S10, S10b, S11, S12b in the generation worker by the pool-size-0 path (§3.3 step 5), so the pool freezes no copy while a pool worker holds the verification replay's model

Which configuration is primary at each size (the pool, or the single worker that is the pre-decided fallback — also on the low tier and in hosts that forbid extra workers) is measured at M1 and M2b by §12.3's rule; pool size 0 gives the same model (J-P10)

Emulation-first defaults (item 23; J-A23.41): every stage rule of this part — default, extensions, every always/never/first…then — follows §7.6's emulation rule, its reading rule for absolutes and its marker (J-A23.71); §10.2's RelationRule.extension and §4.7 S10b's placement.extensionWeight are the placement family's form of that marker

Countryside decided with the town, drawn after it (FTG's order; item 26; J-A26.41): S2 demands the hinterland's households and its food, fuel and timber with the town's (§4.2 S2; §4.9 farm table); S12a sites them once districts are typed and claims cut (S7b); the hinterland unit draws fields and woods into the land the perimeter leaves after S9 commits corridors — concurrently with districts' pooled stages, which changes no output

Elaboration by click — trigger policy over the laziness contract (owner 2026-09-26; item 28; J-A28.41, J-A28.42): the contract says what may be derived lazily, the trigger policy says when; it belongs to the viewer not the model: elaborate = click | view, a per-user view key (§2.9); the key decides only the moment a pure rung is derived, never its content; one model either way (CI §6.5 (9) derived-complete digest over click orders too); click is default

items.statement: Saved, then stale until clicked: a derived rung is kept (elaboration cache, §2.9) and shown across zooms and sessions; a batch changing one of its recorded inputs (a designation, an assignment, the band, the storeys, the wing rings or a spanned passage's face, the households, a table slice it cites, or a dossier event of items 18, 22 or 31 — §2.8 ElaborationRecord.inputs) sets it stale (an unstored rung; a stored plan is re-cut inside the changing event instead, §7.3, J-A28.72); the cached result stays on view flagged at every zoom stop with a change marker (§8.5) until the next click re-derives it from its canonical prior — committed state never the cache (§6.2): the stored plan where one exists, else the as-built plan carried along §2.6's interior ladder (wings rung reads stored or as-built wings) — as a least-disruption mutation never a re-roll (§2.6, §7.3; J-A28.71); viewing never re-derives a current rung

items.statement: S1 (2) Coast: from a sea bearing (MFCG's sea angle kept as the request's coast bearing) and intent (bay/headland/straight/fjord/islands), one closed-outline routine draws the sea polygon; arms (COV-FTG-H04): base line two arms from a point near the town toward two frame edges, each with a shape row (smooth/gentle/sharp: lateral amplitude and count of 3–5 control points, then centripetal Catmull-Rom) and a detail row (none/bays/deep bays/rough/jagged: fBm amplitude, frequency, warp strength, for bays count and depth of indentations) — our own values, calibratable; displaced by domain-warped fBm under an amplitude envelope damping detail near the town → resample → Chaikin

items.statement: Coast simplicity (GEO-13): normal displacement clamped at every sample to 0.8 × local feature size on that side (distance to base shape's medial axis via skeleton(rings,'spine') (§3.4) as §3.8's spine reader with its sampled-medial-axis downgrade; for an open arm the distance to the facing arm or frame) — keeps small islands, elongated ovals (end radius ≈ b²/a), fjords simple; a resampled ring that still self-touches is repaired by non-zero union: the component containing the anchor (town side) keeps the outline id, every other loop typed by rule (land loop in sea above minimum islet area → islet; water loop on land above minimum pond area → pond; smaller absorbed) and reported (property test §13.2)

Contours and coast (GEO-14; J-P12): the vector coast is authoritative — raster lowered below sea level on the sea side; every land cell within two cells of the shore raised to ≥ sea level + 10 cm; every sea cell held ≤ sea level − 10 cm; contour lines are not model geometry: extraction and clip to land faces are §8.2's relief tier (F-CONTOUR, §5.2), so a contour never crosses the shore (cliffs and sub-cell spits included; steep-coast and cliff fixtures in the golden suite)

The same closed-outline routine with a closed base curve makes lakes (from sinks), ponds, islands (raised closed curve) and, with elevationCm set, the floating-island outline of the LAYER hook, which gets its own arena, Terrain, datum and frame (§2.2, §2.3) and may carry its own terrain from the same S1 with a request echoing the ground (e.g. conjured river with the ground river's bearing; AM-2); where it floats is II.6's placement rule, its occlusion §8.4's LayerSpec.occlusion

items.statement: S1 (3) Hydrology: sinks filled by bucket-queue priority flood on the integer heights of hydrology grid Terrain.hydro over frame + margin (16 m TOWN, 25 m CITY, 32 m METROPOLIS; §2.3) with exact flat surfaces (a filled depression keeps its spill height, never raised by ε); depression deeper than the table's lake threshold typed a lake; then D8 flow direction and accumulation

Rivers by descent: inlet on the arena's upstream edge (frame + margin; requested bearing or highest edge), so the drawn margin shows the river arriving; course traced by steepest descent with a lateral meander term (Chaikin-smoothed control polyline, knots mostly alternating sides; our own construction); terrain carved to the course, bed descending monotonically to the outfall so no depression is created and the flood not repeated; after the carve D8 recomputed on carved corridor cells and neighbours and accumulation once (≈2 ms at CITY), so the river always reaches sea, lake or frame
River width w = w0 · acc^0.4 clamped to the class band (FTG's ≈31 m mean river width at CITY one calibration point); tributaries by the same rule from secondary inlets

River bounds (GEO-36): knot offsets clamped to half the control spacing (river.controlSpacingM); S1 records control knots in WaterBody.controls with ordinals in course order (§2.3), the recorded input a moveCourseKnot edit addresses (§7.1); a self-touching course is re-traced with offsets halved; carving capped at carveMaxCm (400 cm TOWN and CITY, 600 cm METROPOLIS); a course needing more is re-routed by F-RIVER (§5.2), never trenched

Mouths (IMP-9, COV-FTG-H11): mouth 'estuary' = widening width profile (MFCG's delta-river option is a widened mouth); mouth 'delta' splits the course inside the delta zone (within the table's distance of the sea where bed slope below threshold) into 2–4 distributaries at splits spaced ≥ 3 channel widths, each carrying an accumulation share drawn from the water.delta stream (each ≥ 0.2), width w0·(share·acc)^0.4, traced by descent to the sea without rejoining; a distributary that would meet another merges and the land between becomes a river island under (4)

S3 (8) The castle (MFP-3, COV-FTG-G09): when requested or drawn, the castle bailey sited by defensibility (height + water on ≥ 1 side + control of the main route, O8 d), restricted by the castle option to inside/on/outside the stage-1 boundary, under a hard filter that no (5) route crosses the claim or, when water is within reach, the castle-moat band planned with it by (10)'s rule: 5–7-vertex polygon on a jittered circle, area band TOWN 1.0–3.0 ha, CITY 1.5–3.5, METROPOLIS 2.0–5.0 (anchored on MFCG's plain-size castles 1.3–3.4 ha), compactness ≥ 0.75 (MFCG's threshold, checked and repaired here by §4.8's rule before the trace welds)

on_enceinte castle placed across the boundary so exactly two of its vertices lie on it — the weld vertices — and the bailey's outer arc (its boundary between the welds on the outside) becomes the stretch of town wall the castle shares (9); the castle's town-side gate fixed now at the midpoint of the bailey side with the least-cost path to the plaza (for on_enceinte, among the sides of its town-side arc), so the castle street is a routable destination and a ring castle moat can carry its deck

S3 (9) Stage-1 trace: for a walled stage 1 the registered EnceinteStrategy traces the enceinte by S5a's rules (§4.4): boundary pulled to defensible ground within the 40 m band with gates and weld vertices pinned, then pinned-vertex smoothing and topology-preserving simplification; between the weld vertices of an on_enceinte castle the trace is the bailey's outer arc itself, one wall carrying both enceintes' wall roles (§2.7 Castle.cityWeld); pull and simplification treat the water planned in (2) and an inside/outside castle's planned ring moat as water, never crossed (§4.4), so no channel (10) carves can cut the trace; S5a commits this trace unchanged for k = 1; an unwalled town keeps the boundary itself as stage 1's boundary

items.statement: S3 (10) Water carvings and their decks → the L0 batch (GEO-19; J-P36): carved into L0 before S4, seen as water by every later stage: harbour basin and canals of (2) with their decks; a castle moat when water is within reach — around an inside/outside castle a ring band around the bailey outside its curtain's outer half-band and a berm with one deck at the castle gate perpendicular to the moat; for an on_enceinte castle only its outer arc: the channel along the shared stretch between the welds outside the trace's outer half-band and a berm (the city moat's own stretch there when the town has one, one channel at the wider of the two width rows; otherwise a channel clipped at each end by trace ⊕ (outer half-band + berm), ending against the town wall's berm beside each weld), while the bailey's town-side arc takes its castle template row's townSide (§4.8) and its castle gate needs no deck

items.statement: City moat when moat is inner or all: a channel of the era row's width along the (9) trace outside its outer half-band and a berm (table 2–5 m), with one deck at every main gate and at a harbour gate (7), where the gate's route (for a harbour gate, the route that placed it) crosses the channel, perpendicular to it

items.statement: Decoration ponds: the pond row of §4.9's decoration table (count by rung and biome), sites scored on hollows, flow accumulation and damp ground, each ≥ pondClearM (150 m) beyond the predicted built extent {T ≤ t_K} and ≥ 30 m from every (5) route and planned canal

No castle moat crosses the city trace (a ring surrounds a bailey the trace keeps off; an outer arc runs beside the trace), so §4.4's rule that the trace crosses water only at a river's water gate holds with every castle option; (8)'s hard filter keeps every solved route off a planned castle moat, so no castle moat needs a deck except at a ring moat's castle gate; every deck has S1 (5)'s form and two states
When a moat was carved, T is recomputed once over the new water (≈4 ms at CITY) for stages k ≥ 2; stage 1's boundary is never re-derived from it

S3 (11) The harbour route (J-P35): once the L0 batch commits, the harbour ↔ plaza route is solved on (3)'s lattice with committed water impassable except along decks, every reservation of (2) and (8) impassable and (walled stage 1) the (9) trace impassable except at gates; a harbour inside {T ≤ t_1} or of an unwalled town routed by heap A* from the plaza of the nucleus whose partition holds it; a harbour outside is reached through a gate: one multi-source Dijkstra from every gate's exit (the far bank vertex of its moat deck where (10) carved a city moat, the gate itself otherwise) over the lattice outside the trace finds the serving gate (least cost; ties by gate ordinal; a harbour gate competes, with N = 0 the only gate) and the branch at once; the harbour route = that gate's inward street, passage and moat deck (S4 re-solves through the deck, §4.3) and the branch; crosses a moat only on that gate's deck, adds no road through the wall (roads leaving the walled stage stay N, plus a harbour gate); data committed by S4 outside T's road set; costs one heap search of the castle street's size inside S3's §12.4 row (PLAUSIBLE); fixtures §13.2 walled coastal harbour fixtures

wiring.read_by: S4 commit; market siting (12) harbour attach; §13.2 fixtures; §12.4

items.statement: S3 (12) Principal market (item 24; owner: "the central market does not actually have to be central"): before the L1 batch, with gates, trace and harbour route fixed, the principal market's site is chosen by the trade-convergence score over candidate sites — rule table market.siting (§7.6; our own rows) with a controlled random term of share 0.1 from the reserve.market concern (§6.1)

wiring.read_by: L1 batch; market Reservation rank; S4 width_knots; report

items.statement: Market siting candidates and score terms (defaults): main plaza of each nucleus — plaza carries rank 'principal', attach points are the market's: kind 1.0, routes 0.5 × fraction of gate routes (5) rooted at it; each gate inside or outside — a flanking square around the gate route's stretch just inside/outside beside the gate plaza (§4.8): kind 0.3 inside or 0.15 outside, trade 0.6 × gate's trade weight; town bridge's landward ends (13) — flanking square around the bridge approach S4 routes to the deck's bank vertex: kind 0.35, traffic 0.5 × fraction of arterials whose bearings lie across the river; harbour's landward attach (11) — flanking square between basin attach point and harbour route: kind 1.0, trade 0.6 × min(1.5, p ÷ portRef); busiest inward street — middle third of the street of the gate of highest trade weight, flanking square astride it: kind 0.25, trade 0.4 × that gate's trade weight; slope, flood band and wind exposure enter as (1)'s site penalties

items.statement: Port demand fraction p = share of manifest buildings whose class requires 'coast' (§10.2); portRef = the table's reference port, median p over B-CITY's harbour seeds — a stored cell of market.siting (§7.6) computed by running S0–S2 alone on every B-CITY harbour seed; a scripted pass sets it at M1 and re-runs whenever a shipped roster row changes (new value shipped as a table-version bump with declared shift §13.3); a contract test recomputes the median and fails on a stored value that differs (§13.2); 0.12 (PLAUSIBLE) until the M1 receipt

Defaults compared (before penalties and random term; J-A24.43): single-nucleus town — plaza 1.5 (kind 1.0, routes 0.5), a gate ≤ 0.9, bridgehead ≤ 0.85, busiest street ≤ 0.65, so an inland walled town's plaza wins and the default reproduces MFCG; port — harbour 1.0 + 0.6 × min(1.5, p ÷ portRef): 1.6 at the median port, 1.3 at half the median, equal to plaza at p = ⅚ portRef, so the principal market leaves the plaza for the harbour in at least half of port seeds before penalties — the share §13.2's T24-1 and §13.7's row require (measured at M2b with §13.7's re-tune fallback); stays on the plaza where trade is mostly overland; parity presets pin the plaza by setting every other kind weight to its off value (item 23)

A flanking square is a market reservation of the principal row's area band (the plaza band of (2)) laid astride its way's stretch, that way passing through it as an arterial passes a gate plaza (§4.8): impassable to every other route except at its attach points (the two points where its way enters and leaves and the midpoint of each flank, where a side street may end as at a plaza); S4 places width_knot vertices at those two points (§4.3) so the square reads as a widening; chosen site, score and runners-up recorded in the report; setAttr on the reservation's rank or a drawBoundary moves the market by hand (§7.1)

The L1 batch: plazas, precinct, a flanking principal market's square and the castle bailey enter L1 as barrier faces carrying the reserved role: no way crosses them (S4, S5) other than a flanking market's own way; S8 does not cut them; the claimed entity is built inside them (§4.7, §4.8); every other claim larger than a block is S7b's (§4.5 S7b (3)), every secondary market among them except a polycentric nucleus's plaza

S3 (13) Destinations are typed entities: plazas' attach points and a flanking principal market's; each gate and its bearing (an external bearing per gate for a walled town; an unwalled town derives bearings by the same law on its own land); the town bridge — the crossing site nearest the centre when a river passes through the stage-1 region (scored at (1)), connected in town (§4.3) — every other site a bridge only when a route (S4) or growth proposal (S5c) uses it (S1 (5)); the harbour (its destination node = basin's landward attach point; route (11)); the castle's town-side gate; the precinct

Island towns (FTG-19): when the settlement's land component does not touch the frame, external destinations are shore points — the harbour, one landing per requested bearing (shore point nearest the bearing with best deep-water score) and a ferry point — and O4 (g) counts landings as the external connections

Dossier-backed elements at creation (item 22 (d); §7.7; J-A22.41): a brand-new map from an existing dossier holds every dossier element from the start: the blueprint's assignments and the dossier-backed elements enter S2's manifest as fixed rows — one (class, ordinal) each at the head of its class, present at every population, never withdrawn by the roster's arithmetic (prefix stability holds) — S7b allocates them before the roster's free demand in each rank of its order (§4.5), S10 (3) claims them, S10b's generation request places them (§4.7); the log's positions 0…k assign events (§7.7) record these placements as the generation run's own (place nothing a second time); replay reproduces them because the base derivation reads the same creation prefix (§7.4); a dossier element arriving after creation is a dossier request on the current map (§4.7 S10b, §7.7); one arriving with an epoch's inputs a mutation at that epoch (§4.11)

wiring.read_by: S2 manifest; S7b; S10 (3); S10b generation request; §7.4 fold; §4.11 epochs

items.statement: S0's sewer feature (item 14; II.7.1): toggles.sewers ∈ {auto, on, off}; at TOWN auto resolved by the feature table's P(sewers) row — II.7.1's law of the request's population and the intent's wealthLevel — drawn from blueprint.features with the other auto features, recorded in autoResolved; at CITY and METROPOLIS the rung row fixes existence on and a requested off hides the underground layer instead, reported in requestedVsBuilt (II.7.1); resolved value Features.sewers, which every dependant reads from the model (II.7)

items.statement: S4 candidate lattice: built once at S3 (depends only on frame, terrain, water, reservations) and reused by S3's pick contour, gate routes, field T, S4's routes and every S5a boundary; a jittered hexagonal point set at ≈25 m spacing, adjacency known by construction (six neighbours per point, jitter bounded so no edge crosses another; no Poisson sampling, relaxation or triangulation)

wiring.read_by: S3 (4)-(11); S4 routes; S5a boundaries; two-point roads 0147

items.statement: Edge cost = length × (1 + k_slope·slope²) × waterCrossingPenalty (impassable except along a pinned crossing deck — a site or built bridge) × reservationPenalty (impassable inside a reservation; plaza and castle reached only at attach points and gate) × wallCrossingPenalty (only at gates) × existingFabricCost (epoch > 0: crossing a built face costs by its class, so growth reuses streets) × landValue

wiring.reads_or_produced_by: terrain slope; decks; reservations; built faces

items.note: k_slope and landValue values not given in the unit (table)

items.statement: At epoch 0 S3's plaza-rooted Dijkstra tree gives every plaza-anchored route; a tree path that crosses a claim or water S3 added after the tree (castle bailey, a moat) is re-solved by heap A*, as are routes without a plaza end and every route at epoch > 0 (with existingFabricCost)

S4 commits the gate routes solved at S3 without re-solving: each split at its gate into inward street (plaza attach ↔ gate, primary) and outward arterial (gate ↔ frame edge at the bearing, through), so roads leaving the walled stage = N (plus a harbour gate) and each gate carries one road out and one street in (MFCG's gate identity; MFP-4)

Where S3 carved water across a solved route (the city moat just outside each gate) S4 re-solves only that stretch, from the last lattice node before the channel to the first beyond it, through the gate's deck, which continues the gate passage straight across the moat perpendicular to it

S4 remaining routes: the town bridge (each of its two ends to the nearest arterial on its bank in town); a site outside the boundary a route uses reached through the nearest gate, never a new wall crossing; every other site stays a site unless S5's growth uses it; the castle street (castle's town-side gate ↔ plaza, across the castle-moat deck when there is a moat); the precinct's frontage ↔ the plaza side it faces; canal decks inside the boundary ↔ the nearest arterial; harbour ↔ plaza and island gate ↔ landing were solved at S3; a polycentric town's gate-to-gate route between adjacent nuclei joins their plazas through both nuclei's gates; for a merged pair it crosses the cross wall at its gate

One graph, then one smoothing (GEO-16): all routes solved first on the lattice; the arterial graph is the union of lattice edges they use, each with its multiplicity; split into chains at every node of degree ≠ 2 and every pinned node (gates, attach points, deck ends, landings); junctions closer than 8 m merged on the graph; each chain simplified (Visvalingam) and smoothed (Chaikin × 2, then curvature-limited to the class's minimum radius) once with end nodes pinned, inserted into L1 once as a spine — a mandatory chain carrying the way role (§3.6) whose attraction folds any residual near-duplicate within 26 cm into a shared stretch — so routes sharing a run become one street, never braided near-duplicates

Class and width from multiplicity and betweenness on this graph (width table keyed by class, class by betweenness; O4 c); where a way's width varies along it (widening at a market or gate) S4 places width_knot vertices at the class-change junctions (insertChain opts.knots, §3.4), so width is a knot profile on the spine (§2.2 rule 5)
Junction rules: minimum crossing angle 30° (else deflect); Y → T conversion where the acute arm can be bent within its class curvature limit (G-P5)

Decks are fixed edges of the graph: smoothing never moves their vertices; each approach curve stays within the class radius; a river/canal deck approach that cannot meet the radius takes F-ROUTE's ladder (§5.2) — another site on the same reach within its search band, then an extra bridge placed as §4.2 S1 (5) — while a moat deck stays fixed to its gate, whose passage it continues straight; every deck a route uses becomes a built bridge when the spine lays its span through its two bank vertices (§2.7)
S4 test: on B-CITY no two spines run closer than their class separation for more than one step length; every deck's way angle within ±10° of the channel normal

Result: through-roads continue to the context margin with their bearings (O14); MFCG's radial gate → plaza legibility (streets converge on the plaza) with real metres and terrain (O4 a, d); later growth stages add main roads through S5b (§4.4), which runs this router incrementally with every existing arterial fixed, under the same F-ROUTE ladder; S4's local operator for edits is §7.3's

Markets as destinations (item 24): a flanking principal market is on its way already — S4 commits that way through the square between its two attach points and places a width_knot at each (the square a widening of the street profile, §2.2 rule 5); a side street may end at a flank's midpoint attach as at a plaza; every other market (the plaza when it carries the principal rank, S7b's secondary markets) is reached as a plaza or claim is, at its attach points; no market re-roots the plaza-rooted tree or field T (J-A24.41)
items.note: restates flanking-square width_knot rule of S3 (12)

items.statement: Trade flow (items 72, 77; J-A77.41, J-A77.42): TradeFlow declared and derived here — in two parts at generation: gates, harbour and dominantBearingCdeg at §4.2 S3 (7) as soon as gates and bearings exist (read no route), and ways after S4 commits the routes — and both again at each epoch (§4.11), from the circumstances' trade slice (CircumstanceSlice.trade: partners, bearings, modes, fill; §7.7 layer 2) with the gates' and roads' geometry; a derived record — Document.derived.tradeFlow (§2.9) caches it, rebuilt on load, never canonical; draws no random number

wiring.reads_or_produced_by: CircumstanceSlice.trade (dossier port V08; §7.7 layer 2); gates; routes
wiring.read_by: S3 (4) trade weight; S3 (12) market siting; S10b trade rows; §4.5 trade-position component; V06 epochs

items.statement: interface TradeFlow { gates: {gate: Id; weight: number}[] (with harbour Σ = 1); harbour?: number (water partners' share when the town has a harbour); dominantBearingCdeg: Cdeg (weighted circular mean of partners' bearings, item 72 (a)(3)); ways: {way: Id; weight: number}[] (absent ways weigh 0) }

items.statement: Partners to gates: a road partner goes to the land gate whose bearing lies angularly nearest its bearing (ties by gate id) — the gate S3 (4) picked for that bearing; a river or sea partner to the harbour, else the water gate on its river, else the nearest land gate; a gate's weight sums its partners' weights, normalised with the harbour's to one (the bearing's trade weight S3 (4), (12) read); with no partner every gate weighs the same and the harbour nothing

Ways' trade weight: sums the weights of every gate and the harbour whose S4 route to the plaza (§4.2 S3 (5), (13)) follows it; main streets in from the busiest gates carry the most; a way on no such route weighs 0; §4.5's trade-position component and its gate and main-street kernels read these weights (item 72)

Without a dossier the blueprint's external bearings and the intent's trade setting fill the slice (§7.7 layer 2), so a standalone town has the same record; a user's gate or road edit re-derives it with the geometry

Two-point roads (item 101 (i)): a drawWay declaration in its points form (two points and a class, or more points for a free-hand line, §7.1) is routed at its dry run: each consecutive pair joined by this router on the lattice with the class's costs and existingFabricCost (prefers existing streets and plot lines), each point snapped to the nearest lattice node or existing way vertex (the author's snap, §9.5, resolves points first); chain smoothed and inserted as S5b inserts a main road (§4.4); a stretch across water takes a deck by S1 (5)'s crossing rule — its preview draws a bridge; the dry run returns the derived route as the declaration's resolved shape, stored resolved (§7.1), pinned nodes the handles; no later derivation moves it (item 101's R13)

wiring.reads_or_produced_by: drawWay points form (§7.1); lattice; author's snap §9.5
wiring.read_by: §7.1 dry run; V09 authoring canvas; V10 clerk

items.statement: Each growth stage k runs four sub-steps; stage 1 commits the boundary, gates and trace S3 fixed (§4.2 S3 (6)–(9)); a stage k ≥ 2 takes its boundary first, then its main roads, then its trace, so every gate lies on the boundary it was picked on

S5a boundary (FTG-5, COV-FTG-D26; J-P7): boundary of stage k is a level set of network travel cost T(x) — least cost from the plaza(s) over the S3/S4 lattice, a lattice edge inside an arterial's corridor costing ρ_road per metre and any other edge ρ_off per metre, both times the slope term; water impassable except along decks; reservations impassable

Anisotropy ratio a = ρ_off/ρ_road, a stage-regime and form row: walled core 1.3, walled rings 1.8, ribbon 4, suburb 3, linear-street form 8 (our own values); FTG's measured road/non-road 90th-percentile radius ratio 1.26–1.65 on its two captured cities is the calibration target for extramural stages (B-REF, §13.5); a controls the wide-versus-elongated balance of ribbons and suburbs
items.note: values restated in the regime table's a column

items.statement: T is one field: computed at S3 (≈4 ms at CITY), recomputed once after S3's L0 batch only when a moat was carved; S4's remaining routes and the harbour route are not in its road set; each S5b's new main roads re-settle T incrementally only at nodes whose cost they lower, so no stage computes a new field (SCL-3)
items.note: restates S3 (10)'s recompute (0117)

items.statement: Stage 1's boundary is S3's contour and S5a commits S3's trace unchanged; for k ≥ 2 the boundary is taken from T as it stands when stage k begins (before its own S5b): t_k chosen so the land of {T ≤ t_k} ∪ the enclosure of stage k − 1 equals the land of stages 1…k from S2 (lattice nodes sorted by T, cell areas accumulated; exact to one cell) — the union keeps stages nested even where a moat raised T just outside the previous wall — boundary is that region's outer contour, Chaikin-smoothed and resampled; S5b then picks and routes primaries on it; their re-settlement serves stage k + 1 onward

S5a trace (GEO-18, FTG-8): for a walled stage fixed before the stage's secondaries grow (stage 1 by S3; k ≥ 2 right after S5b) by one rule set, the registered EnceinteStrategy: boundary → pulled to defensible ground within a 40 m search band (local ridges, slope breaks, river banks: a cost-surface path around the town with a penalty for leaving high ground), gates pinned where arterials cross the boundary (stage 1 S3's gates; k ≥ 2 every crossing of an S4, earlier-S5b or this stage's S5b arterial), an on_enceinte castle welded through its two weld vertices (shared edge one wall; MFP-3) → pinned-vertex Laplacian smoothing in 3 passes (wall.smoothPasses, a wall-table row; provenance ref:MFCG 12710731 three pinned smoothing passes (code), P12; J-A46.43), gates, weld vertices and the two shore anchors of an open chain never moving → topology-preserving Visvalingam (kernel simplify §3.4: minimum segment 20 m, no interior angle < 100°; a removal that would make the trace touch itself, cross water, enter a reservation or move a pinned vertex is refused) → inserted on L1 through insertChain as a mandatory chain carrying wall role, gate vertices carrying wall_gate; on a shore or bank the trace is attracted onto the outline (shared stretch one edge carrying both roles, §3.6)

wiring.read_by: L1 wall chain; S6 barrier; §4.8 furniture; Wall records §2.7

items.note: S3 (9) restates the rule set in brief

items.statement: A second castle on an outer enceinte (the citadel of §4.2 S0) is sited by §4.2 S3 (8)'s rules against its stage's boundary and entered as an L1 barrier face in that stage's trace batch, with its gate and any moat deck

Water and the waterfront (COV-MFCG-C07; J-P25): the trace never crosses water except at a water gate where a river passes: its two vertices on the river's banks carry ('gate_end', gate, 0|1) and the Gate names them in banks (§2.2 rule 7, §2.7); a generated gate's bank vertices are the trace's vertices on the shores, placed by S5a's L1 trace batch after the water exists (L1 Steiner vertices on L0 shores, or L0 shore vertices where the trace attracted); an edited gate's (§4.11, §7.3 (b) 3) are promoted to L0 by the water's batch (§3.3 rule 3); every water gate names its bank vertices the same way; both kinds held under a warp unless fromLevel = 0, as a deck's are (§3.6; J-K35)

On a coast or river bank the trace may be an open chain whose ends are anchored on a shore, bank, cliff or another enceinte; its enclosure is closed by the L0 shoreline for every "enclosed" and "sealed" test

waterfront row: open (default — MFCG's coastal wall stops at the water; FTG's captured wall an open 17-tower chain bank to coast: no wall along quays and beaches), quay_wall (a wall along the waterfront), sea_wall (a full wall); under either wall a water gate stands at every quay access, so every quay stays reachable through a gate

placement 'aroundStage' traces only the stage's new ring, as an open chain anchored on the previous enceinte (FTG's "around stage lots"); nothing grown later crosses the trace except at a gate; S6 treats it as a barrier; if an inward pull would leave the stage's land short by more than the S5d tolerance the pull is capped at the smoothing step (reported); F-WALL's ladder is §5.2's

Outer moats: when moat is all, S5a carves stage k's moat (k ≥ 2) right after committing its trace, through §4.11's carve path; its way rule meets only arterials (each just outside one of the stage's gates; secondaries not yet grown), so every way is kept with a deck and nothing cut: the L1 batch places each deck's two pinned bank vertices on its arterial where the channel's banks will cross it (deck_end rows of a fresh Bridge, built with that arterial as its way, §2.7), the span between carrying deck (the arterial re-routed between the gate and its next pinned node beyond the channel where it would meet the channel more than 10° off its normal, as §4.3 re-solves S3's moat stretches); the L0 batch inserts the channel (era row's width, outside the outer half-band and a berm) through those prepared vertices, so each span becomes its deck perpendicular to the channel and continuing its gate's passage; S7 builds bridge furniture (§4.8); S5c treats the moat as water; nothing finer than L1 exists yet so the carve clears nothing; the innermost enceinte's moat is S3's

S5b main-road step (FTG-4; stages k ≥ 2 and every epoch stage): N_k = the gate law of §4.2 S3 (4) on the land inside the stage's enceinte with its waterfront reduction where the stage's boundary runs along a sea or lake shore for ≥ gate.waterfrontShare of its length (walled; J-A46.42), or one primary per mainRoadSpacingM of boundary (unwalled; 450 m at CITY); existing arterials cross the new boundary c times; when N_k > c S5b spawns N_k − c radial destinations on the boundary by nested picks (largest angular gaps first, terrain-scored like gates) and routes each with the incremental S4 router (§4.3) from the nearest junction on an existing primary outside the previous enceinte (never through an inner wall) to the frame at its bearing, under S4's F-ROUTE ladder (§5.2), extra-bridge rung included (its L0 batch of two same-level shore splits precedes the L1 batch)

wiring.read_by: stage main gates; T re-settlement; V06 epochs

items.statement: S5b crossings become stage k's main gates; posterns only for an explicitly requested remainder; an outer enceinte never gets fewer gates than arterials cross it; a request below that is raised and reported (a requested gate count applies to the innermost enceinte, MFCG's semantics)
S5b test: primary length per km² and the share of gates on primaries in band from TOWN to METROPOLIS; each epoch stage whose N_k exceeds its crossings adds ≥ 1 primary
items.note: band values not in the unit

items.statement: S5c growth of the secondaries: inside the boundary a priority queue of proposals grows streets FTG-style (CONFIDENCE C5): each proposal {origin junction, heading, curvature, goalHeading, class, remainingSegments, branchCounter, priority}, lowest priority first; step length by class (secondary 25–40 m, lane 15–25 m; FTG's district streets persist at (L + 0.5)/2 ≈ 25–30 m, where our tables start)

Division of labour with the bent cut (MFP-2; J-P4): in walled regimes S5c grows only the arterial-connecting secondary network at district scale — proposals seeded at arterial junctions and gate plazas, separation floor 120/160/200 m at TOWN/CITY/METROPOLIS, destination bias toward other arterials — and every lane and finer intramural street comes from S8's recursive bent cut, inheriting the wall's and shore's direction (MFCG street-signature targets §13.5); in extramural regimes (ribbon, suburb, unwalled rings, ground between polycentric nuclei) growth works at block scale as FTG's does

Heading model (FTG-17, FTG-6; J-P8): ou, a mean-reverting curvature walk κ ← ρ·κ + (1 − ρ)·κ_goal + s·√(1 − ρ²)·ξ per step Δs, ρ = e^(−Δs/ℓ), κ_goal = (θ_goal − θ)/L_r, s from headingSigma (degrees per 100 m); organic defaults 20° per 100 m, ℓ = 90 m, L_r = 250 m; planned 5° per 100 m; at organic defaults a 600 m street's net turn p50 21°, p90 50°, 0.1 % beyond 90°, per-30 m-step turn p95 11.4°, p99 14.9° with Gaussian tails (receipt fixall_pipeline_ou_heading.out, 4 000 streets per setting); radiusHold: ring proposals keep curvature 1/r about the centre with small s (ringed preset); gridLock: headings snap to the preset's grid table (american); CI tests the drift distribution per preset
Branching after n segments with a per-class probability, perpendicular ± jitter (FTG's Continue) or tangential to the centre (FTG's Curve around origin, the ringed preset's ring branch)

Destination bias, switchable per class and preset: a proposal that can reach an unserved destination or existing spine within ≈1.5 step lengths turns toward it; off for suburb offshoots and ring proposals

Legality (GEO-37): minimum separation from parallel spines = the regime's separation; same clearance to shores, wall setback bands, reservations and the stage boundary: a proposal within max(minimum block depth of the regime, separation/2) + half its corridor of any of them and within 30° of parallel is deflected or rejected (no strip thinner than a plot depth); a proposal meeting a shore or reservation at ≥ 30° ends there; a wall never crossed except at a gate — a proposal reaching the setback band stops there; snap to a junction within 0.35·step

Crossings follow the preset's crossing matrix (proposal class × crossed class → stop in a T, cross with a materialised crossroads, or deflect): organic crosses only a lower-or-equal class collinear within 6° (rare crossroads, O4 b); ringed crosses radials with rings; american crosses on the grid

Water in S5c: a proposal whose class row allows a bridge (secondary and lane by default) meeting a river or canal bank within 0.35·step of a site's bank vertex snaps to it and continues across that deck to the far bank vertex, building the bridge (§2.7) — sites' 40 m spacing playing FTG's minimum distance between bridges; any other proposal meeting water ends there as at a shore; slope ≤ class limit
Junction rules as §4.3 with T-preference in organic regimes; junction-degree band a preset row: organic 4-way 0–15 %, ringed 20–45 %, american 40–80 %

Between stages: prune dangling secondary chains shorter than one block width; trim only S5-grown provisional spines running beyond the boundary (FTG-18); S4 and S5b arterials never trimmed; the boundary becomes the next stage's start

S5d capacity check (FTG-2): right after S5c the stage's new coarse faces are priced: built land per face = face area − corridor reserve of its spines (declared half-widths) − reservations; each face's band is the driver-only prosperity field at its centroid (S6 pass 1's kernels) cut by provisional cut points computed as §4.5 computes the recorded bands, over land grown so far (S6 records the town's FieldBands once over all stages); if land per band falls short of Σ n(c,b,k)·plotArea(c,b)/plotShare by more than 5 % in total, one top-up runs: the level set grows to cover the shortfall, S5a re-traces only the affected arc between its pinned gates, S5c grows the added rim — except along a moat: a moated arc is never re-traced, so a moated stage's shortfall moves to the next stage's quota (last stage's to the exact check), reported; a remaining shortfall goes to the exact check after S10 (§4.7) and to the F-SITING reconcile, reported (F-BUDGET-STAGE, §5.2)

wiring.read_by: exact check §4.7; F-SITING; F-BUDGET-STAGE §5.2; plotShare fallback 0080

Stage regimes (StageRegime rows per rung, era, form): dense core (walled, stage 1) block-depth floor 30–45 m (applied by S8), separation 120–200 m (district-scale secondaries only), a 1.3, ou bias on, lanes from S8, T-preference; walled rings (walled stages ≥ 2) 45–70 m (S8), 120–200 m, a 1.8, ou bias on, courts and rear lanes (S8); ribbon (default extramural, outside the last enceinte along arterials) plots directly on the arterial, depth band 30–50 m, starting beyond the outer setback/glacis (MFP-9), density falloff by a distance-to-gate kernel, a 4 (MFCG's outskirts: 71–85 % of extramural buildings within 100 m of a gate road); suburb (FTG C10; preset, era row or shanty toggle only, MFP-6) final regime outside the last enceinte, 40–60 m, separation 80 m, a 3, offshoots, bias off — optional perimeter lane (FTG-20: previous enceinte's outer boundary offset by setback and glacis, typed lane, broken at arterials) seeds offshoots at a 60–90 m spacing row besides arterial seeds; offshoots grow as cul_de_sac/lane proposals without destination-bias termination, no infill below the band; plots directly along offshoots with small lots, a per-plot density Bernoulli from the distance-to-gate kernel leaving gaps; calibration references FTG's 83 cul-de-sacs, 30.00 m suburb streets, 14.70 m lot outlines; american/ringed presets on request, gridLock/radiusHold, crossing matrix and junction band per preset; fixture: ringed on a flat site gives ≥ 3 closed rings with radius CV ≤ 10 % and ring × radial crossroads

items.statement: District grower (CONFIDENCE B9): seeds = the sited features (every market — principal's reservation and each secondary's claim, one market district per market, item 24 — harbour, gates, castle, temple precinct, river banks, the bridgeheads (both landward ends of every bridge carrying an arterial, the town bridge among them), parks) plus a density-guided remainder, N_d seeds in all; a grower (MFCG 12710731's district-builder idea) claims adjacent coarse faces of the L1 skeleton in round-robin turns: on each turn it skips with probability 1 − rate(kind) — district.growthRate table, one row per seed kind: gate, castle and bridgehead 0.1, riverbank 0.5, every other kind 1 (provenance ref:MFCG 12710731 growth rate by seed kind (code), P13; J-A47.41) — otherwise absorbs one admissible neighbour drawn uniformly

wiring.reads_or_produced_by: S3 features; markets; bridges; S5 coarse faces

items.statement: Admissible neighbour: the shared edge passes the edge test (no arterial of class ≥ primary, no wall trace, no water, no reservation boundary) unless the seed kind allows it, and the grown patch passes the patch test (area within the district band, compactness ≥ 0.5, no hole); a hole check → split
items.note: "unless the seed kind allows it" — which kinds allow which barrier is not enumerated here

items.statement: Grower rounds: a round gives every unfinished grower one turn in seed-id order; a grower with no admissible neighbour is finished; growth ends when every grower is; each turn's skip and pick draws come from district.seed keyed by the grower's seed lineage (its feature's; a remainder seed's first face) and the turn number, so §7.3's S6 operator re-grows a scoped regroup by the same turns; faces no grower could claim (enclosed by barriers or band tops) seed further districts in face-id order, grown by the same turns (MFCG 12710731's leftover rule)

A district whose area ends below the band's floor merges into the neighbour with the longest shared edge, except one grown from a seed whose rate is below 1: it keeps at least its seed face, so the rates set its size (small gate, castle and bridgehead wards behind §13.5's MFCG anchors row, 2.4–17.6 ha at size 40; J-A47.42); arterial barriers and the count law are ours (J-A47.41)

One law for count and band (MFP-10): N_d = round(3.5·√(A_ha/10)) seeds over the settlement's land A (FTG's 10 ha anchor in its middle; MFCG 12710731's ⌊√(city cells)⌋ matched in metric terms on its size sweep), band [0.5, 1.5] × A/N_d, so mean district √(10A)/3.5 — ≈7 ha at 60 ha, ≈14 ha at 250 ha, ≈22 ha at 600 ha

A district's faces is a FaceRef (§2.5): its L1 faces and every face nested in them (§3.3 pool step 3); after S8 cuts lanes the finer faces inherit the district through parent (§2.8), so containment is 100 % by construction (O11 b; §5.3's containment row checks it)

Quarters (MFP-10, VIS-4; J-P2, J-P28, J-I1): after typing S6 builds §9.1's quarter merge tree (QuarterNode) once per model: repeatedly merges the adjacent pair with the smallest cost — combined area, plus 1 000 ha when their kinds are of different families (central + market, docks + riverbank, gate + ribbon, craft + craft … share a family), plus 10 000 ha when a wall or water barrier separates them — until one root remains, ties by id; quarters are the tree's cut at min(N_q, L) nodes (after L − min(N_q, L) merges, L = number of districts; every district stands alone when N_q ≥ L; QuarterNode.cityCut; N_q can exceed district count at TOWN)

wiring.read_by: S13a names every node; §9.4 city-band label unit; II neighbourhoods

items.statement: N_q = round(1.37·B^0.267), B the roster's building count: least-squares fit of MFCG's district counts on its size sweep (9/12/18/22/24 districts at 1 475/5 242/13 091/31 951/48 379 buildings), giving N_q = 9–10 at TOWN (1 200–1 500 buildings), 13–14 at CITY (4 500–6 000), 17–18 at METROPOLIS (12 000–15 000) (receipts fixall_pipeline_mfcg_fits.out, fixall_pipeline_r2_quarters.out); S13a names every node of the tree; the quarters are the city-band label unit (§9.4)

Typing (G-P5; MFP-7; J-P1): a data-driven scorer per district kind reads the roster's remaining demand per class, the kind's relation rows (RosterTables.districtKinds[].relations, §10.2 — item 16's templates: docks at the harbour, gate wards at gates, central → market/merchant, a market kind at every market reservation, noxious crafts downstream and downwind, near the castle → military/administration, waterfront → docks) and a random term; faces typed greedily from the largest with a mixed-use floor (no single-use district unless requested, R5)

items.statement: Kinds are feature-named; wealth is not a kind — "the rich quarter" is a description the naming engine derives from the prosperity field (§10.4) — so no district is zoned residential or by class; the district's identity, read after placement from its character vector, names and describes it (item 72); the kinds stay this typing, which later stages read

A staged power relation (item 88; J-A88.42): when the dossier port fills a staged PowerRelation (§2.7; empty in the base), the scorer gains one soft row between the S6 kinds the quarter-identity rows name for its two powers (the kind of each identity row whose power is that power's PowerStanding.kind; §10.2; §7.7 layer 2): an adjacent row for an alliance, an avoid row for a rivalry or feud (any other pair type none), weight relation.adjacencyWeight (0.3; our own, extension, 0 in parity presets) × its strength

Shanty districts (FTG's rule as the default; items 27, 23): a shanty/squalid kind is admitted only when the roster's average band (household shares' mean over the band set) is poor or squalid, and only once the settlement's first half is built (shanty.trigger, shanty.afterStageShare 0.5; provenance ref:FTG shanty rule); where admitted it replaces the typing of the districts of lowest mean pass-1 band among the districts of the stages whose cumulative quota share (§4.2 S2's stage rows) exceeds shanty.afterStageShare (a district's stage is its growthStage, §2.5), as many as its demand fills, and takes the cluster row (§4.7 S11, item 70; FTG's tents row in parity presets)

items.statement: Our preference that shanties lie outside the enceinte is the shanty kind's extramural relation row — soft, extension: true, weight 0.6, zero in the parity presets — a tendency not a law (J-A27.43); the shanty toggle (S0) forces the kind on where FTG's trigger would not fire; MFCG's "one prominent feature per named type" survives as the district's namingFeature; a district's fabric is bent-cut unless a template is requested (II.1, II.2)

Prosperity field (owner: prosperity is a gradient and a band; AM-6): P(x) = Σ_i w_i·kernel_i(x) + characterOffset(district) + ε(x), clamped once to [0, 1]; driver kernels from a table: distance decay to the plaza and every market (principal at the row's full weight, a secondary at the secondary row's, item 24), to main streets, gates, water and harbour (+); elevation above the flood line and upwind (+); low, damp, downwind, flood-prone (−); walls (−); attractors at reserved institutions (castle, precinct, plaza); the three dials' driver terms and the district pressure (item 72); ε a low-frequency fBm from the field's own sub-stream with a declared share (default 0.15); smoothed by a Gaussian of one block width (σ ≈ 60 m at CITY); stored per coarse face and as a raster

items.statement: Field mechanism (budget §12.4): 32 m cells over frame + margin; each driver kernel splatted within its radius (or one distance transform per driver class); the Gaussian an O(N) three-box blur; computed in two declared eager passes (LC-2): pass 1 at S6 — first the driver kernels existing after S5 (the kernels S5d uses; S6's typing reads this driver-only state), then after typing the district-type term characterOffset(district), which completes pass 1 (S8's block bands read pass 1 complete); pass 2 at S10a (§4.7), adding kernels around noxious trades, prisons, middens and institutions the block allocation placed; S10 onward reads pass 2

The band set (item 27): one named, versioned table prosperity.bands (BandSet; §7.6), read by every rule table keying a row by band: granularity and the designation templates (§4.7; site-plan table folded into them, J-A19.41), greenery (§4.9), hidden-plot shares (§4.6), island supply law (II.6), ladder rows (§4.11), the interior ladder's rows read at the occupants' band (§2.6, item 28 (f)), the roster's household and lifestyle rows (§10.2); default set six bands in order: squalid (FTG squalid, MFCG slum, share 0.011, reads poor/dense with §4.7 S11's hovel and cluster rows — FTG's tents row in parity presets); poor (poor, slum, 0.011, poor/dense); modest (modest, craftsmen, 0.217, modest); comfortable — the middle band (comfortable, craftsmen, 0.435, interpolated between modest and prosperous); prosperous (wealthy, merchant, 0.217, prosperous); rich (aristocratic, patriciate, 0.109, rich); weights 1/1/20/40/20/10 (provenance ref:FTG lifestyle distribution)

items.statement: MFCG's ward-class shares 0.70/0.17/0.07/0.07 of the open-source model's 30 class-typed ward-deck entries for craftsmen, slum, merchant, patriciate (receipt research/findings/os-model.md) are the anchor of §13.5's built-land share per band group, never a district typing (J-P1)

Band interpolation: a rule table may carry rows for some bands only; a band without its own row takes the linear interpolation along the value between the nearest rowed bands' centres (how the four granularity rows serve six bands and how class-mix weights §4.7 S10b item 71 are read at a plot's value); an end band takes the end row

Middle band: the band §4.11's geometry floor bounds a once-richer plot's manifested geometry to (item 31: the shell, never the interior, which follows its occupants' band through §2.6's interior ladder, item 28 (f)); designated per settlement as the band that holds its median household under the roster's wealth shares (comfortable under defaults: cumulative 0.239 after modest, 0.674 after comfortable); recorded on FieldBands.middle at S6 with the cuts and moved only as they move (J-A27.42, J-A31.45); each settlement's middle its own

The continuous gradient between and within bands is our extension; a parity preset keeps the reference's tier count and shares and sets the interpolation's blend to a step at each cut (item 23; J-A27.41)

Bands (LC-6, FTG-2): cut points computed once per town so the share of built land in each band equals that band's share of the plot land the roster demands (household wealth shares × the band's plot areas, S2) — capacity and demand agree by construction — recorded as the town's FieldBands (§2.5) with the band set's ids in order and its middle; move only by an explicit setAttr on that record (re-derives every block whose band changes) or by an epoch; a field brush (§7.2) never moves them; a block keeps its recorded band unless its value crosses a cut by more than the hysteresis (0.02), so a replay reproduces the session's bands; a block whose band changes past the hysteresis at an epoch is marked DUE for §4.11's survivors' ladder (item 31)

wiring.read_by: FieldBands (§2.5); S8; S10; §7.2 brush; §4.11 survivors' ladder; V06

items.statement: Bands used only where a table needs a class; continuous rules (coverage, plot size, greenery share, building scale) interpolate linearly between band rows along the value, so quarters blend at their edges

Over time (LC-12): an epoch re-evaluates the drivers with new circumstances; surviving plots keep their built state and change only through §4.11's explicit, rate-limited transformation events — the survivors' wealth ladder, whose rungs a DUE block climbs by duration and by its stock's replaceability, bounded by the geometry floor (item 31); under decline the field contracts toward the survivors' core (§4.11)

The owner rule clause by clause (AM-6): continuous field P(x); predictable drivers: the kernel table; controlled random component: ε with its declared share; banded only where a table needs a class: FieldBands; continuous rules interpolate: §4.7, §4.9; dynamic over time yet predictable: epochs move drivers, survivors transform by rule; editable: the brush and setAttr on FieldBands

items.statement: S7b (3) District claims (J-P41): every item larger than one block — institutions whose requirement exceeds the district's upper block area (e_hi², as §4.6's stop test defines it), the district's share of the park and green quota (§4.9), area-bearing assignments, a castle's esplanade — sized from its requirement table and cut out of the district's coarse faces other than its wall_strip faces by claimSubFace (within = that face list, §3.4) at the best siting score, entered as a Reservation; S8 cuts around it as a hole (the slit exists), S10 keeps only sub-block claims, S12b builds parks only on reserved faces or residue

No S7b claim takes strip ground, as no S8 cut does (§4.6): a strip's ground is the band, setback and glacis S10's step (0) builds, where the hard invariant "footprints ∩ (band ⊕ setback) = ∅" leaves a claim nothing to stand on; only S7's gate plazas use a strip's setback zone (§4.8); a castle's esplanade is therefore claimed beyond the bailey's outer strip, so the spacer reads as glacis, then green (§4.9)
S7b claims test: 100 % of institutions and parks larger than one block placed at their requirement (O18 f), and 0 S7b claims meeting a wall strip

Secondary markets (item 24): the N_markets − 1 secondary markets S2 demanded, less any polycentric plaza S3 (12) ranked secondary, are S7b claims: each sited by the market row's district score — gate wards, harbour and riverbank districts and districts of later stages first, then any district by demand — under two rules whose defaults are MFCG's behaviour: never touching (market.minSeparationM 150 between market reservations, and no shared edge with another market or the plaza) and small patches (the claim takes the smallest coarse face of the chosen district holding the secondary row's area band, 0.10–0.25 ha at CITY); enters as a market reservation with rank 'secondary', its district typed market (a feature name, J-P1), S8 cuts around it, §4.7 S11's stall and centrepiece rules read its rank; a market that cannot be sited is reported and dropped (F-SITING), never forced (J-A24.42)

items.statement: S7b (4) Edge greens and orchards (§4.9): for every district touching the settlement perimeter whose band row carries the edge-green-or-orchard rule, S7b draws the choice — before (3) cuts the claims — from that district's alloc.district stream with the rung's probability (RungProfile.greenery.edgeGreenProb, §1.1): a green becomes one of the district's claims (3), built by its own S12b on its own faces; an orchard becomes a row of the hinterland's allocation {cls: 'orchard', areaM2, near: district}, built by the hinterland unit's S10 in the first ring beside that district; no district stage ever writes a hinterland face

items.statement: S7b (5) Sky pseudo-districts (owner-staged; AM-2, AM-10, AM-13, AM-15; II.6): when recipe.layers.islands is on for a rung whose row admits islands (II.6 (1)–(2)), S7b first draws the island count on the island.place stream by II.6's count law and for each open slot creates its sky pseudo-district's Allocation — before (1) and before any island exists — filled from the richest band down under II.6's supply law: plot land = supported area A(S_carried, S_town) × dense core plot share (0.62, §4.2 S2), recomputed as households are added, until it is used or three districts' worth of households are allocated; a slot whose supported area is 0 gets no allocation; an institution island's allocation holds its one institution (the IslandInstitution row's or the assignment's) and exists only where the town's supply admits it; the ground's districts get the remainder so the population stays whole; SkyStrategy, registered after S7b by declared I/O, takes these allocations (each with supported area and altitude) and sizes and places each island (II.6)

items.statement: S7b (6) The underground pseudo-district (owner-staged; item 12, II.7.3): when Features.sewers is on and the preset yields navigable mains, S7b creates the underground pseudo-district's Allocation after (5) and before (1) — the poorest band's undergroundShare, classes whose row is underground: 'preferred' and, in an epoch, the crowding hook — capped by the predicted navigable capacity; rows, law and cap are II.7.3's; ground districts receive the remainder

S7b (7) The undercity (owner-staged; item 65, II.7): where an undercity exists S7b creates its allocation after (6) and before (1) — the H households of II.7.5's size law (squalid band's first, then poor band's), the outlawed and clandestine institutions whose mode is underground — capped by the void's capacity; II.7 states the rows and cap; districts above ground receive the remainder so the population stays whole
Pseudo-district allocation order: sky (5), then underground (6), then undercity (7), all before the ground districts' allocation (1), which receives the remainder
items.note: derived ordering statement

items.statement: The due mark and the dossier's rows (items 22, 31; J-A31.45): §4.11's geometry floor reads FieldBands.middle as designated (J-A27.42, J-A31.45); an epoch's re-evaluation acts on a block only by marking it due when its value crosses a cut by more than the hysteresis (Block.due, §2.5); §4.11's wealth ladder does the rest — surviving plots transform by the ladder's rungs, never by a re-derivation; S7b allocates S2's fixed dossier rows before the free demand in each rank of its order (§4.2 S2, item 22 (d))
items.note: restates bands bullet (0204) and S2 dossier rows (0127)

items.statement: Neighbourhood character (item 72; owner quote on mix of assigned lots, political powers, trade flow, naming): a district's kind is what the stages read to build it; its character is what it has become — derived from what was placed, never assigned once; this paragraph is the one statement of the character vector, quarter identities, three dials, band range, pressure and partition; records are §2.5's (CharacterVector — the one meaning of "character"; the per-district input once also called character is DistrictIntent, §7.7; J-A72.41 — District.identity, District.bandRange, District.pressure, District.nameHistory) and §2.7's (Institution.powers); row types §10.2's; inputs §7.7 layer 2's circumstance slices — the dossier's facts or the blueprint's own as their stand-in (item 20 (h))

wiring.read_by: CharacterVector etc. (§2.5); V01 neighbourhoods; V08; V10 clerk

items.note: TERM: "character" = CharacterVector; retired synonym for DistrictIntent

items.statement: (1) Significance (J-A72.45; owner: "each church individual value is greater than the lodging"): every count, share and dial weighs a placed instance (a use — workplace, shop, institution — or a residential building) by σ = BuildingClassRow.significance × rank × size × patronage: class base value (cathedral ≫ church ≫ lodging house; guildhall above workshop; houses, lodging, common shops low — our own rows §10.2) × the institution's rank (1 unless its row or the dossier gives one) × size (footprint area over class median footprint, clamped [0.5, 2]) × patronage (1 + the dossier's wealth or rank of the institution when given, clamped [1, 2])

(2) Character vector — five components, derived (item 72 (a); CharacterVector, §2.5): written by S12c Character (§4.1: town-wide, generation worker after the pool's merge, before S13a) and by each epoch's character step (§4.11); a pure function of placed lots, slices and geometry, draw-free, recomputed on load and equal on recomputation (J-DET-12)

wiring.read_by: identities (4); S12c; §4.11 character step; §10.4 naming; V01; V10; §2.9 load recompute

items.statement: CV (1) Lot mix: for each class family f (a tags value of the class, one of the families §10.2's identity rows name — religion, craft, trade, lodging, residential, military, administration, harbour, noxious, learning, arcane, crime …): mix[f] = Σ_(i∈f) σ_i ÷ Σ_i σ_i over the district's instances
items.note: family list ends "…"

items.statement: CV (2) Political alignment: for each power p of the powers slice powers[p] = Σ_i σ_i·w_i(p) ÷ Σ_i σ_i, w_i(p) the partition weight of (7); when the port fills a staged alliance (PowerRelation §2.7; item 88) powers[p] gains relation.spill × strength × powers₀[q] and powers[q] the converse, from unspilled powers₀, vector then scaled back to its unspilled sum (relation.spill 0.25; our own, extension); a rivalry or feud acts only through typing's row

CV (3) Trade position: trade = the district's frontage length on each way × the way's trade weight (§4.3 TradeFlow), summed and divided by the town's largest such sum (busiest district 1); tradeBearingCdeg the weighted mean bearing of the gates whose routes cross it
CV (4) Economic role: for each sector s, sectors[s] = Σ_(i∈d) σ_i·w_i(s) ÷ Σ_(all i) σ_i·w_i(s) — the district's part in the town's weighted presence of that sector

CV (5) Relations: mainRoad = share of its frontage on through and primary ways; anchors = significant institutions (σ ≥ character.anchorSigma 5) within character.anchorRadiusM (400 m) of its boundary, each weighted σ_anchor × (1 + c) ÷ (1 + distance ÷ radius), c the district's contribution share — its share of the anchor's suppliers (plots at the tail of the anchor's supply edges, §10.2) and of its members (Membership records of the anchor's power housed in the district, §2.7, when the module has materialised them, else 0)

(3) Three distributions (item 72 (d′); BuildingClassRow.distribution, §10.2): district-defining — a class that IS a district (red-light district, slums, foreign quarter, guild district: dossier institution kinds); each dossier instance claims ONE district: S6's typing places defining instances first (known before placement, S2's fixed dossier rows), each taking the not-yet-claimed district that scores highest by the relation rows of its identity row's kind (§10.2) or, for a row without a kind, by its defining class's own relation rows (§10.2 brothel rows; J-A72.51), one district per instance; two in one district only when no unclaimed district scores above zero (reported)

wiring.reads_or_produced_by: dossier institutions (V08); S2 fixed rows; relation rows

items.statement: A district-defining instance shapes its district without filling it: S7b allocates it the ordinary demand for its band with the defining class's share raised to its identity row's targetShare (§10.2); its band, granularity, greenery and lighting rows are the defining kind's (slums: the squalid band through the kind's characterOffset and §4.7 S11's cluster rows, item 70); its identity's source is dossier

A dossier that adds a district-defining instance to a town already drawn converts the district whose character vector lies nearest the kind's identity row toward it by item 22's least-disruption mutation, as a dossier event at §4.11's step (e) (§7.7 item 5): its S6 kind re-typed, the allocation's delta placed in S10b's least-disruption order, nothing re-rolled

dispersed — every ordinary class (smiths, alchemists, chapels, bakers, inns, shops, houses): S7b (1) spreads it over all districts by capacity and affinity with a controlled random share of the affinity score (dispersal.random 0.3; drawn on alloc.district, no new concern), so some districts hold several, some one, some none, and no rule gathers a dispersed class into one district (J-A72.46); FTG's sub-district clumping (S7b (2)) stays the parity presets' behaviour and a cluster-tag option inside one district
items.note: tension with S7b (2) sub-districts: resolved (parity preset + cluster-tag option)

items.statement: singular — a one-off anchor (cathedral, palace, university, great market): sited by its own rules (S3's reservations, S7b (3)'s claims, its hard rows), weighing on its district through its σ and on the districts around through (5)'s anchors

(4) Quarter identities (item 72 (d′); RosterTables.quarterIdentities, §10.2): each row a σ-weighted count of class families with a threshold (a count, or per hectare for rows scaling with the district), optional band condition, priority and singular flag (religious quarter: chapels and churches weight 1, cathedral or great temple 3, threshold 3); S12c gives each district the highest-priority row whose threshold and band condition it meets (a singular row to its highest-scoring district only); else its dominant component — the family of its largest mix share or the sector of its largest sectors share when that exceeds identity.dominantMin (0.35) — named by that family's or sector's row; else a plain residential identity by its band ("the modest quarter"): an identity, never an S6 kind (J-P1 refined, J-A72.42)

A dossier-declared identity — a district-defining instance's, or the kind bias of a naming claim matched to the district (§7.7, item 82) — wins over every emergent one; District.identity records the row, its source (dossier, emergent, dominant, plain) and the week it was taken (§2.5); the kind stays the typing later stages read; the identity names and describes the district (§10.4; J-A72.42)

(5) Band range (item 72 (d‴); owner: a neighbourhood's prosperity defines the floor and ceiling of what any building inside can be): S10a writes each district's bandRange = [floor, ceiling] (§2.5) from its area-weighted mean pass-2 value by RosterTables.bandRanges (§10.2: a row per band split at the band's middle — the rich band's upper half the rich band alone; a prosperous district spanning middle band to rich, item 71's mix; a poor one squalid to modest), so S10b and S11 read it before they place and build

Every prosperity-driven state of a building inside the district stays in the range: the class a new build or re-designation takes (item 71's weights outside are 0, rest renormalised, §4.7 S10b), the template row's band it reads (a band outside read at the range's nearest end), its condition and upkeep, its extensions (mutator adapt and add steps, §4.7 S11), its occupants' band, its interior-ladder rung (§2.6, read at the occupants' band)

wiring.read_by: S10b; S11 mutator; §2.6 interior ladder; V02; V03
