items.statement: Occupants' band vs range: S7b (1) allocates by the range bandRanges gives at the district's area-weighted mean pass-1 value (provisional, never stored); S10a, writing bandRange from pass 2 at its step (ii), moves any household S7b allocated to a district whose written range excludes its band to the first district in S7b's order whose range admits it and whose capacity holds it, before its step (iii) distributes households to blocks — each move reported; a household no such district holds goes to the district, in S7b's order, whose range lies nearest its band and whose capacity holds it — or, when it fills a dossier's population and no district's capacity holds it, stays in its own, housed by §4.7's re-provision (Households per building; J-A20.72) — its band read at that district's range's nearest end (a derived band, reported), never a shortfall, so the population stays whole (§7.7 item 2), as §13.2's T19-4 bars; only a household filling no dossier's population and held by no district's capacity meets F-SITING's ladder (§5.2); the range always holds the district's own band (J-A72.50)
items.note: one very long sentence; ladder of fallbacks for household placement

items.statement: Item 31's geometry floor still keeps a standing shell (a mansion in a district that fell keeps its geometry, while condition, occupants and interior are bounded by the range — subdivided, worn); no informal cluster and no hovel goes up in any district whose range excludes the squalid band (§4.7 Informal clusters)

(6) The three dials (item 72 (d″), (d4)): driver terms of the prosperity field with declared weights, never replacing other drivers, each moving a building's prosperity-driven state within its district's range and clamped there; they read the applied standings and shares of §4.11's hysteresis (PowerStanding.appliedStanding, §7.7 layer 2; each sector's applied share, the fold of §4.11 The dials' inputs over epochs, derived on replay, never stored); with N powers a power's amplification A_p = N × appliedStanding_p (1 at an even standing)

wiring.reads_or_produced_by: applied standings/shares (§4.11 fold; V08 dossier slices)

items.statement: Port rows on the dials (item 88; J-A88.42): when the dossier port fills §10.2's staged rows (PortRows), the governing power's A_p (the standing whose governing holds) is multiplied by PortRows.legitimacy, and a dossier institution's visible impairment (DossierInstitution.impairments, §14; §7.7's F4 row) whose type is a non-physical row of PortRows.impairments (physical: false) lowers that institution's own term by conditionSteps × severity × dial.conditionStep; while the rows are empty legitimacy reads 1 and no impairment acts

The institution dial: every class and infrastructure element answers to its powers (BuildingClassRow.powers, RosterTables.powerLinks, §10.2; the dossier's Institution.powers override, §2.7); an instance's term dial.institutionWeight × Σ_p w_i(p) × (A_p − 1) scales its institution attractor kernel in field pass 2 and steps its condition by one step per dial.conditionStep of the term; a rising power's institutions extend within the range (mutator's adapt budget)

The quarter dial: a district whose identity row names a power (QuarterIdentityRow.power) adds dial.quarterWeight × (A_p − 1) to its characterOffset in pass 1 — at generation only for a dossier-declared district-defining quarter (known at S6), for an emergent identity from the next epoch on (J-A72.40)

The economy dial (owner: "the market share affects their application"): sector amplification A_s = S × share_s (S the sectors the slice lists; even mix → every A_s = 1); an instance's blend A_i = Σ_s w_i(s) × A_s of (7); term dial.economyWeight × (A_i − 1) scales its class's driver kernel in both passes (trade-led town lifts markets, warehouses, quays; toll-led its gates, bridges, roads) and steps its condition as above — a 40 % sector amplifies its classes twice as strongly as a 20 % one, an even mix changes nothing, no term for rank (J-A72.49); the same shares shift the roster's town-level character (§4.2 S2, §10.2; J-A72.43)

Trade as a driver: the gate and main-street kernels scale by 1 + trade.kernelScale × their gate's or way's trade weight (§4.3; trade.kernelScale 1.0); the map reads the make-up and standings, never models the economy or powers (D-10, D-32; item 20)

Dial defaults (our own, calibratable): dial.institutionWeight 0.10, dial.quarterWeight 0.08, dial.economyWeight 0.10, dial.conditionStep 0.05, each an extension the parity presets set to 0, as they do trade.kernelScale

(7) Shared buildings partitioned, never doubled (item 72 (d5); J-A72.48): an instance serving several powers or sectors receives one amplification: w_i(p) = link_i(p) × appliedStanding_p ÷ Σ_q link_i(q) × appliedStanding_q over the powers it serves (link its class or override weights), toward sector s likewise with applied shares; each set sums to one; amplification is the weighted blend, never their sum; contributions (σ in (2)'s mix, powers, sectors and pressure) split in the same proportions (a guild chapel serving craft guild and church counts once, split by relative strength)

(8) The pressure (item 72 (d‴); J-A72.47): at each epoch's character step (§4.11) District.pressure (§2.5; in the model digest; written only by epochs) becomes pressure.retain × pressure + Σ_i σ_i × excess_i ÷ Σ_i σ_i (excess_i the amount instance i's amplified value would lie above the ceiling band's upper cut, positive, or below the floor band's lower cut, negative; pressure.retain 0.5); the next epoch's pass 1 adds pressure.weight × pressure (0.5) to characterOffset; so a thriving institution lifts its neighbourhood over epochs until the value crosses its cut past the hysteresis, the range moves and buildings may follow by §4.11's ladder; no brush writes it; with no epoch it is 0

(9) Over time (item 72 (b)): at each epoch the character step recomputes the vector, adds the clamped excess to the pressure and re-derives each identity with hysteresis: a district takes a new identity row only when that row's weighted count exceeds its threshold by identity.hysteresis (20 %) while the held row's has fallen below its own, for identity.dwellEpochs (2) epochs running; a district whose held identity row names an S6 kind (QuarterIdentityRow.kind) is re-typed to it by the epoch (a lifecycle edit of District.kind, cause the epoch) — later placements read the new kind's rows, nothing standing re-rolled, stock follows by §4.11's ladder; a new identity renames the district only by §6.3's epoch case (§10.4), old name kept in District.nameHistory

(10) Emulation and staging: vector, identities, range and partition derived and draw-free; the dispersal share, identities' kinds, dials and pressure are extension rows, zero or off in the parity presets (kinds stay S6's, no dial enters the field; item 23); the dossier's standings, shares, partners and district-defining institutions are SettlementForge inputs typed now as §7.7's slices and assignments; the epoch's recomputation, renames and pressure run on the staged evolution engine's epochs (§4.11), whose step and records the base carries; the bars are §13.2's (item 72)

S8 scope: runs per district (one batch each, districts in lineage order in the generation worker) on every coarse face except its reservations (a reservation inside a face is a hole) and its wall strips (never cut, §4.8) whose kerb polygon kerb(F) (the kernel's single kerb function: face minus buffered spines, §3.7) step 1's stop test does not already accept as a block (each face's threshold inside the district's block-depth range, from the granularity law's plot depths at pass-1 band, §4.7, and the regime floor, §4.4)

wiring.reads_or_produced_by: S7b claims; S7 strips; kerb §3.7; granularity §4.7

items.statement: In walled regimes faces are district-scale, so S8's recursion produces every intramural lane and secondary and propagates the wall's and shore's direction into the fabric (MFP-2); S8 plans each cut on kerb(F) of current L1 faces, inserts each accepted lane at L1 in the district's transaction extended to the crossed spine as a T-junction (step 7), recurses on the children's kerbs; S9's corridorUnion then commits exactly those kerbs (contract test "S8's working block ≡ S9's committed block, Hausdorff 0", §13.2), so no insetRing by corridor half-widths is needed (GEO-20)

The wall is a barrier: S7 has cut each enceinte's wall strips off the faces beside the trace (§4.8), so kerb(F) of a face beside a wall stops at the strip's boundary (inner setback line, or the intervallum's kerb where the era row has one); no cut planned through a wall's band or setback; band, tower and gatehouse faces built later inside strips by S10's step (0), so S8 never meets an L3 face
S8 wall test: on every walled B-CITY seed, 0 lanes cross a wall strip and 0 L3 band faces are cleared or split by an L1 batch

Sides (GEO-22): before any rule reads a side, the face boundary is reduced to runs (kernel sideRuns §3.4): maximal boundary chains whose cumulative turning stays within 10°, each with its chord direction; a crossing street's fillet arc replaced by its virtual corner (NG PF-1's method); "perpendicular to a side" measured against the run's chord or, on a curved run, the tangent over a ±5 m window at the contact point — never the one short segment a cut hits on a Chaikin-smoothed, round-joined kerb; M0 (b)'s face set is §16's

The recipe (MN-3): the mechanism of NG 1.2.2's plain bisector as read in its code (reader-tier, via the digest) restated in our metric terms; profile's measured statistics remain the §13.5 targets; MFCG 12710731 and VG 1.6.9 differ where step 5 says; given a face F, steps 1–11
items.note: clean-room provenance statement §17.1

items.statement: Step 1 stop test: obb(F); face stops as a block when its minor extent is under a threshold drawn from cut.stop: τ = e_lo·(e_hi/e_lo)^g (power by dmath.pow §6.5 (3)), g = |(u₁+u₂+u₃+u₄)/2 − 1| — four uniforms folded into a bell over [0, 1] (mean 7/30, mass near 0) — so most faces stop close to the shallow end and a few run deeper (provenance ref:NG 1.2.2 per-face stop threshold (code), P1; NG and MFCG compare area; ours re-expresses on extent because a block's depth decides whether frontage rows fit; J-A34.41)

Block-depth range (stated once): e_lo = max(2·d_lo, r_lo), e_hi = max(2·d_hi, r_hi) — two back-to-back rows of the band's shallowest and deepest plots, floored by the regime — [d_lo, d_hi] the plot-depth band the granularity law gives the district at its pass-1 band (GranularityLaw.bands(…).depthM, §4.7 S10 (2): interpolated along the prosperity value, scaled by the rung's depth factor), [r_lo, r_hi] the district's stage regime's block-depth band floor (§4.4; both 0 for a regime whose row gives none); the band's plot depth d̄ = (d_lo + d_hi)/2; the band's upper block area e_hi² (J-A34.42); depth rows and regime floors re-fitted at M-1 under this reading (§13.5's blocks row)

wiring.read_by: S7b (3) claim threshold e_hi²; step 8 substitution bound; deep-interior rule; §13.5

items.statement: Slope term (COV-MFCG-C05): on a face whose mean slope exceeds 5 %, the working major axis is the OBB major axis rotated toward the contour direction by weight min(0.5, slope/0.3), so cuts on a hillside run with the fall line and blocks lie along contours (our own rule — no reference reacts to slope; provenance own, cell marked extension {over: 'both', mode: 'option'}, so parity presets switch it off, §7.6; J-A33.42)

Step 2 position: f = (c + b)/2 along the working major axis, c the relative position (0–1) of F's area centroid's projection, b the average of three uniforms from cut.t; no outlier term, clamp or redraw — f never strays more than 0.25 from (0.5 + c)/2; a lopsided face is cut toward its mass (P2); on a holed or annular face f = m + (1 − 2m)·b over the outer ring's OBB length, m = min(0.45, e_lo ÷ that length), no centroid term (NG's hole-aware law, P2); the σ of 0.066 (plain) and 0.098 (holed) that §13.5 and §16 M0 (b) read are NG's measured outputs, never inputs (J-A35.41)

Step 3 start: the minor-axis line at f meets F in one segment around the OBB centre's projection (concave face: the segment containing the point nearest to it); its two ends are candidate starts, one on each long side; start A is the candidate on the run whose chord is most nearly parallel to the working major axis (ties: earlier run in boundary order), deterministic with no draw (P3; J-A36.41); runs are ours (GEO-22); leave A exactly perpendicular to its run

Step 4 corner: first leg leaves A along its run's inward normal; λ = how far it runs inside F before reaching the boundary; corner K sits o + (λ − 2o)·b from A (b the average of three uniforms from cut.t; o = e_lo, on a holed/annular face o = e_lo/2), or at λ/2 when λ < 2o, so the bend lands near mid-course and at least o from both ends (P4); K fixed before any far side is chosen (J-A37.41, superseding J-P16's perpendicular-ray far side and its fallback chain)

Step 5 far side and second leg: among runs facing the first leg (inward normal against its direction), whose perpendicular foot from K falls inside the run and whose segment K–foot crosses no other boundary, the far run is the one whose chord (curved run: tangent at the foot) meets the first leg nearest a right angle (ties: earlier run); second leg is K's perpendicular onto that run (every cut arrives square); no such run: plan fails (E_NOT_TWO_CROSSINGS) and step 8's ladder takes the face (P4); two bends never (3/519 in NG's measurement)
Measurement M0 (b): compares our block-area, cut-length and junction-angle distributions with NG's on the same faces — the check of the adopted rule (§16)

Straight or bent: table row cut.bendMode (J-A37.42): flatten (default; P5) — cut A → K → foot, K dropped (A → foot) when the triangle A–K–foot has height below max(cut.flattenM, 0.02 × |A–foot|), cut.flattenM = 0.7 m (provenance own: NG's two model units ≈ 0.7 m through its export scale 0.35 per unit — an inference recalibrated at M-1 on §13.5's bent-cut signature); straightFirst — the MFCG parity preset's value (P5; VG likewise): straight A → first leg's hit if the first leg arrives at the run it hits within asin(√0.99) of square (≈84.3°, tested without trigonometry: the unit directions' cross product squared exceeds 0.99) and step 8's checks pass; otherwise planned as under flatten; the preset reads cut.flattenM = 8 m (MFCG's default two model units at its 4 m export unit), reproducing MFCG's street signature (§13.5) through §7.6's per-preset values

Step 6 fillet (COV-NG-N19): lane and street cuts only, never lot cuts (§4.7); at a kept corner with deflection δ and shorter leg ℓ, one draw from cut.arc keeps it sharp with probability s + (1 − s)·min(1, w_min/ℓ), s = sin²(δ/2) = (1 − cos δ)/2, cos δ = û₁·û₂ (no trigonometric call), w_min the district's minimum plot frontage (low end of GranularityLaw.bands(…).frontageM at pass-1 band); otherwise K gives way to a circular arc tangent where the shorter leg ends and, along the longer leg, as far from K as that end is, sampled in equal chords no shorter than w_min or the lattice minimum edge; an arc with under three sample points or leaving the face leaves the corner sharp; radius follows from the legs, never a constant (P6, shared by MFCG; J-A38.41); NG's measured 53 % filleted share is this rule's output (§13.5 fillet bar)

Step 7 ends in the model (GEO-21): each junction end extended along its arrival direction from the kerb to the crossed spine and inserted there as a T-junction (splitThrough §3.4), so the L1 face splits and the lane joins the street graph, junction census, betweenness and R3; NG's "stop half the crossed road's width short, square caps" is the renderer's stroke rule, produced by S9's corridor union and junction wedge; a cut end meeting a dead end or hole follows §3.6's contact semantics (antenna end → T-junction; hole joined by connectHole §3.4); an end arriving at a wall strip's setback line (no spine) stays there square to the line as a lane ends at a reservation; an end at the intervallum is a T-junction like any other

Seam portals (J-P32): when the crossed spine bounds the district (an arterial or boundary secondary) the T-junction's vertex lies on a chain two districts share, so S8 records it as a baseLane portal with its SeamAmendment in the shared Seam record of that boundary run (II.1), which both districts' contracts read; a planned end inside the portal gap of an existing portal on that spine — max(6 m, 2 × the wider lane's width), a table row — slides along the spine out of the gap toward the side keeping its arrival within 85–95°; if neither side does, the cut takes its next ladder rung; so two districts' lanes never meet at one boundary vertex (the crossroads step 10 forbids) and each portal vertex carries exactly one lane

When a re-derivation removes a lane, its end vertex loses its portal role (removeEdges on its VertexRef, §3.4) and is dissolved; its portal and amendment leave the Seam record, so the spine reads exactly as before the lane, and the neighbour step's reversal restores the neighbour's kerb (II.1 (3))

A district's effective scope — its own faces plus this seam exception (the chains, corridors, strips, wedges, neighbouring rings and Seam records its lane ends touch) — is §7.3 item 1's; every other entity of every other district stays byte-identical, and the locality oracle checks exactly that (§7.3, II.4)
items.note: multi-stated seam exception (earlier compression target)

items.statement: Step 8 transaction and ladder (GEO-23): before step 1, on any face with a reflex vertex deeper than the band's plot depth (L- and C-shaped faces, faces wrapped round a cul-de-sac antenna), a reflex pre-cut splits the face perpendicular to the reflex vertex's longer run, and antennae are split off at their roots (FTG's fix for internal corners); then splitFace(F, cut) as a transaction; reject if either child violates minEdge, min angle or the class's minimum block width

Cut ladder, each rung under an operation-count work limit: (a) a turned frame — re-plan steps 2–7 in the working frame turned by 36° (attempt k turned by k × 36°; ≤ 2 more frames, ≤ 3 in all), drawing afresh from cut.t for steps 2 and 4 on the stream key's attempt component (§5.1 (6)) (P7; NG retries like MFCG in frames turned by 36° up to ten times, then NG leaves the face whole and MFCG restarts the whole city — ours bounded, restarts nothing, D-9; J-A39.41); (b) the straight cut from A along the mean normal (average of start run's inward normal and far run's outward normal as found in the unturned frame; start run's inward normal alone when step 5 found no far run); (c) the always-succeeding cut — straight, perpendicular to the longest run through its midpoint, clipped to F's own component by boolean intersection; when §3.6's contact rule refuses it (interior within attractCm of a shallow reflex vertex or touching an antenna) its foot slides along the longest run in steps of 2·attractCm, alternating sides of the midpoint (first toward the run's lower (y, x) end), each candidate re-clipped and re-tested under the rung's work limit, until the contact rule passes (for k shallow reflex vertices at most 2k candidates fail; a run too short to hold one passing candidate is a face below the band's block width, which step 1 already types a block); the slide draws nothing and is reported as W_CUT_SLID with its step count (J-Fredteam-1); (d) substitution — F becomes a court, green or landmark block chosen from the district allocation's pending claims (NG's substitution rule, K6) — only for faces ≤ 2 × the band's upper block area; a larger face reaching (d) is cut by (c) again (that slide, never a repeat of a refused cut); no rung restarts anything above F
Every district reports the share of its built land left as court or green by substitution (soft bound ≤ 5 %), so MFCG's "empty areas inside city walls" cannot return silently

Step 9 width (COV-NG-N20): one scalar per lane w = w_lo + Δw·min(1, L/L_ref)^p, Δw = w_hi − w_lo, [w_lo, w_hi] the cut class's metric width band (alleys 2–3 m, lanes 3–5 m), L final kerb-to-kerb length, L_ref the district OBB's major extent, p one draw per district on cut.width with ln p uniform between ln 0.5 and ln 2 (p = 0.5·4^u; powers by dmath.pow §6.5 (3)) — longer cuts wider, saturating at the band's top (P8; free-end term withdrawn as a drawing artefact; J-A40.41); in a walled regime a cut exceeding the lane length band is typed secondary; never narrower than a lower class (O4 c); template roads take fixed per-district widths (II.2)

Step 10 continuation (J-P11): a cut may continue across an existing lower-or-equal-class street when collinear within 6° (the rare crossroads) — only inside its own district, never across a district-boundary edge (GEO-42)
Step 11 recurse on both children with their own sub-streams

Deep-interior rule (IMP-8, GEO-25; J-P15): when recursion stops and a block's local thickness exceeds twice its band's plot depth, the district's band row chooses the interior now, in S8, by target shares: court (hollow block, perimeter plots around a shared court), back_lane (lane spine through the middle, parallel to the longer frontage), through_alley (alley spine joining two opposite frontages), rear_plots (second row reached through the front row); defaults poor court 0.35, back lane 0.25, through-alley 0.30, rear plots 0.10; modest 0.45/0.30/0.15/0.10; prosperous 0.65/0.15/0.05/0.15; rich 0.75/0.10/0/0.15 — our own values, calibrated at M-1 on NG's hollow-block frequency and MFCG's inner-lot removal; rows keyed by §4.5's band set (a band without a row interpolates, item 27); lanes and alleys chosen here inserted as L1 spines in S8's own district batch (S10 never writes L1), so no sibling block left stale
Keep-test: the court share of deep blocks within band per class (§13.5)

Hidden plots and reach (item 30): a court or rear_plots interior is reached from the public way by the block's reach, drawn with the treatment and recorded beside it (Block.reach, §2.5); S10 builds what it names: open — an open slot between two front buildings, an alley face (§4.7 S10 (9)) or the L1 spine of a back_lane or through_alley (the references' every-plot-fronts-a-street baseline and the parity presets' only value, item 23); passage — a covered way under a front building: an L3 face of kind passage (alley-as-face) of width passage.widthM (2.4–3.5 m by band) S10 cuts along one side line of the front plot the rule picks (widest frontage in the middle third of the run) from the kerb to the court or rear row; front plot keeps identity and its footprint ends at the passage's edge; S11 gives its building a wing spanning the passage at every storey above ground (BaseWing.spans §2.6; plan rung reserves the cells, item 28); chosen only where the front row is continuous (arrangement row), else reach stays open; gated — an opening in a frontage enclosure (PlotBound gate of a compound's wall or gatehouse arch, §4.7 S11) into a private court, chosen only where arrangement is compound or detached

wiring.read_by: Block.reach; S10 (9) passage faces; S11 spanning wing; BaseWing.spans; V02 buildings; V03 plan rung

items.statement: Reach weights (band rows): squalid and poor open 0.25, passage 0.75, gated 0; modest 0.70/0.30/0; comfortable 0.80/0.15/0.05; prosperous 0.60/0.05/0.35; rich 0.30/0/0.70 — interpolated along the prosperity value, non-open weights scaled by (0.5 + density) and by the rung (TOWN 0.6, CITY 1.0, METROPOLIS 1.2; village rung rows 0, PART III); the draw is the block's interior draw (cut.interior, one pair: treatment, reach)

Hidden-share target per band row (district share of plots with exposure hidden): squalid 0.20, poor 0.12, modest 0.04, comfortable 0.02, prosperous 0.04, rich 0.08, ± 0.03; read at the district's plots' area-weighted mean prosperity value (interpolated), scaled by the rung factor (TOWN 0.6, CITY 1.0, METROPOLIS 1.2) and by (0.5 + district's area-weighted mean density value), capped at one; base weights fitted at M-1 on B-CITY so every rung's districts meet their scaled targets; §13.2's bar checks each district against its own (§13.7's row holds the fit's fallback; our own values, calibratable, J-T; 0 in parity presets and every village rung); made deliberately, never left over (J-A30.41)

Exposure (item 30 (a)): when S10 types a plot's access edges it sets Plot.exposure (§2.5) by reading the block's interior access graph (plots, alley faces, passage faces, court residues; edge between two nodes sharing an L3 edge; public kerbs — corridor edges of every L1 way, alley and cul_de_sac spines included — as roots), by adjacency and reach depth, never a sight line (J-A30.42): street — an access edge on the kerb of a through, primary, secondary or quay way; lane — on a lane, cul_de_sac, track or path kerb and none on a street; alley — only on an alley face or through_alley spine's kerb, each open to a public kerb at its ends; court — only on a court residue whose own reach to a public kerb is one open step; hidden — every access edge on a face whose reach to any public kerb passes a passage face or gated opening, or two or more interior faces; sealed — a hidden plot whose every reach passes a sealed passage (§2.8, §4.11)

Access guarantee unchanged: every plot, hidden ones included, has ≥ 1 access edge and a chain of access faces to a public kerb (F-PLOT §5.2; chain-reachability bar §13.2); knowledge is a separate fact: knownTo on plot, building and institution records (§2.5, §2.6) takes §2.5's default and is otherwise a dossier fact; it moves label visibility and the reader's answers (§9.2), never geometry; a local or secret institution prefers hidden plots through the placement solver's exposure row (§4.7 S10b, item 16; concealed institution's mode and front: §4.7, item 63)

At the city band a hidden court draws as a court behind buildings (ground and court tones under the building masses, §8.5), never as an empty block; hidden plots arise, are sealed and reopen over epochs by §4.11's kinds; a user seals or opens a passage, hides or reveals a place by §7.1's events; villages have no hidden share by default (PART III)

Holes (NG's hole-aware bisector, C13 — ours): a cut that would cross a hole is routed to the hole's boundary (a slit committed by connectHole §3.4), the annulus becomes simply connected and the same ladder applies (step 2's holed position law and step 4's halved offset) — the primitive the stage-2 ring template needs (II.2); cuts inserted as lane/alley/secondary spines (lanes real ways in the same graph); junction fillets at street corners are a style-time smoothing (Urban Places' arcs), not a model change

Partition recipes (COV-MFCG-G03): PartitionRecipe rows built only from the kernel's splitFace, radialSplit, ringBand, insetRing (§3.4): fan (k radial cuts from the centroid with alley-width gaps), semiFan (from a boundary vertex), ring (an inset band around a court, split into segments by slit cuts, short sides first); used by park layouts (§4.9) and institution templates (cloister, quadrangle; §4.7 S11)

wiring.read_by: §4.9 park layouts; §4.7 S11 institution templates; V02

items.statement: The strategy slot: S8 calls FabricStrategy.partition(district); the base registers BentCutFabric; stage 2 registers RingFabric, SquareFabric, StreetFabric (G-P2, §14)

An alley that presents itself (items 29, 30, 31): for item 29's side and rear entrances an alley presents itself exactly when the back_lane, through_alley or rear_plots treatment, or S10's alley rung and passage choice (§4.7 S10 (9)), gives the plot an access edge beyond its frontage (Plot.access, §2.5); §2.6's entrance rules read that edge set and nothing else

Back courts across epochs: §4.11's rung 2 makes and unmakes such interiors on standing plots: densify … back_court cuts a yard into rear plots reached by a new passage where the passage choice allows one and the plot's manifested band's row (§4.11's floor) carries a rear-plot or hidden share (a middle-floored plot's yard is infilled instead); thin … back_court clears one — households re-homed and buildings vacated first (§4.11 rung 2) — and seals its passage; each a recorded event through this rule's shares, never a re-cut of the block's interior

The staged crime term (item 88; J-A88.41): when the dossier port fills §10.2's staged crime row (PortRows.crime: settlement crime scalar in [0, 1]; schema-complete and empty in the base), it multiplies each district's hidden-share target by 1 + crime.hiddenScale × crime (default 0.5), item 64 (b)'s basement-access probability (II.7.3 Basement accesses (2)) by 1 + crime.accessScale × crime (default 1.0) and item 65's undercity demand (II.7.5 size law) by 1 + crime.undercityScale × crime (default 1.0) — its three readers, each citing this statement; row empty → every factor 1 (our own rows, extension, 0 in parity presets)

wiring.read_by: hidden-share 0281; II.7.3 basement accesses; II.7.5 size law; V04

items.statement: S9 Corridors (L2): corridorUnion(l1Faces) (§3.7), the single kerb function, commits exactly the kerbs S8 cut against — half-corridor strips, junction wedges and built blocks; runs once per district and once for the hinterland's faces; a wall strip's L2 is its half-corridor strips along the arterials at its gates (and along the intervallum where there is one) and one built block, the strip block (§4.8)

The main plaza is S3's reservation, typed as a square face; other squares come from S7b claims sized from population (O7); gate plazas and forecourts from S7 (§4.8); streets exist as geometry from here on; "negative-space streets" is purely a style, and §8's figure-ground contract fills blocks in a ground tone

S10a Block allocation and field pass 2 (eager, town-wide; LC-2, FTG-1): each district's Allocation distributed to its blocks in three declared steps from the district's alloc.block stream (keyed from the district's lineage; §2.5, §6.1), blocks by score then id: (i) field-driving classes — noxious trades, middens, prisons, institutions below a block — first by scores needing no prosperity (downstream, downwind, extramural, frontage class, adjacency); (ii) field pass 2 adds their kernels to pass 1 (§4.5), from which each district's band range is written and any household S7b allocated outside it re-homed (§4.5 (5)); (iii) every other class — households by band, ordinary workplaces, shops — by capacity per band under pass 2, sub-districts receiving contiguous block groups sized to their clusters (COV-FTG-E02); result persisted as one block-level Allocation per block

wiring.read_by: block Allocation (§2.5); pass 2; bandRange; S10; S10b

items.statement: The block score is S10b's rule score at block granularity (item 16): a class's relation rows and supply edges (§10.2) evaluated against the block's context — frontage classes, distance rasters at its centroid, classes already allocated to it and to the town's other blocks — so a brewery's block scores its distance to the blocks holding its maltings and granary and a tannery's its downstream, downwind and extramural rows before any plot exists; hard rows filter blocks, soft rows and supply distances weight them

From S10a on, every district's S10, S10b, S11 and S12b, and the hinterland unit's, is a pure function of these records and its own sub-stream writing only inside its own faces (§4.1), so content does not depend on derivation order, viewer order or worker count
items.note: restates laziness contract (0013)

items.statement: S10 (0) Shared-edge bands, eager (J-I9): a block whose interior is wall_strip gets no plots; its L3 content built eagerly on the generation worker after S10a and before the pool's freeze, in one step covering the strip blocks on both sides of each trace at once (band cross edges split the trace, which both sides' districts share, so no district overlay may write it; §3.3 pool steps 1 and 3; cost §12.4); commits by bandUnion (§3.7) the enceinte's half-band on each side of the wall edge; the rest of each strip — inner setback, or outer setback and glacis, or berm up to a moat — as typed unbuildable residue (setback, glacis; ditch in place of glacis on the town side of an on_enceinte bailey whose castle template row asks for a dry ditch, §4.8); each side's parts of every tower and gatehouse on the trace; the same batch lays §4.5's margin bands along the perimeter and any reservation boundary two districts share

The enceinte's band and glacis (ditch parts included) and each tower's and gate's footprint are the unions of these parts across the strip blocks (§2.7); S9 has already committed the strip's corridors and nothing after S10 writes L1 or L2, so no batch ever clears or splits these faces; the step ends by rebuilding the L3 static partitions it touched, so a pooled plot line finds the band's inner edge through the index (§3.3 pool step 1); a regeneration re-runs this step one-sided for its own scope (§7.3 item 2); a castle's curtain band built the same way inside the bailey's blocks; the hinterland unit's S10 builds §4.9's hinterland recipe instead of frontage-first plots

S10 per built block (1)-(2): (1) classify each kerb edge as a frontage by way class; (2) read the block's context (district kind, prosperity value and recorded band, density, growth stage) → the granularity table gives target frontage-width and depth bands, a join maximum and a vacancy-run share, interpolated along the prosperity value and scaled by the rung's RungProfile.granularity (frontage × and depth × on every band; the rich band's join maximum + joinMaxDelta; §1.1, AM-4) — GranularityLaw.bands takes the rung (§14)

wiring.read_by: plots; S8 block-depth range; fillet w_min

items.statement: Band rows are §4.5's band set (item 27); every re-derivation other than a rung-3 event of §4.11's ladder reads the block's manifested band — the field band raised to its plots' geometry floor by §4.11's block-level reading (item 31; J-A31.43) — for every geometry row, and the field band for occupancy, condition and labels; the band row also carries the target share of interior and hidden plots that S8's deep-interior rule and this stage's cut meet together (§4.6, item 30)

Granularity table (default rows; all calibratable, J-T §13.7): poor/dense frontage 4–6 m (log-normal, CV 0.25), depth 12–20 m, join max 1, vacancy-run share 0.03 (NG 95–99 % attached, party walls 39–43 % of perimeter); modest 6–9, 18–30, 2, 0.06 (FTG quad side median 10.3 m, footprint median 103 m²); prosperous 9–14, 25–40, 3, 0.08 (MFCG ≈18.6 lots per block); rich 14–25 (joined), 30–60, 5, 0.05 (owner: fewer, bigger buildings, bigger yards and courts); institution/assigned by requirement class, by requirement, whole block above a share threshold, — (FTG landmark-first)

wiring.read_by: S10; S8 depth range; S2 plotArea; §13.7

items.statement: S10 (3) Claims first: institutions and assignments smaller than a block claimSubFace (may span several faces, §3.4) the contiguous area and frontage class their requirement demands (the designation template's size budget, S11, item 19) before ordinary plots are cut (larger ones are S7b reservations); claims-first covers every claim existing at generation — the roster's institutions and requirement classes and every assignment or dossier element present in the recipe (they enter S2's demand; §7.7, item 22 (d)); one arriving after the city is built is placed by S10b's solver and applied by S11's mutation (§7.7)

S10 (4) Per-frontage regions (GEO-24; J-P13): the block (minus claims and S8 interior) partitioned into one region per frontage run by its straight skeleton, each region's depth capped by skeleton height and band depth — if the skeleton is downgraded (F-SKELETON) a reflex pre-cut partition (a perpendicular cut from every reflex vertex, built exactly from sideRuns and splitFace) is used instead; validated skeleton arcs enter the arena through insertChain (§3.8); plots laid as strips perpendicular to each region's frontage, widths from the band, depth = min(band depth, region depth); side lines are bent lot cuts perpendicular to the frontage arriving at the region's rear line; strips never leave their region, so reflex corners, notches round cul-de-sacs and tight curves cannot produce overlapping or hourglass plots (property test §13.2)

S10 (5) Corners and seams: the corner plot takes the higher-class frontage and the shorter frontage's depth; the wedge left between two regions becomes a corner plot when it meets the minimum width and angle, else a declared wedge class (bounded < 0.5 %) or residue
S10 (6) Residue typed: court (from the S8 interior), yard (assigned to the adjacent plot when its area < 1.5 × the plot), green, vacant, shore (the shore setback)

S10 (7) Joins and splits, one law: strips cut to the band's lower end, then a merge operator joins k adjacent plots (along a frontage, or back to back keeping a frontage) up to the band's upper end, keeping members; poor bands stay at the lower end; both directions read the same context vector — one code path (O18 g); orderings (item 31): a join takes vacant or same-owner neighbours first, then a rear plot into its front plot, then the frontage neighbour with the shorter frontage; a split takes the widest frontage first, then the deepest yard

A designation's size budget (S11's template) is what a join is asked for — by S10 at generation, by S10b's solver for a later placement (a JOIN request), by S11's mutator when a designation outgrows its plot; a larger class placed by S10b's class mix asks this law for its join (item 71); across epochs the law runs incrementally — a due block re-cut with its neighbours fixed under §4.11's ladder, churn cap and geometry floor (item 31) — and a plot vacated by decline merges into a neighbour's garden or a field by the same operator (plotToGarden, amalgamate; §4.11, item 8)

S10 (8) Vacancy runs (COV-VG-VN-170): runs of frontage totalling the band's vacancy share, each at least one band frontage long, left unbuilt from the plot.vacancy stream — typed vacant, or a garden yard joined to the neighbour — so no built block is necessarily fully ringed

S10 (9) Alleys: slivers narrower than the minimum plot width that connect two ways become alley L3 faces, not spines (GEO-25); where the frontage is continuous §4.6's rule may reserve a covered passage under the front plot's building instead of an open alley (item 30; passage face §2.5)

S10 (10) Every plot gets its ContextVector, its DerivationRecord and access edges (100 %, O5 a): every plot is built with an access edge; NG's frontage-less lots (about 42 % of its lot leaves, its courts by construction) have no counterpart outside the deep-interior rule (§4.6), which chooses a deep block's interior by band shares (J-P15, J-A42.41)
Party walls are shared L3 edges carrying the party_wall role in row classes, one edge per wall (§2.2)
items.note: restated §4.1 S11 row (earlier CF-PIPE-03 now consistent)

items.statement: Unbuildable bands: the shore setback (§4.2 S1 (8)), the wall strips (band, inner setback, outer setback and glacis; MFP-9; step (0)) and reservations are never plotted; ribbon plots begin beyond the outer wall strip
Exact capacity check (FTG-2): after the last block of a stage, plots per class × band compared with the stage quota; a shortfall goes to S10b's reconcile and the report (F-BUDGET-STAGE)

S10b Placement (O7; per district; allocation honoured) — the one placement solver (item 16): each block's allocated classes placed onto its plots by the placement solver, the one solver every path that puts a use on a plot calls: this stage at generation, the hinterland unit's S10b on its outside plots, every assign event (§7.7), a dossier event and a positive placement (§7.7, items 20, 22) and the relocation of a use across epochs (§4.11, item 17); inputs are data: relation templates and supply edges of the class rows and neighbourhood kinds (§10.2), per-assignment overrides of PlacementCriteria (§7.7), the plot's ContextVector (§2.5)

wiring.read_by: Use placements; S11; §7.7 assign; V08 dossier events; V06 relocation; V09/V10 placeAt

items.statement: Hard rows filter, soft rows score: a relation row marked hard excludes every plot failing it; passing candidates scored Σ_rows w_r·s_r(plot) + Σ_edges w_e·s_e(plot); each soft row's satisfaction s_r ∈ [0,1] read from the context vector — a distance row decays by its falloff between withinM and beyondM; a sameStreet row is 1 on the frontage way of the named class's nearest placed member, 0 otherwise; a clustered row rises with the number of the class's members within its radius; band and exposure rows compare the plot's band and Plot.exposure with the row's values (item 30) — and each supply edge's s_e decays from 1 at the plot to 0 at the edge's maxDistanceM along its mode

Capacity rows (plotArea, plotShape, frontageM) read the template's size budget (S11); a hard capacity row a plot cannot meet is what a JOIN request answers (S10 (7)); candidates filled in descending score with capacity accounting, ties by plot id; households take residential plots of their band ± drift
items.note: "± drift" value not given

items.statement: Default placement rows are the references' own rules — noxious trades downstream and extramural (upstream high, outside the enceinte), mills and water trades on water, inns and the market hall at tier-1 junctions or gates (market squares themselves S3's and S7b's, item 24), religious precincts and faction turf as attractors, warehouses at the harbour, frontage class and area fit — and rows the references lack (supply edges, upwind and high-ground rows, trade clustering on one street) are soft rows whose weights placement.extensionWeight scales (default 1; parity presets of §13.6 set 0; item 23)

Supply distances by mode (item 16 (b)): street — from class distance rasters (16 m, one linear distance transform per class) as land distance × the rung's detour factor (a table cell, default 1.3, calibrated at M1 against the way-graph Dijkstra on B-CITY; pre-decided fallback: factor refitted per rung); river and sea — ∞ unless plot and provider both lie within the shore setback of one navigable water body (§4.2 S1 (8)), else the distance along that body's bank chain; road — street distance to the gate through which the provider is reached plus the provider's distance beyond it; a gate provides the import resources its bearing's trade row lists and the harbour those arriving by sea

wiring.read_by: supply edge scoring; S2 need propagation imports

items.statement: Inside the pooled S10b a provider is a block whose S10a allocation holds a producing class (eager, town-wide — laziness contract holds) or a placed plot of this district; a post-build request measures to the placed plots over the L1 way graph (one multi-source Dijkstra per provider class; budget §12.6); a hard supply edge with no provider inside maxDistanceM fails the plot; S2 has already demanded the producer (need propagation), so the failure is a siting shortfall, never a missing class

Live-in (MFP-7): craft and shop rows default to liveIn; a live-in household is sited first at its workplace and recorded as the building's dwelling, so arterial frontages are shop-houses and residential-only blocks stay the exception (block-level acceptance §13.5)

Outside classes, and under §4.9's fill farm mode the farm households, are placed by the hinterland unit's own S10b (under perimeter and rivers the farm households are town households placed by their districts' S10b) — the same solver over the outside plots its S10 built at S12a's sites, whose seeding scores are the outside classes' relation rows (§4.9; FTG-7)

Requests after the city is built (an assignment, a dossier element, a positive placement, a relocation) take the least-disruption order: vacant plots and vacancy runs first, then under-used plots (a yard part or outbuilding the template can take), then plots whose present use can move within the same district (the displaced use re-placed by this solver with one further level of displacement at most — §7.7's DisruptionBudgetRow.displacementDepth, default 1 — never a cascade), then a JOIN with a neighbour by S10 (7)'s orderings; a rejected site (§7.7 rejection record, item 20) excluded while its rejection holds, a locked plot always; a pinned assignment's plot is fixed (§7.7 precedence); among candidates passing the hard rows the order is lexicographic — disruption cost (DisruptionBudgetRow.weights for the request kind: per displaced use, per join, per subtracted part, per vacated plot), then score descending, then plot id; every displacement, join and vacated plot is a lifecycle event of the causing edit (§2.8, §7.4); the placed plot's buildings then mutate to the designation by S11's operator (item 18)

wiring.read_by: lifecycle events §2.8/§7.4; S11 mutator; V08 dossier; V06

items.statement: Concealed institutions (item 63): placed as one item with its front by the concealment rule of this section's Concealed institutions paragraph
items.note: pointer

items.statement: Reconcile and infeasibility (O18 f): at generation a bounded plan–fit–reconcile loop (≤ 3 rounds) adjusts inside the district's allocation where a class finds no plot (one more JOIN; a class demoted within its band; surplus capacity typed as yards, greens or vacant plots); never reaches into another district (moving demand between districts only in S7b's reconcile and S10a's band-range re-homing, §4.5 (5); J-A72.50); what it cannot place goes to F-SITING's ladder (§5.2), whose rungs this stage computes as: the reconcile; then every soft row's weight set to 0 for the item; then the manifest reduced, lowest-priority classes first and never a dossier-backed item (item 20) — the report naming, for every unplaced item, the hard rows that blocked it and its closest options (plots in order of the number of hard rows they fail, then score descending, then plot id — each with the rows it fails; J-A20.42)
items.note: earlier CF-PIPE-04 now consistent (F-SITING ladder named)

items.statement: A hard row is never relaxed silently: a post-build request no plot satisfies returns the same closest options as an F-EDIT action (§5.2) — choose one, relax a named row for this item, or withdraw — except a dossier request, which places at its first closest option with the hard rows it fails reported (§7.7 precedence, J-A20.71); so placement never gives up silently (O18 f; FTG V1 "would regularly give up")

wiring.read_by: F-EDIT; V09 application; V10 clerk; V08 dossier

items.statement: S10b mechanism (budget §12.4): context-vector distances from per-feature-class distance rasters (16 m; one linear distance transform per class) computed once per model, and the provider rasters of the producing classes from S10a's block allocation the same way; S10b is a top-k over candidates pre-filtered by district affinity and requirement class with incremental capacity; both entry points read from recipe.entryMode (§2.9): content-first (default) and layout-first (thumbnails, then populate); people derived lazily from the household's key, pinned only by an explicit edit (§10.3)
items.note: layout-first entry mode — its consumer path not described here

items.statement: interface PlacementItem {cls: string (roster class id); band?; designation?: Designation (S11); count? (generation: the block's allocation row); id?: Id (a Use, assignment member or dossier element placed or re-placed); criteria?: PlacementCriteria (§7.7 overrides); pinnedTo?: Id (a positive placement, §7.7, item 20 (g))}

interface PlacementRequest {kind: 'generation'|'assignment'|'dossier'|'positive'|'relocation'; items: PlacementItem[]; scope: Scope (blocks or district the solver may use, §14); fixed: Id[] (placed members kept, §7.7); exclude: Id[] (locked entities); rejected: Id[] (plots under a live rejection, §7.7)}

wiring.reads_or_produced_by: callers: S10b, hinterland S10b, §7.7 assign/dossier/positive, §4.11 relocation

items.statement: interface PlacementResult {placed: {item; plot; score; joined?: Id[]; displaced?: {use; to: Id|null}[]}[]; unplaced: {item; blockedBy: string[] (relation-row and supply-edge keys); closest: {plot; fails: string[]; score}[] (fewest hard rows failed, then score, then plot id)}[]}

wiring.read_by: F-EDIT; report; V09/V10 closest options UI

items.statement: interface PlacementSolver {place(req: PlacementRequest, ctx: StageContext, k: Kernel): KernelResult<PlacementResult>} — one implementation, registered by name (§4.12, §14); its draws are the siting concern (§6.1)

S11 Site plans and footprints (L4; O17; one batch per block) — the designation template: one rule evaluation per plot, no search: one template per roster class (§10.2 template rows; item 19), keyed by band with continuous columns interpolated along the plot's prosperity value and discrete columns switching at the band cut (§4.5); gives the size budget (plot area, footprint area, floors), structures (slot list: main building, workshop, forge, yard, court, stables, store, journeymen's rooms … by role and count), arrangement, coverage, setbacks, separation (party wall / slot / passage), front-line jitter (item 43), the frontage treatment of the main slot (none, lean-to stall, stall, shopfront, arcaded front, gate, wall), yard partition, boundary treatments and the specialisation (the designation's variant in this band with its room programme, item 28, §2.6: e.g. three rows of one smith template); density a modifier column on coverage and separation

wiring.read_by: SitePlan (§2.5); BuildingGenerator.outline (§2.6); V02 buildings; V03 programme

items.statement: Geometry columns read the plot's manifested band (§4.11 plot-level read); specialisation and programme read the field band, so a poor smith in a once-rich shell is a poor smith in a big house (item 31)

Every path that creates or changes a building reads this one table — S11 at generation, the mutator on every designation change, S10b's relocation (§4.11) and every assignment (§7.7), whose drift bounds bound the mutator's adapt and add steps relative to the template; two smiths apart differ by degree along the value, never by switch; default rows reproduce FTG's lifestyle-banded building pools and MFCG's ward-type sizes and spacing (item 27), interpolation our extension; J-A19.41 holds within a class; the class itself is S10b's class-mix draw (item 71)

A front's building reads the front's template; its concealed function adds only concealed rooms, a concealed door and a link down (item 63, Concealed institutions); materials are not template columns — the material rule, texture and colour only, is §2.6's (J-A19.42)

Arrangement rows: row — one or more footprints end to end along the frontage; footprint = plot ∩ the frontage band of the row depth (boolean, GEO-26; J-P14), the band set back by the plot's front-line jitter h, so every party wall is the plot side line and (block one L4 batch) one shared edge even on bent or curved frontages; stored as one quad wing with four corners recorded (BaseWing.corners; stepped quads on a slope each with its own; J-P31, J-P39) handed to outline() as fixed input (§2.6); depth from coverage; rear yard; boundary: frontage none, rear wall (dense) or fence; where: dense and poor bands, shops, workshops (NG 95–99 % attached; FTG's warehouse rows) · set-back compound — hall or house set back behind a forecourt, 2–5 disjoint outbuildings (stables, workshop, chapel, barn, brewhouse) placed by a small greedy packer on the plot's OBB grid around a court; enclosure wall (rich, prosperous; ours — NG draws none — an extension the parity presets set to the fence, §7.6; J-A44.41) or fence, with a gate on the access edge; manors, inns, temples, guildhalls, farmsteads · detached — one OBB-aligned footprint at the frontage with side yards and a path; frontage fence, railing (rich) or hedge with gate, side hedges; prosperous/semi-rural sparingly (R4/R5) · hovel — one small footprint on a mostly bare yard plot; none or hedge; squalid bands, outskirts · tents — 1–3 small round or rectangular footprints (6–15 m², class tent, roof tent) with a fire-pit pin, dirt surface; none; squalid and shanty districts after the first half of the stages (COV-FTG-E07), FTG's row kept by parity presets; sharing with cluster is item 70's · cluster — many small structures (shacks, tents, lean-tos by the cluster rows §10.2) packed across the plot, each with its own door on a footpath web reaching an access edge (packing, fire gap, households per structure: Informal clusters, item 70); none; informal plots of the lowest bands with no standing building where admitted · institution — the claim's own template (§2.6 footprint templates, axis-locked composer, ring recipe for a cloister); wall with gatehouse gap, churchyard wall; claims · vacant run — no footprint; wall (dense) or fence; vacancy runs

Treatments stored as §2.5's PlotBound records on the plot edges; drawn at district LOD as a stroke distinct from buildings (§8.2's treatment row); walled or fenced frontage counts toward O17 (d)'s streetwall continuity; walls and fences export to VTT and GeoJSON (VIS-8)

wiring.read_by: PlotBound (§2.5); §8.2 renderer; §11 VTT/GeoJSON export; O17 (d) metric

items.statement: Front-line jitter (item 43): each plot's main slot may stand back from its frontage by h, evaluated once per plot and stored rounded to the centimetre as SitePlan.frontJitterCm (§2.5): h = u·min(√(plot area)/3, jitter.maxM), u uniform [0,1) — one draw of the plot's siteplan stream (§6.1; no new concern) — kept only when h ≥ jitter.minM, else 0; law's shape emulated default (provenance ref:MFCG 12710731 front recession (code), P9), construction and values ours; under defaults the area term binds only on plots under ≈20 m²

Jitter construction: h taken square to the frontage on the frontage band's normal — a row footprint is plot ∩ the frontage band between offsets h and h + row depth; a detached, hovel or compound main slot's front stands h behind the template's setback — front stays parallel to a bent or curved frontage, every party wall stays the plot side line (J-P14), the strip in front is the plot's forecourt yard part (§2.5); where the plot's depth cannot hold h in front of a footprint meeting the class's floors in width and area (§3.10), h falls to the largest value that can, and to 0 when that is below jitter.minM
items.note: edge defined

items.statement: Jitter values: jitter.maxM and jitter.minM are designation-template columns (§10.2), maxM interpolated like coverage; defaults (own): jitter.maxM 0.4 m poor/dense, 0.7 m modest, 1.0 m prosperous, 1.5 m rich; jitter.minM 0.3 m all bands; each band cell marked extension {over: 'MFCG', mode: 'option'}; the MFCG parity preset reads jitter.maxM 4.8 m, jitter.minM 2 m (J-A43.41); institution, tents and cluster rows carry jitter.maxM 0, unmarked; any row whose maxM < minM draws none

Jitter floor: a front nearer its frontage than attractCm (26 cm, §3.2) would be shared by §3.6's stretch attraction and collapse to 0, so jitter.minM is bounded below by attractCm + 1 cm — the column's declared range (§7.6) — against which an editTable or editPreset setting it lower is refused naming the bound (F-EDIT, §5.2); recessions drawn are {0} ∪ [jitter.minM, jitter.maxM] (J-A43.42)

Jitter changes: a kept main slot keeps its stored recession through a designation change; an added main slot evaluates h at the target template's columns with its draw from the mutation's siteplan.mutate stream (mutator step 2); Regenerate (keep settings) re-evaluates the same draw, reproducing the same fronts; bars §13.2 (item 43)

The row arrangement's footprints are made by the boolean and passed to BuildingGenerator.outline() as fixed quad wings, returned with heights and roofs and never re-fitted (§2.6); every other arrangement's footprints come from outline() itself — rectangles and L/T compositions as rect wings with per-wing ridge axes (VIS-10), footprint templates and the axis-locked composer for institutions (COV-FTG-F16, COV-MFCG-G05) — each shaped inside its slot's working hint (SlotPlan.hint, §2.5, never stored by S11)

The first carry (J-P42): S11 inserts each footprint's rings through every wing vertex on the wings' union boundary and, when the block's batch has committed, carries every wing onto the committed face by §2.6's wing-carrying rule — from the ring it inserted to the ring the kernel committed (attraction may have moved a vertex up to attractCm, §3.6), each boundary run re-read, a rect whose sides now carry other vertices recording its corners — so every stored wing's boundary runs are its footprint's rings vertex for vertex and the union of a building's wings is its footprint face exactly (§2.6's check)
Scale (COV-FTG-F09): footprint targets multiplied by the district's buildingScale (0.5–2, continuous; FTG's smaller/bigger as a district edit or an Adjust regeneration)

Heights from the class tables on every wing (floors × storey height + roof rise by pitch; eave and ridge per wing; tower heights for keeps and church towers), with the ground datum baseCm from the terrain by §2.6's deriveBase (FTG-13; J-P19) — carried though the top-down view never shows them

Entrances: the building's entrance set by §2.6's rules — main entrance on the footprint side facing the plot's frontage access edge (§2.6 rule 1, owner's rule item 29), side, rear and yard doors and the basement decision as §2.6 states — re-derived whenever the designation mutates; roof kind by class per wing (style sheet chooses the construction §8.2); materials from MaterialRow (COV-FTG-F20; §2.6); description, opening hours and sub-locations from the class table and naming engine (COV-FTG-F21, FTG-11); yards partitioned into typed parts

The designation mutator (item 18): a change of designation (assign/unassign, setAttr on a plot's use or class, a relocated use §4.11, a dossier re-designation §7.7) never replaces the plot's buildings with a fresh roll; mutate(plot, to) derives the new design from the present one by a recorded delta toward the target template at the plot's current prosperity (item 19 (c))

Mutator step 1 Match: the present design's parts (slots by BuildingSlot.role, wings, storeys, roofs, entrances, yard parts, treatments, a stored composition's or plan's rings, §2.6) matched to the target template's structures by role through a compatibility table (house–hall, storefront–house front, stable–store, workshop–forge … our own rows, editable): each part kept (fits target role within size tolerance), adapted (kept with an attribute change: storey added within floors band, wing extended within budget, frontage treatment or roof kind changed), converted (kept as another role the table allows) or subtracted (no role, no protection); each required structure without a match is added
items.note: compatibility table rows enumerated with "…"

items.statement: Mutator step 2 Order and draws: subtract, convert, adapt, then add, so added parts pack around kept ones on the plot's OBB grid by the compound packer from the plot's siteplan.mutate stream (§6.1: a geometry concern keyed by the plot's lineage — same change from same state draws the same numbers on every host; a New random of the plot changes nothing past); added parts minted from the causing event's seq and ordinal (§6.3), kept parts keep addresses, subtracted parts become tombstones with the event's seq (§2.8); the old house stays recognisable inside the new workshop

Mutator step 3 Land: when the target's size budget exceeds the plot the mutator asks S10b's solver for a JOIN with a neighbour by S10 (7)'s orderings, the neighbour's use relocated by the same solver; when no join is allowed (locked neighbour, hard row) the template's underSize column decides: the compact rows, or a refusal reported with the blocking rule

Mutator step 4 Protection: a locked part or path is never subtracted, converted or adapted (fate kept, §7.3 item 4); a user-edited attribute kept (implicitly pinned, §7.2); an added part that would overlap a kept part placed elsewhere on the plot or reported; the entrance set and basement decision re-derived by §2.6's rules on the result (item 29); the elaboration cache of the plan rung marked stale (item 28)

Mutator step 5 Record and reversal: steps are one MutationRecord persisted in the causing event beside its fates (§7.1, §7.4), cited by the plot's lifecycle event; the event's undo record keeps the former parts; reversing (designation set back, unassign, undo) applies the inverse of the recorded steps when the plot's design is still the record's result (its leaf digest, §6.2), restoring the earlier design exactly; otherwise a fresh forward mutation toward the earlier template runs, reported

Mutator step 6 Timing: a host or user change decides and records the whole mutation at once; across epochs the evolution engine spreads the same steps — occupy if compatible, then adapt, then extend, rebuild only what cannot be adapted — as recorded events (§4.11, item 18 (c)); how a recorded step is shown on the ground over the weeks it takes is §4.11's Works (item 67), which reads the steps and never re-decides them (J-A67.49)

Mutator step 7 One path: generation is the mutation from the empty design (every structure an add, every draw from the plot's siteplan stream), so S11's own batch and a later mutation are one code path (@plat/plots, §14); Regenerate (keep settings) and New random remain re-derivations (§7.1); rebuild (§4.11) is the whole replacement a ruin or redevelopment calls for (item 31's rung 3), never a designation change
type Designation = {cls: BuildingClass; use: string (roster class id); specialisation?: string (template's discrete row; absent: by band); assignment?: Id}

interface MutationStep {op: 'keep'|'adapt'|'convert'|'add'|'subtract'; part: {kind: 'slot'|'wing'|'storey'|'roof'|'entrance'|'yard'|'bound'|'frontage'|'composition'|'plan'; id?; role}; from?; to?; rule: SliceRef (template or compatibility row read, §2.8)}

interface MutationRecord {plot; from: Designation | null (null: generation from empty design); to: Designation; band: {field; manifested}; steps: MutationStep[]; joined?: Id[]; displaced?: {use; to: Id|null}[]; seq: number (causing event; 0 for the generation run)}

interface DesignationMutator {mutate(plot: Id, to: Designation, cause: EditRef | RuleRef | 'generation', ctx: StageContext, k: Kernel): KernelResult<MutationRecord>} — one implementation, registered by name (§4.12, §14); called by S11, by every assign, setAttr and dossier event (§7.7) and by §4.11's use step

Furniture pins (COV-MFCG-I01, COV-FTG-J02, COV-FTG-J05; pin.* streams): the main plaza always gets one centrepiece — statue 0.6, fountain 0.3, market cross 0.1 default weights (MFCG one in every market square, 60 % statues) — offset toward the plaza's longest edge for statues and 30 % of fountains; each gate plaza gets a well, cross or trough with probability 0.5; every block draws one weighted decoration row from a deck applied to its unused plots and vacancy runs (wells, pumps, troughs, large trees); singletons (bandstand, statue, monument) placed once per district in an unused plot by a deck draw; campfires in squalid districts; market stalls (small tents) line each market square's edge band and ring its market hall by rank: principal one per ≈150 m² of square (≤ 40), secondary one per ≈200 m² (≤ 20); a flanking principal market takes the main plaza's centrepiece rule and a secondary market a centrepiece with probability 0.5 (our own rows, calibratable); what each band draws (footprints, yards, treatments, pins, plot outline as optional cadastral layer) is §8.5's

Markets and hidden plots in S11 (items 24, 30): every market square (plaza when principal, a flanking principal market, each secondary claim) takes the pins above by its rank; the market hall's nearMarket row (§10.2) binds it to the principal market by default; a passage the block's reach names is cut by S10 (9) as its passage face and S11 gives the front building the spanning wing; a hidden plot's main entrance faces its access face (court or passage) as §2.6's entrance rules put a set-back building's on the court leading from its gate (item 29), so every plan roots at a door opening onto the way its plot is reached by
items.note: restates §4.6 passage rule

items.statement: Vacant plots under decline (AM-8): a plot whose last building is cleared or reused merges into a garden, orchard or field by plotToGarden, or into its occupied neighbour by amalgamate (§4.11's ladders), through S10 (7)'s merge operator with the neighbour's band; the band's vacancy-run share (S10 (8)) is the design's deliberate vacancy: regrowth never fills a run below its share, and decline's vacancies are counted apart from it
items.note: restates S10 (7)'s plotToGarden/amalgamate

items.statement: Households per building (item 28 (f); J-A28.46): S10b places a residential plot's households — per residential slot (a structure with houses, §10.2) of the plot's template row at least one household and at most the row's households.built, by band ± drift, slots filled in slot-list order, required slots first (capacity cannot be read there: building and wings do not exist before S11)

A residential slot the demand cannot fill is dropped from the site plan, its ground typed yard, never below its structure's least count where the structure is required; a residential plot whose required residential slots cannot all be filled is typed vacant by S10b's reconcile, its households placed on the next candidate (surplus capacity, never an empty residential building); a residential slot on a workplace's or institution's plot that is its main slot (a live-in class's among them) or within a required structure's least count, and that no household of its band or drift can fill, is neither dropped nor typed vacant — the workplace or institution and its use stand — and S11 builds it as a slot without houses, housing none, Building.dwelling absent, reported; BuildingSlot.unhoused (§2.5) records that typing, written by every run of this fill and cleared by the designation mutator
items.note: edge cases defined

items.statement: S11, creating each building and its wings, writes each residential building's Building.households (a building S11 builds for a slot with houses; every other building's list empty) from its slot's households in address order, clamped into [1, capacity], a locked or pinned household kept before the clamp drops any (§7.2; §2.6's capacity rule) — §2.6's one capacity function, the one item 31's relet (§4.11) and F-PLAN's never-omit rule (§5.2) read, evaluated on the wings just made

Overflow pass: a household the clamp leaves, or whose slot S11 builds no residential building for, moves by §10.3's relocation (address and people's keys kept): after the district's last S11 block batch, inside the district's derivation (a pseudo-district's alike), overflow households re-placed in address order by S10b's solver over the district's residential buildings housing fewer than capacity — household's band first, then bands its drift admits; score descending, then building address — each move reported; a household no building of the district has room for is an unplaced item of F-SITING (§5.2), reported with the refusing capacities — except a household that fills the dossier's population (§7.7 item 2), never taken off the manifest: its housing re-provided inside its district (item 20 (e); J-A20.72) by S10b's dossier request in least-disruption order (its first closest option where no plot passes the hard rows, J-A20.42), and S11's operator builds there a residential slot of that plot's template (structure with houses) for it within capacity, in the same derivation or causing event — each build and displacement reported, a hand edit's among its dry-run fates (§7.3 item 4)

wiring.read_by: F-SITING; report; §7.3 dry-run fates; V08 dossier population

items.statement: So the solver and the plan agree on how many households a shell holds and no shell houses more than its capacity; the plan rung records the count among its inputs (§4.1); the overflow pass runs inside every change §2.6's capacity rule lists — S11's operator building or changing a residential shell (an epoch's new faces, a rung-3 re-cut, a designation mutation, item 18) — whenever the result's capacity falls below its households, each move a lifecycle event of it (§2.8), as relet keeps to the capacity (§4.11)

Concealed institutions (item 63): a clandestine institution's building stands on the map like any other and what it is, is withheld; this paragraph is the one statement of how such an institution is resolved, placed and built; records §2.6–§2.7's, knowledge filter §9.2's, underground allocations II.7's

(1) Value and resolution (J-A63.41): institution, use and assignment carry concealment: 'none'|'front'|'hidden'|'underground' (Institution.concealment, Use.concealment §2.7; Assignment.concealment with optional named front Assignment.front §7.7), none by default; resolved when first placed — and again only when a dossier event withdraws the mode the dossier set — from the first source giving one: the dossier's fact (mode, optionally named front); an assignment's value; the class table's default-mode weights BuildingClassRow.concealment (§10.2; rows only for classes our tables mark clandestine — thieves' den, assassins' house, smugglers' store, forbidden cult, black market, spy ring … our own rows) read at the plot band's row and district kind, drawn on siting keyed by the institution's lineage (§6.1; no new concern); else none

wiring.reads_or_produced_by: dossier concealment fact (V08); assignment; class rows

items.statement: Resolved mode stored on the concealed use with its map-side source (Use.concealmentSource, §2.7) when the dossier gave none; a map edit sets a mode the dossier did not set by setAttr (§7.1); one the dossier set is dossier-owned, a map setAttr of it refused (§7.7 items 7, 11; J-A20.77, J-A63.22); a dossier event withdrawing the mode it set re-resolves it by this order from map-side sources, the use re-placed by (2)–(6) as that event's least-disruption mutation (§7.7 items 5, 11 (b)), as an open use where the order yields none (§2.7; J-A63.22)

(2) Feasibility and fallback chain (J-A63.41): underground feasible where an underground allocation exists — II.7.3's sewer-front pseudo-district (S7b (6), needing a navigable run, not only a network, J-A14.43) or an undercity neighbourhood (II.7.5, S7b (7)); hidden where the district holds a plot whose exposure is hidden (item 30, §4.6); front where a cover of the cover table has a plot whose hard rows pass; chain fixed: underground → front → hidden; hidden → front; front → hidden; where none feasible the front's closest options are F-SITING's (§5.2): a clandestine institution never placed openly by a fallback and never dropped; every step down the chain reported with reason in requestedVsBuilt (J-A16.43)

(3) FRONT — one item, two uses (J-A63.42): front is a cover class drawn from RosterTables.covers (§10.2: per concealed class weighted plausible covers per band — tavern, funeral parlour, fencing hall, apothecary, warehouse, bathhouse, tailor … our own rows) on siting keyed by the concealed use's lineage unless the dossier or an assignment names one; a named front honoured where its hard rows pass, else F-SITING's closest options offered — never a silent substitute; S10b places the pair as ONE item (J-A16.41): hard rows the FRONT's; soft rows the true class's relation rows and supply edges plus an exposure row preferring alley, court and hidden plots at the true class's weights; both classes' band rows apply; the building carries two Use records: the FRONT's (Building.use, a working business with households, hours, label, description) and the CONCEALED one (Use.concealment; Use.front names the front's use; listed in Building.concealed, §2.6–§2.7), knownTo secret by default

(4) S11 builds the front (J-A63.42): reads the FRONT's designation template row at the plot's band (class, footprint, site plan, labels, public room programme the front's); the concealed use adds three things only, each flagged concealed and carrying its knowledge: (a) a concealed programme — RoomRuleRow.concealed rows (back rooms, strongroom, cellar room, hidden stair) placed by the plan rung (§2.6, stage 3) away from the main entrance and off the public circulation hub, reached only through a service, yard or concealed door (Room.concealed, §2.6); (b) a concealed entrance (Entrance.concealed, §2.6) — where the plot has an access edge beyond its frontage onto an alley or passage (§2.6 entrance rule 2's condition), deriveEntrances adds one service or yard door there on siteplan.entrance, flagged, never the main door; with no such edge none, programme reached from the front's service side; (c) a way down — the basement decision (§2.6) reads the higher of the front's and concealed class's cellar.prob at the band (terrain gate unchanged), and over an underground element within reach the access lottery takes the concealed class's accessMultiplier (II.7.3 Basement accesses, item 64)

wiring.read_by: V02; V03 plan rung; II.7.3 basement accesses; V04

items.statement: (5) HIDDEN: the institution goes to a plot whose exposure is hidden — the exposure row hard for this mode — with a front drawn by its class row's hiddenWithFront share on siting, or bare (its building of its true class with knownTo 'secret')

(6) UNDERGROUND: the institution joins an underground allocation: a sewer-front dwelling of II.7.3 (U1–U3; the allocation's (b)) or, where one exists, a building of the undercity (II.7.5; its clandestine institutions prefer it), with a front by the same hiddenWithFront share; knownTo secret

(7) Mutation (items 17, 18; J-A63.43): a change of the front's designation (assign, the front use's closing, a rung-3 rebuild) runs S11's mutator on the front: the concealed use persists, its concealed door re-derived with the new entrance set where its access edge survives, its concealed programme re-fitted when the plan rung (marked stale) is next viewed; a relocation of the concealed use (item 17's use step; a dossier event) moves it by S10b's request like any use and leaves the front as an ordinary business: Building.concealed loses it, its concealed door stays as an ordinary service door (flag cleared), concealed rooms return to the front's programme at the next plan re-cut; front and concealed use are two records, either can close without the other

(8) The dossier stays the authority (items 20, 22): the dossier says the institution exists and is clandestine; the map places it and never reveals it on its own; an exposure (raid, discovery) arrives as a dossier change applied as a least-disruption mutation (§7.7): the concealed use may relocate with its mode re-resolved, the front close, a passage be sealed (item 30); a map delete of such a place relocates it by rejectSite (§7.7 item 3), as for any dossier-backed element

(9) Knowledge, not geometry: the building's mass and every public part always on the map (J-A30.83); the concealed use, rooms, door and way down carry the concealed use's knownTo, so §9.2's filter draws them only for a view whose knowledge admits it (the rendering part's refinement of J-A30.83), and every export and the reader withhold them (§11.1, §11.2); the public sees the front's label, description and rows

(10) Emulation (item 23; J-A63.44): no reference has concealment; the non-none weights of the concealment column and the cover table are extension rows scaled by placement.extensionWeight, so parity presets (weight 0) resolve every class to none and place every institution openly; with no clandestine class in the roster nothing runs

Concealment checks: §5.3 check rows — every clandestine institution in an allowed mode or a reported fallback; concealed rooms reached only from a concealed door or the front's service side; the underground mode never without an underground allocation; §13.2's T63 group holds the bars

Light sources (item 68; owner quote on night view with spaced torches or magical lights): S11's furniture step places point lights as LightSource records (§2.7; lighting model and derived lights — lit windows, room lights, light shafts — §8.4's) by the light table's rows, each read against its context: host kind, way class, prosperity value along band rows, era row, the magic circumstance (§4.2 S0) and the arena; a district places lights only on its own faces and own half-corridor strips (laziness contract §4.1)

interface LightRule {host: 'gate'|'bridge'|'plaza'|'market'|'door'|'castle'|'guardPost'|'way'|'shrine'|'pin'|'tunnel'|'gallery'|'chamber'|'accessPoint'; cls? (door rows: class id or tag whose main entrance carries it); wayClass? (way rows); arena: 'ground'|'sky'|'underground'; system? (underground rows: sewer, undercity, catacomb, cavern …); kind (LightSource.kind: torch, lantern, lamp post, brazier, fire pit, campfire, magical orb, shrine lamp …); source: 'fire'|'magic'; heightCm; intensityCd; radiusCm (smooth cutoff of §8.4's falloff); sizeCm (own defaults torch 5, lantern 8, lamp post 10, brazier/fire pit/campfire 25, magical orb 30, shrine lamp 5); colour (sRGB; own defaults fire #FF9329, magic #A6C8FF; §8.2's light roles tint only the vector rung's glyph and glow); flicker (default true for fire, false for magic); count? (per host, default 1); offsetCm? (door rows, own default 60); minLux? ({band; lux}[] way rows, interpolated along the value); era?; magic? (('low'|'high')[]); exposure? (default street, lane, alley, court); extension: boolean}

Light hosts: gate row lights each gate (two torches flanking the passage by default); bridge each end of a built bridge; plaza and market a square's edge at the way rows' spacing and its centrepiece; door rows the main entrance (§2.6) of each building of the row's class; castle its gate and ward; guardPost each post; pin rows every emitting pin (which then carries the light, §2.7); shrine a wayside shrine; underground (arena underground, each row naming its system): tunnel rows each junction of a tunnel run, gallery rows a gallery at the way rows' spacing, chamber rows a chamber's altar, hearth or market, accessPoint rows each access point's foot, door rows the doors of sewer dwellings and undercity buildings (II.7.3, II.7.5, II.7.6); a light's address derives from its host's lineage (door lantern from building and entrance; street light from way strip and ordinal; §2.8, §6.3)

Street lights spaced by what they give (J-A68.41): a way row lights each way of its class whose band row targets a minimum night illuminance E* (interpolated along the value of the plots fronting it); spacing s is the largest at which two neighbouring lights still give E* on the way's centre-line midway: 2·I·h ÷ (h² + (s/2)²)^1.5 × f((s/2) ÷ r) ≥ E* (I intensity, h height, r radius, f §8.4's cutoff), solved by bisection through dmath (§6.5 (3)) — a 25 cd lantern at 3 m and target 0.1 lx give lights about 22 m apart; each district lights its own half-corridor strip at spacing 2s, the strip on the way's left (by chain direction §2.2) from s/2 past the way's first junction and the right-hand strip from 3s/2, so the sides alternate and together meet the target without either district reading the other; a site on a door, gate passage or deck moves to the next; a light that cannot stand is skipped and reported (§5.4)
