How much light — partitioned (J-A68.41): distributed by way class, district and band: the era row sets public-lighting density — sparse in the medieval default (plaza, principal market, gates, through and primary ways of prosperous and rich bands), denser in later eras; magic adds magical rows (none by default under D-3; low: orbs on the rich band's squares and the precinct; high: on every primary way and square); hidden and sealed plots and the courts and doors of a concealed institution's building stay dark unless a row names them; an informal cluster's light is its cooking fires — one fire_pit pin with its light per lights.perStructures (4) structures (item 70); sky rows light an island by its supply (II.6); underground rows light the underground layer by its system

Light draws and presets: each choice reads a rule or table; one thing only is drawn — a door lantern's side of its door — on concern pin.light keyed by the host's lineage and rule row (§6.1); a door light's point lies on its building's footprint ring at its row's offsetCm from the entrance vertex (LightSource.entrance), walked along the ring on the drawn side and rounded to the lattice; §7.4 carries it and §5.3's light row checks it; each record copies its row's sizeCm, colour and flicker flag; a fire light flickers by §8.4 (f)'s pure function of render key and view time, never a draw (J-A68.61, J-A68.42); default rows our own (extension); MFCG preset places no light; FTG preset places one window light per lit building at its main entrance (FTG client's night-light anchor, item 50) and no street light; a user adds, moves or removes a light by §7.1's edits

Lights over time: a light follows its host's lifecycle (§2.8): removed with a demolished host, unlit on an abandoned or decayed one, unlit while its host's Works stands before FINISHED (§4.11); an epoch re-runs these rows on its new and changed faces only

Informal clusters (item 70) (1) Tenure (item 70 (a); J-A70.41): a plot's tenure (§2.5) is derived, never drawn: common for commons, greens and market greens; informal for a plot of the tenure table's bands (RosterTables.tenure §10.2; default squalid and poor) with no standing building but shacks, tents or lean-tos, and for vacant, cleared or ruined ground in a declining district (§4.11); rented for a residential plot whose buildings house more households than their template rows' households.built (let out by rung 1's relet, §4.11); owned otherwise; S10b and S11 write it with the plot — at generation a plot is informal only where (2) gives it the cluster row, "no standing building" read over epochs, never before S11 has built (J-A70.49); every event changing its inputs re-derives it; a setAttr overrides it (edited path, §7.2)

(2) Where (item 70 (d); J-A70.43): the template takes the cluster arrangement at generation for residential plots of the squalid and poor band rows of a shanty-typed district and for every residential plot of a block of such a district that the cluster row's wholeBlock share picks — over epochs for plots (1) makes informal — wherever the district's band range admits squalid (item 72, §4.5 (5)) — never on a plot whose geometry floor is the middle band or above while its stock stands (subdivided inside instead, §2.6 interior ladder, item 28 (f)); FTG's staging is the emulation default; the class mix never draws a cluster structure's class (§10.2; J-A70.49); shanty extramural preference remains a soft extension (J-A27.43); the cluster row's relation rows prefer, softly, riverbanks and marsh margins where S1's shore setback and flood line allow building, and the lee of walls and ruins; over epochs vacant, cleared and ruined plots of a declining district join them (§4.11); undercity chambers take clusters by II.7.5's rows (item 65); II.7.3's sewer-front plots keep "no compound, detached, hovel or tents"

wholeBlock: where the cluster row's wholeBlock share picks a block — at generation a block of a shanty-typed district, over epochs a block whose residential plots (1) makes informal: one draw on the block's plot.join stream at S10 (7), reading the district's kind and block's band and no tenure — S10 (7) joins the block's residential plots into one cluster plot (the owner's "shacks on one block") by its join law over every plot of the block

(3) Packing — paths first, then structures (item 70 (b); J-A70.45): S11 builds a cluster plot in one batch from its siteplan stream, every structure its own door by construction: (i) footpath web: from the midpoint of every access edge a trunk path runs inward square to that edge, ending one structure depth (the largest depthM upper end among the cluster row's kinds, which every later "structure depth" reads) before the opposite side; branch paths leave the trunk on alternate sides every 2 × structure depth + path width, each turned by up to ±20° (drawn), stopping one structure depth inside the boundary; paths are yard parts of kind footpath (§2.5) of width pathWidthM (cluster row's; below an alley's) — plot-internal, never a way or way class, so the plot keeps its access edges and exposure (J-A30.42); (ii) structures lining each path left and right, each fronting it; kind drawn by the cluster row's weights by band × climate × era (tents in the squalid band, camps, newest edge; shacks where the settlement persisted; lean-tos against a standing wall); footprint from the kind's band; a lean-to against a standing wall on its own plot (ruin's, party wall or plot wall; never inside a wall strip; J-A70.47); a clear gap of fireGapM at the settlement's rung between any two structures; packing stops when no site fits or the plot's households are housed; (iii) doors: every structure's main entrance on its path face (§2.6 rule 1 for footpath access, J-A70.44); no basement (cellar 0), one storey, RoofSpec.kind 'tent' for a tent, a lean-to's back wall shared with its host wall; a plot too narrow for a trunk and one structure depth takes the hovel arrangement (reported)

(4) People per structure (item 70 (c); J-A70.46): each structure is a residential slot (houses) whose households.built is the cluster row's households per structure by rung × band (more in larger towns and poorer bands; our own rows); capacity is §2.6's one capacity function (shack, tent, lean-to programmes carry no circulation and the one-room unit: floor area over minimum room); the generation fill houses the households within it, the overflow pass re-homing any excess (never omitting a household, §5.2)

(5) Presets, drawing and time (item 70 (e), (f); J-A70.42): default preset — the cluster row takes the squalid and shanty districts' informal plots; parity presets keep FTG's tents row (1–3 tents) and MFCG's hovel, the cluster packing an extension (item 23); city band draws a cluster as a speckle of small roofs over its paths in the ground tone (§8.5's cluster exception), district band each structure with its entrance tick (§8.2); the naming engine names the cluster once, as a place (§10.4; one label, §9.1), never each structure; accretion, fire and formalisation are §4.11's

Class mix (item 71) (1) A class draw above the template (J-A71.41): when S10b places households of a block's residential plots, each plot's residential class (hovel, cottage, house, row house, town house, manor …, distinct class rows with own templates) comes from RosterTables.classMix (§10.2): one row per band, weights over residential classes, read at the plot's manifested value (J-A19.43) by §4.5's interpolation, an end row applying flat beyond its centre; default rows raise larger classes monotonically through every band (just above the prosperous cut mostly houses with a few manors, rising to the rich row, all manors); J-A19.41 holds within a class

(2) The town's wealth shifts the weights (item 71 (b); J-A71.42): each class's weight × max(0, 1 + wealthShift × (wealthLevel − 0.5)), then renormalised; wealthLevel the intent's (§7.7; with a dossier, the wealth §7.7's derivation table derives); wealthShift the class's column in the mix row (positive for larger classes); cuts stay the town's own, so "rich" is relative while a rich metropolis's prosperous quarter holds more manors than a poor town's

(3) Largest classes on prime frontages (item 71 (c); J-A71.43): per block S10b draws the multiset of classes — one per residential plot at that plot's value, on siting keyed by the plot (§6.1; no new concern), weights clamped into the district's band range — and assigns them largest first (by template size budget, ties by class id) to plots in descending prestige: sum of prestige rows' weights (ClassMixRow.prestige §10.2 — through or primary frontage, a square, park edge, corner, waterfront) over the plot's frontages, ties by plot id; a hard relation row filters first (item 16's rows win); a class whose size budget exceeds its plot asks S10 (7) for a JOIN by its orderings (the reconcile's JOIN at generation), the joined neighbour's draw discarded

(4) Households and buildings (item 71 (d); J-A71.44): households' bands are the roster's (with a dossier, those filling its population, §7.7); the mix decides only which building each takes — any class the mix gives a plot within its band ± drift; a manor that falls to the middle band keeps its shell (item 31's floor, §4.11) and is subdivided inside (item 28 (f)); S2's land estimate reads the mix's expected plot area at each band's centre

(5) Class mix emulation: the mix is our extension; parity presets set it to a step at each cut — one class per band row, the references' banded pools (item 23; T23-1 reads it) — with wealthShift and prestige weights 0

Neighbourhood placement and the band range (item 72): S10b places a class by its distribution (§10.2, §4.5 (3)): dispersed by S7b's allocation over all districts; a district-defining instance's district taking its defining class up to its identity row's targetShare of its placed uses; singular by its own rules; every prosperity-driven read of S10b and S11 (class drawn, template band, new building's condition, occupants' band, mutator adapt/add) clamped into the district's band range (§4.5 (5))
items.note: restates §4.5 (3), (5)

items.statement: A returning dossier element (item 80): among requests after the city is built, a dossier request for an element whose assignment returns to active (§7.7, item 80) ranks first the plot of its former building (the building whose formerUses names its use) ahead of the least-disruption order, so a reopened institution reopens where it stood, repaired by §4.11's Works when the change is dated

Notice posts (item 82; J-A82.41): the furniture step places a notice pin (§2.7) where §10.2's notice rule puts one — at the principal market and each gate plaza by default, at the main entrance of each class tagged notice, and wherever a named-feature claim of the dossier names one (§7.7, item 82)

S7: the trace is S3's and S5a's, fixed before that stage's secondaries grow; S7 builds everything that stands on the traced wall, once per enceinte, after S6 has typed the districts, in one L1 batch per enceinte; its geometry at L3 and L4 built inside the wall strips by S10 and S11 after S9

Wall strips, band, setbacks, intervallum (GEO-38, MFP-9, COV-FTG-G07; J-P29): S7's L1 batch cuts two wall strips off the L1 faces beside the trace; inside: the band's half (wall thickness by era 2–3 m) plus the inner setback (table 6–10 m; MFCG's buildings never touch the wall), bounded by the inner setback line — or, where the era row asks for an intervallum (lane on inner and outer enceintes at CITY and METROPOLIS in the high-medieval preset, none at TOWN), by the intervallum spine, inserted as an L1 lane whose kerb is the strip's edge; outside: the band's half plus the outer setback and glacis (table 10–20 m), bounded by the glacis line — or, where a moat runs along the wall, by the moat's inner bank (strip = band's half plus berm)

wiring.read_by: S8; S10 (0); S5c legality; Wall records §2.7

items.statement: Setback lines carry the structural setback role (§2.2 rule 7), run from gate to gate, stop at each gate's plaza claim or arterial corridor, and close on the secondaries S5c stopped at the setback band, so each strip is a face of its own; strip faces inherit their district from the faces they were cut from and are typed wall_strip; S8 never cuts a strip and its lanes end on the strip's boundary (§4.6); S10's eager step (0) builds inside each strip block the L3 half-band, setback and glacis residue and its side's parts of every tower and gatehouse (§4.7); both faces unbuildable: no plot cut in a strip, so the hard invariant "footprints ∩ (band ⊕ setback) = ∅ on both faces" holds (§5.3); ribbon plots start beyond the outer strip (O8 b)
items.note: unbuildable-strip rule stated in §4.5 S7b (3), §4.6, §4.7 and §4.8

items.statement: Gates — exactly N by construction (MFP-4): main gates are where S4's and S5b's arterials cross the trace (N₁ picked in S3; each outer enceinte's gates its S5b primaries' crossings), so roads leaving each walled stage = its gate count and no arterial ends blind against a wall; water gates where a river passes (bank vertices named by Gate.banks §2.7), at every quay access under a quay_wall or sea_wall waterfront (§4.4), and at a harbour gate (§4.2 S3 (7)); the castle has one town-side gate; posterns a separate road-less count added only on request; N = 0 honoured in S3

Gate plazas (G-R1): a small plaza claimed in S7's L1 batch at each main gate inside the wall, taking the inner strip's setback zone around the arterial (MFCG B14); forecourt squares at churches and temples are typed open spaces sized by the institution's class; gate passages stay open by construction: a wall strip ends at the corridor of the way through each gate, so band and gatehouse parts S10 builds never meet that corridor; the intervallum's corridor is the strip's inner edge; F-WALL's last rung is §5.2's

wiring.read_by: market siting gate squares; §4.7 pins; F-WALL

items.statement: Towers at every trace vertex whose turn exceeds a threshold and along straight runs at a spacing (35–60 m by rung and era; FTG's 39 m median and MFCG's tower-per-vertex the two reference points); kind (round, square, bastion, octagonal) by era row; heights and a ground datum per tower; each tower's footprint built per side of the wall by S10's step (0)
items.note: turn threshold value not stated

items.statement: The castle (MFP-3, COV-FTG-G09, COV-FTG-G10): the S3 bailey reservation becomes the castle's plot; its curtain is its own enceinte of kind bailey along the reservation polygon with towers at its vertices and along its runs; an on_enceinte castle is already welded into the town wall through its two weld vertices

Castle template table: gatehouse at the town-side gate S3 fixed, with an inward spur; keep — rect (by lir), square, octagon, round or cruciform with corner projections, by era and rank rows — opposite the gate, on the highest ground or central, by row; optional inner ward (inset of the bailey by 30–40 % with its own gate, wall chain in S7's L1 batch) by rank; internal paths as path ways keep ↔ gatehouse ↔ wall stairs (S7's L1 batch; keep and gatehouse footprints S11's); surround row (Castle.surround §2.7) — esplanade (MFCG's green spacer, claimed by S7b beyond the bailey's outer strip), a park with perimeter path, a plaza, a cliff skirt on a cliff site, or none; a moat (Castle.moat; carved at S3 when water within reach: ring with gate deck around inside/outside bailey, only outer arc around on_enceinte); for on_enceinte a townSide row 'dry_ditch'|'none' by era and rank (default dry_ditch; J-P36)

A dry ditch types the glacis part of the bailey's town-side outer strip ditch (§4.7 S10 (0); the bailey enceinte's glacis holds it, drawn by §8.2's ditch role; ditch names only this dry residue — a wet moat is a WaterBody named by Enceinte.moat and Castle.moat, §2.7) and is broken at the castle gate by the castle street's corridor, so the street crosses on a causeway; none leaves plain glacis; no castle moat crosses the town wall (§4.2 S3 (10))
items.note: TERM: ditch vs moat distinction

items.statement: Compactness (F-CASTLE): the 0.75 gate (MFCG's threshold on compactness 4πA/P², kept as a shape check) checked when S3 sites the bailey, before the trace welds, and repaired in place first in MFCG 12710731's order — thinness first, then shape (P10; J-A45.41); pinned vertices (an on_enceinte claim's two weld vertices, and once the town-side gate is fixed the two end vertices of the side carrying it) never move; at generation S3 (8) repairs the claim before it fixes the gate on the repaired polygon

Castle repair (1) Bloat: while the claim's nearest boundary vertex lies within castle.minInnerM (castle-table row, 40 m: MFCG's coded 10 units at its 4 m unit) of its area centroid (regularFit's centre §3.4), every free vertex moves radially away from that centre by 5 % of its distance to it (a 5 % scale when nothing is pinned), step by step, stopping at the area band's top; (2) Equalise: each pass moves every free vertex 20 % of the way to its place on the claim's best-fit regular polygon (regularFit §3.4 — as many vertices as the claim, centre the area centroid, radius and phase from the ring's first Fourier component), for at most 20 passes; repaired when compactness reaches 0.75; unrepaired when a pass gains less than 0.001 or passes are spent; a repaired claim checked again against S3 (8)'s hard filter, counts as unrepaired if it fails

Castle repair, ours (J-A45.42): bloat moves only the claim's own vertices inside its reservation (MFCG pushes its committed mesh); an unrepaired claim takes the ladder's next rung — re-site to the next candidate (reported), last a keep without a bailey (reported) — never a restart (§5.2), where MFCG restarts the city; the claim polygon is the target of the warp equalize and bloat edits (MFCG's documented castle-resize workflow; the equalize brush takes the same step, §7.1)

Castle acceptance: castle area and compactness inside the band on ≥ 99 % of seeds with a castle requested (0 ways through reservations; MFCG's census baseline of 178 equalise passes and 11 bloats); every re-sited castle reported

Several enceintes (citadel, inner, outer, suburb, bailey, palisade, earthwork) are stage rows in the table; up to two castles (§4.2 S0); every wall carries a lifecycle for wall → ring road conversion (§4.11's wallToWay, a retypeEdges on the wall's role set)
items.note: enceinte kind list

items.statement: Water furniture — bridges stand on pinned decks: S1's on rivers; S3's on the moats and canals it carves; S5a's on outer moats; a carve edit's on its channel by its way rule (§4.11); one L0 shore-split batch's where no site stood (§4.2 S1 (5)); S7 builds the furniture of every built bridge when a way's span is first laid through its deck — at generation, or by its operator after an epoch or edit — and none for a site: deck perpendicular by construction; class from the way; stone or timber by era and prosperity rows; deck height (deckCm) from the two bank elevations plus a clearance row; minimum spacing 40 m (FTG); fords where the class allows
items.note: decks catalogue restated (see 0060-0064)

items.statement: A deck S1's water operator re-sites keeps its Bridge address (§6.3); bridges and piers are re-based by §2.6's datum step (deriveBase) after a terrain stroke (§7.3 (a))

Harbour (GEO-19, COV-FTG-H17): basin reserved and carved at S3 before any street; S7 builds only its furniture on the reserved shore: a harbour-wall row — shape (none, one arm, two arms; following the coast or projecting) and type (wall, wall with rocks, detached breakwater) — moles, quays as quay ways along the waterfront (bank class quay), piers as pier ways at 12–20 m spacing, straight or branching, on the harbour and open coast (FTG's ≈75 m length reference), timber or stone by era, each pier carrying its deck height like a bridge (read by the shadow pass and 3-D export, §8.4, §11.1); moles, breakwaters, quays and piers are pier/quay ways in S7's L1 batch
A pier, a mole, a breakwater arm rooted on one shore and a detached breakwater are harbour works under §5.3's crossing invariant; MFCG's 1.2 ± t pier casing is a style

Canals and moats were carved with their decks at S3 (canal along the chosen line; MFCG's canal builder, which also draws its rivers, covered by S1), outer moats at S5a; S7 adds their quays, bank classes and the bridges on their decks; a carve requested later by an edit goes through §4.11's conversion path, whose way rule gives every arterial it meets a deck and records every cut, never a silent overwrite

S12a Hinterland siting (eager, no geometry; after S7b, before S8; O14-core; FTG-7): makes the hinterland's content decisions once and writes no plat edge: the field-system preset and parameters, land-use ring radii, outside sites and seeds of the count-driven outside plots, decoration sites (ponds excepted: carved at S3) and the crop rotation, all recorded in the hinterland's Allocation and derivation record; geometry is the hinterland unit's (§4.1) at L3 inside the hinterland's L2 blocks (faces outside the perimeter S6 inserted, with S9's corridors and the headland S10's step (0) laid along the perimeter, on whose inner edge the unit's lines end)

wiring.reads_or_produced_by: S2 demand; S7b hinterland allocation; SiteResources

items.statement: The order is FTG's — decided with the town, drawn after it (item 26; J-A26.41): countryside content is S2's demand, sited after the town's districts are typed and claims cut; geometry drawn after the town's L1 and L2 fabric is complete, into the land the perimeter leaves, concurrently with the districts' pooled stages (no output change; faces disjoint) — so the town never reads the countryside and the countryside reads the whole town
items.note: third statement of the countryside order (restatement)

items.statement: A hinterland re-derivation (§7.3's S12 row) first re-runs step (0) for its headland parts, restricted to its faces, then the unit's S10

The unit's S10 partitions the hinterland blocks under the farm mode by the field-system preset: open-field strips (long narrow faces perpendicular to lanes), enclosed fields (FTG-style; hedgerows a green_line role on their L3 boundaries), or the sector look as a style preset in either of two recorded constructions — VG 1.6.9's (Voronoi cells seeded along the main road, on the shores and on a ring, clipped to the land and either side of that road and bisected at right angles; P17) or MFCG 12710731's variant (a lobed farm belt split recursively into 0.6–1.3 ha fields by square or skewed cuts with 8 m paths, a farmstead on one field in five; P18); the preset works inside the mode's extent; cells become fields in outward order (nearest the settlement's edge first, ties by cell id; VG's greedy claim outward re-derived for a non-point built extent) under the extent rule: demand stops when arable demand met, fill runs over all land the mode gives the fields (J-A57.41)

MFCG variant's split runs in the model down to the furlong-sized field faces and continues at render time to its 0.6–1.3 ha fields and 8 m paths, drawn from each furlong's render.instances stream (strips render-time segmentation; J-I6; J-A57.42); its farmsteads are the farm table's count, as under every preset (J-A57.43)

Land-use rings (gardens/closes/orchards → fields → meadow/pasture/commons → coppice → wild wood); managed woodland and coppice sized by the wood rows and wild wood beyond, as L3 wood faces with forest edges by domain-warped density noise (a render-time property); every land component gets uses (both banks, islands); arterials continue to the frame at their bearings (S4); fields keep the shore setback of §4.2 S1 (8)

Model and render split (SCL-3): model field faces are FTG-sized furlongs (≈2.5 ha; ≈1 600 in CITY's 39 km² margin), each carrying crop, livestock and rotation slot — ≈12 ms at CITY run in the hinterland unit, hidden behind the pool (§12.4); open-field strips inside a furlong are render-time segmentation (count and width a style and era parameter), so the strip look costs no model faces

One farm table (FTG-7; item 26): FarmTable {arableHaPerCapita (era, with provenance), householdsPerFarmstead, fieldHaPerFarmstead, fuelM3PerCapitaYear, timberM3PerCapitaYear, coppiceM3PerHaYear, woodM3PerHaYear, extent: 'fill'|'demand', reserveArable: boolean} is the only source of the countryside's numbers: S2 demands farmsteads = round(arableHaPerCapita·P/fieldHaPerFarmstead) farm plots and their households — under perimeter and rivers the same households housed in the settlement and no farmstead plot — and the hinterland unit's S10 gives each farmstead, or each such household group, its fields at S12a's sites, so farmland per capita and the farm classes' field area agree by construction (MFCG's "not enough farms" removed)
items.note: householdsPerFarmstead: consumer not named in this statement

items.statement: The staged import share (item 88; J-A88.42): when the dossier port fills §10.2's staged hinterland row (PortRows.hinterland; empty in the base), the arable demand arableHaPerCapita·P — and with it farmsteads and fields — is multiplied by max(0, 1 − importPct × farmlandScale), importPct the dossier's share of food imported in [0, 1]: food brought in needs no field, served through the gates' and harbour's import rows (§4.7 S10b); while the row is empty the factor is 1
items.note: farmlandScale default value not stated here

items.statement: Fuel and timber (item 26): coppiceHa = fuelM3PerCapitaYear·P/coppiceM3PerHaYear and managedWoodHa = timberM3PerCapitaYear·P/woodM3PerHaYear (era rows; defaults 1.0 and 0.15 m³ per head per year against yields of 4 and 2 m³/ha/year; own, calibratable), demanded by S2 with the farmsteads; outside classes' produces (grain, fuel, timber …) and supply edges carry them into S2's need propagation (lumber yards and charcoal burners the providers); the unit lays coppice in ring 4 and managed woodland beyond, up to the land the frame's wood propensity offers; what the frame cannot hold is the settlement's import, reported and served through the gates' and harbour's import rows, never a failure (J-A26.42)

Extent (our extension; default fill, the references'): fill — demand fixes the counts and woods follow the landscape, countryside fills the frame; demand — fields and woods sized to demand and the frame's remainder stays wild wood, pasture and waste
items.note: TERM collision: 'fill' is both an extent value and a farm-mode value

items.statement: The arable reserve (reserveArable, default false): when on, S2 records arableReserveHa and S5c prices growth onto fertile ground while the reserve is short (§4.4) — the hinterland kept clear of suburb growth only when demand requires it, only as a tendency
items.note: restates §4.4 (0180)

items.statement: Hinterland test: 100 % of outside-class buildings on outside plots with occupants; farmland per capita ± 20 % of the era row and equal to the farm classes' area; wood area against the fuel and timber rows with the import share reported (bars §13.2)

Farm modes (item 26; provenance ref:FTG farmland modes, keys ours; J-A26.43, J-A26.44): FTG has four farmland settings — three layouts Farmsteads, Around perimeter, Around rivers — and Default picking by size and landscape, climate presets overriding; FarmModeRow {rung; relief: plain|rolling|hilly|mountainous; land: fertile|poor; mode: fill|perimeter|rivers; riverBandM} per rung × landscape — S0's relief class and the fertile share (SiteResources.fertile ≥ 0.4 on at least half the cells: fertile, else poor) — plays Default: fill (FTG Farmsteads: farmsteads whose households live on their land, filling remaining countryside from the perimeter outward, lots larger where land plentiful; each lot a count-driven outside plot with driveway); perimeter (no farmsteads; farm households in the settlement, demanded as households of their band and allocated by S7b with the town's; fields close to the settlement ring by ring outward from the perimeter along the main roads until arable demand met; remaining frame in landscape uses); rivers (as perimeter but fields only within riverBandM, default 300 m, of a river's banks on both banks; no river → reads as perimeter; band short → remaining fields laid as perimeter beyond the band, shortfall reported, never a failure)

wiring.read_by: S2 farm demand; hinterland S10; S7b

items.statement: Farm mode defaults: fill at TOWN and CITY on plain or rolling fertile land, perimeter at METROPOLIS and wherever the land is hilly, mountainous or poor; ClimateTable row's farmLayout rows|perimeter|rivers is FTG's climate override (arid → rivers, cold → perimeter — FTG's Desert and Polar presets; temperate rows leaves the rung × landscape choice); the mode depends only on rung, climate row, S0's relief class and S1's resources, so S2 reads it before it demands farm plots; the hinterland's derivation record carries it; the field-system preset lays fields inside every mode; the village rungs take fill (PART III)

wiring.read_by: S2; hinterland derivation record; PART III; V07

items.statement: Count-driven outside plots (COV-FTG-I03, COV-FTG-B09): the hinterland allocation (S7b) lists the outside classes — farmsteads (under fill), water and wind mills, quarries, mines, lumber yards, charcoal burners, fisheries, lodges — and the decorations; sites seeded by score on SiteResources — the outside classes' relation rows (§10.2), the same rows the placement solver reads: quarries on stone, mines on ore, lumber at the woodland edge, fisheries on the shore, water mills at a reach with fall, windmills on exposed high ground, farmsteads on fertile land near a lane — with a clustering term (a seed's score rises for each seed of its own kind within the cluster radius; FTG's rule); S12a fixes the seeds; the hinterland unit's S10 divides the outside land into exactly that many lots by a weighted Voronoi (power diagram with area targets) clipped to the land; each lot an outside plot (L3 in hinterland blocks) with its yard and a driveway face to the nearest way corridor (VG's lonely houses); edge orchards (S7b (4)) are lots of their allocated area in the first ring beside their district; the unit's S10b places allocated outside classes and, under fill, the farm households

wiring.reads_or_produced_by: S7b hinterland allocation; SiteResources; relation rows

items.note: cluster radius value not stated

items.statement: Crops and livestock (COV-NG-VS27): every field face takes crop and livestock from the era/region crop table (our own rows) under a rotation scheme (three-field by default: winter grain, spring crop, fallow per furlong, each field's slot from its furlong index); pastures take livestock; the lit preset's field textures read these attributes

Hinterland decorations (COV-FTG-I12): decoration table rows {kind, count by rung and biome, placement score, trail: yes/no, keepClearCm} places ponds (small closed outlines from S1's routine, carved at S3), copses (wood faces), stone circles, ruins (outline footprint in the ruined lifecycle state), wayside shrines (one per through-road by default) and boundary stones at the margin crossings — sited by S12a, built by the hinterland unit; a row with trail links its decoration to the nearest way corridor by an L3 path face; fields and woods keep back by keepClearCm; our own rows and counts, calibratable

S12b Greenery (after S11; O19; owner ruling AM-1): a rule family reading the prosperity value, the district kind and the greenery propensity field, never leftover space; the same rule family as coverage and plot granularity: every share a band row of §4.5's band set (a band without a row interpolates, item 27), the value for a plot interpolated along its prosperity value, so greenery blends at quarter edges; rows are defaults with provenance "owner ruling + O19 answers", all calibratable (J-T, §13.7), scaled by the rung's RungProfile.greenery (park area per 1 000 inhabitants ×, the edge-green or orchard probability, the private-green shift; §1.1, AM-4)

S12b writes only inside its own faces (§4.1): its L3 batch lays parks and groves on its own reserved green faces and residue, then its L4 batch types yard-planting parts; avenue and street-tree rows are Greenery entities along its own half-corridor strips (Greenery.along §2.7) that write no plat edge; the hinterland's rows are the hinterland unit's
items.note: restates §4.1

items.statement: Greenery rule table: yard planting by plot class (reads site plan, value; every plot): row → rear kitchen garden (≥ modest) else bare/midden; compound → formal or kitchen garden + orchard part; detached → garden; hovel → bare, pen or midden; cluster → bare ground, paths, a midden (item 70); institution → forecourt/churchyard · formal gardens (value): compound plots, share rising from 0 at the modest band's centre through 0.3 at the prosperous centre to ≥ 0.6 in the rich band → formal_garden yard parts (grid) · parks and ornamental grounds (value, institutions, greens): rich or planned districts 0.4–0.8 ha of park per 1 000 inhabitants of the district, only on S7b reserved faces or residue ≥ 0.3 ha; palace/cathedral close/monastery an ornamental claim of 0.5–2 ha → park, garden faces owned by the institution or commons · avenues (way class, value, planned flag): tier-1 ways (through, primary) bounding or crossing rich or planned districts; prosperous districts with probability 0.5 (the district's greenery stream) → avenue rows at 8–12 m spacing in each qualifying district's own half-corridor strip (a boundary way gets a row on each side whose district's rule fires) · street trees (COV-FTG-I09): secondary streets in prosperous and rich districts with probability 0.3 → one row at 10–14 m in the half-corridor strip of the wider side (by corridor half-width; ties: the side left of the way's direction), planted only by that side's district · edge green or orchard: modest districts touching the perimeter, S7b draws the choice — green/commons claim 0.1–0.3 ha inside the district at its edge, or an orchard 0.2–0.5 ha as a hinterland row in the first ring beside it; green built by district S12b, orchard by the hinterland unit's S10, both owned by the commons · churchyard: every church/temple plot a churchyard part ≥ 30 % of the plot's yard · market green: an unpaved market square (era table) → market_green · castle esplanade (MFP-11): an inside or inner castle, a 20–40 m green spacer between bailey and town · poor quarters: yard planting on ≤ 15 % of plots; a tree by the well (a pin rule at squares and wells) · hinterland ring supply: orchards ring 1, commons ring 3, coppice ring 4 (hinterland unit) · ambient scatter (COV-FTG-I09): pasture, meadow, commons 0.5–2 single trees per ha by biome row, clumped by a cluster process, each unit on its own land-use faces · shoreline band (COV-FTG-I09): round ponds and lakes where the bank is not quay or beach, a 5–15 m tree band, each unit on its own faces · trees at render: every green entity instanced by §8.10's layouts (ranked tile stamp for areas — wood 3–5 m, garden 4–6 m; jittered grid for orchards 6–8 m; jittered line for avenues and street trees at their spacings and hedgerows 8–12 m) keyed by entity and instance ordinal from render.instances/<entity> (§6.1); positions independent of LOD band; crown diameters in metres consistent with building sizes; species from the entity's mix; never stored; overrides are instance events (§7.1)

wiring.read_by: Greenery entities; yard parts; §8.10 trees; §7.1 instance events

items.note: edge-green row restates S7b (4) (0215)

items.statement: greens toggle (MFP-11): on — the park row fires in every band at a floor rate (0.1 ha per 1 000 inhabitants in modest districts, 0.05 in poor) and one park district seeded per 25 000 inhabitants regardless of wealth (MFCG grows park districts independently of wealth); off — parks and park districts not generated, yard planting and every other row unchanged; auto — the feature table (§4.2 S0); the resolved mapping written to the report

items.note: park-district seed: consumer is §4.5 grower seeds ("parks")

items.statement: Park layout (COV-MFCG-I03, COV-MFCG-G03): a park's inside laid by a PartitionRecipe (§4.6): a radial fan of groves with alley-width paths when its compactness is ≥ 0.7, otherwise a semiFan from the vertex at its longest edge (MFCG's rule), plus a perimeter path (FTG's); groves are grove L3 faces and paths L3 path faces (fan gaps and perimeter band), not ways, so S12b never writes L1 after S9; formal gardens use a grid

Species and climate (COV-FTG-I11, COV-FTG-I15): a ClimateTable row per biome (temperate-deciduous, temperate-coniferous, mixed, maritime, arid, cold — biome a circumstance, §7.7) sets the ground-cover role, the tree-species mix with separate inner and outer shares for woods, the default field system and farmLayout, the default roof form and pitch, and the scatter densities; Greenery.species carries each entity's resulting mix, which the crown symbols and orchard kinds read; our own rows

wiring.read_by: Greenery.species; §8 crowns; roof defaults (§2.6); farm modes

items.statement: Greenery acceptance (O19): (a) Spearman(prosperity, private green share) ≥ 0.7 within ± 5 points of the table mean, σ ≤ 8 across seeds; (b) public-green rule satisfaction ≥ 95 % and park/green area per 1 000 inhabitants within its band, reported; (c) 100 % of greenery typed and owned or common, untyped leftover green = 0; (d) tree scatter NN p1 above the canopy threshold and a pair-correlation per class; (e) ≥ 10 000 trees within a 16 ms frame at district LOD (per rung and tier in §12.7); (f) greenery control monotone and continuous (§7.8); (g) city-zoom greenery passes the legibility check and no option coupling drops the layer; restraint at city zoom is §8.5's; the grove tag and VG's dramatic forest kept as options; trees a layer toggle

The owner rule clause by clause (AM-1): trees and greens here and there (poor-quarter tree-by-the-well pin, edge greens, street trees, ambient scatter); parks (park row with per-capita band and the greens toggle); artificial landscapes (formal gardens, orchards, avenues, ornamental grounds: their rows); placed by rules reading prosperity and district type (every row's reads column and interpolated band rows); rich quarters gardens, parks, tree-lined ways; modest a green or orchard at the edge; poor little; yard planting follows plot class; same rule family as coverage and granularity
items.note: traceability summary

items.statement: One more member of the family (AM-10): II.6's island supply law is a band row of this family: supported area and altitude interpolate along the prosperity value between band rows exactly as coverage, granularity and greenery do, read the same field, and are zero below the supporting threshold; its rows are II.6's IslandRule

Gardens over epochs (item 31): yard rows read the plot's manifested band for the yard parts that exist (S11's yard partition is geometry, bounded by §4.11's floor) and the field value for what is planted in them; rung 1's densify … infill builds over the garden part and thin … infill re-gardens it, re-running the yard-planting row for that plot alone (§4.11)

S13 is two parts (§9.1): S13a (model; eager for every district) draws names from the naming concerns only in §6.3's cases (a successor keeps its predecessor's name) — quarters (every node of §4.5's merge tree), districts, ways, landmarks and water, with short forms — builds each labelled thing's LabelEntity with candidate spines and anchors (§9.3), numbers addresses, and writes each district's one-line description from its venue mix, features and prosperity (§10.4; COV-FTG-E10); S13b (view) places labels per zoom stop (§9.1, §9.2; GEO-29), so the first paint is complete and the same for every viewer without any placement entering the model
items.note: restates §4.1's S13a/S13b statement (0016)

items.statement: S14 builds the columnar display list — the city band eagerly for the first paint, finer bands on demand per district, a transient list per drawing export, a DisplayDelta after every edit (§8.1, §8.9, §11.1); S15 is the optional module (§10), never in the one-click path

Names and descriptions from character (items 67, 70, 72): since S13a follows S12c (§4.1), a district's naming and one-line description read its identity and character vector beside its venue mix, features and prosperity (§4.5, §10.4; item 72); an informal cluster takes one place name and one label, never one per structure (§4.7, §10.4; item 70); a building's description reads its Works stage at the drawn week (§4.11 Which week is drawn: the document's week unless the viewer's week key names another) — "being built", "being demolished", "ruined since …" (§4.11, §10.4; item 67)
items.note: restated §4.7 clusters (5) and §10.4

items.statement: The one built path — add a growth stage (GEO-27, LC-12, FTG-4, FTG-14): grow(doc, epochInputs) appends an epoch event to the log and runs at that log position (§7.1, §7.4) on the persisted model with the epoch sub-stream: S2 (delta demand = the suffix of the sequential roster between old and new population, §10.2 — prefix-stable, no survivor's use withdrawn by arithmetic) → S5 for the new stage when a residual remains after the regrowth-first order (S5a boundary grown from the previous one and, if walled, trace and gates; S5b main-road step; S5c with built-face legality; S5d) → S6 (districts extend over new faces, existing districts keep ids; drivers re-evaluated with new circumstances, brush strokes kept as Δ) → S7 (new enceinte's furniture) → S7b (allocation of the delta demand in regrowth-first order — old plan's vacancies, ruins and traces first, new faces only for the residual) → S12a (outside sites for new outside classes; the hinterland unit builds their plots) → S8–S13 on new faces only (S10–S12b in the derivation pool over a copy frozen as §3.3 step 1)

wiring.read_by: epoch event (§7.1, §7.4); V06 evolution engine; §13.2 M4 test

items.statement: S5c's proposals cross water only on a deck — a built bridge or a site the proposal builds (§4.4) — so an epoch's growth uses the crossing sites S1 and S3 left unused
items.note: restatement

items.statement: Built-face legality (GEO-27): in an epoch a growth proposal may not cross a face holding footprints unless it runs along plot boundaries or back lanes (§4.3's existingFabricCost applies to S5c too, pricing a route along plot lines far below one through buildings) or a declared demolish conversion is chosen at its table cost (by building class and age), recorded as events; plots cut by a new corridor are re-cut through the conversion path — buildings that still fit kept, others demolished with lifecycle events — never re-derived from scratch
items.note: demolish table cost values not stated here

items.statement: Survivors — wealth ladder and geometry floor (LC-12; owner 2026-09-26; item 31): surviving plots and buildings keep their built state; a re-evaluated field never re-derives them and never removes an occupied building; it acts only through the explicit, recorded, rate-limited events of the wealth ladder — three rungs by the time a block has spent in its new band and by what its standing stock allows — drawn from …/epoch=e streams (ladder's own draws on epoch.transform; a rung-3 re-cut's plot.* and siteplan concerns keyed by the block's and new plots' lineage with the epoch component, §6.1 — no new concern)

The engine scheduling the ladder is the owner's staged evolution stage (DEF-8); the base carries now the due mark, the table, the operators, the floor and the edit kinds, each usable by hand (§7.1) and undoable (§7.4); with no epoch nothing here runs, so the static baseline is unchanged (item 23): neither reference evolves (MFCG fixes granularity by ward type, FTG by lifestyle tier at generation; FTG's "regenerate area" is a re-roll, which this ladder never is)
items.note: hook: base side + V06 other end

items.statement: The trigger — a band change past the hysteresis marks the block DUE: after S6 re-evaluates the drivers each block's band is read again against FieldBands with hysteresis 0.02: a block whose value crossed a cut by more than it is marked due — Block.due = {band, since, epochs} (§2.5): the band it must meet, the epoch of the crossing, the epochs spent in that band counted up at every later epoch — until its stock meets the band or the band changes again (a new mark; a flicker inside the hysteresis marks nothing); mark per block, memory per plot (builtBand); "the neighbourhood grew poor" is the aggregate of its blocks' marks and plots' records, never a district switch (J-A31.43)

The rungs act through operators the base already has — item 18's designation mutator (mutate §4.7 S11), item 17's use step, item 30's passage choice (§4.6), S10 (7)'s join-and-split law in incremental form (§4.7) — as LadderOp conversion events, so no occupied building is demolished by a band change and nothing re-rolled (J-A31.41)

Rung 1, at every due epoch — use, occupancy, condition. Growing poor: relet raises a building's household count within §2.6's capacity (J-A28.23), the roster's households (with a dossier, those filling its population, §7.7 item 2; item 20 (h)) and item 17's relocation filling them (§10.3); the interior follows the occupants down §2.6's interior ladder (item 28 (f)): the plan rung re-cuts the programme for the new count inside the unchanged wing rings (one household with staff rooms → lodging house → tenement of one-family apartments off a corridor → single rooms) inside the relet event for a stored plan (§7.3 stored-plan row; J-A28.72), otherwise when next clicked (unstored rung stale, §2.8); F-PLAN never drops a household (§5.2); outbuildings convert to dwellings and workshops, sheds and hovels infill the yard (mutate toward the field band's use and specialisation columns; densify … infill inside the manifested band's yard rows); the garden is built over (§4.9); condition steps down Building.condition kept → worn → neglected (§2.6; rendering classes §8.2, never a shape change, item 19); the roof is lost only by the decline ladder's decay after the last household left (vacate; derelict state of §2.8's ladder)

wiring.read_by: relet; V03 interior ladder; §8.2 condition classes

items.statement: Rung 1 growing rich: renovation and extension by mutate's adapt and add steps toward the richer template (item 18); households re-united (relet down to the row's built count; the interior re-cut back up the ladder removes what the subdivision added and restores the earlier plan where nothing else changed, §2.6); infill cleared once its households are re-homed and the garden reclaimed (thin … infill; infill whose households cannot be re-homed within the epoch's churn cap waits); condition restored; use, condition and interior read the field band; geometry reads the manifested band

Rung 2, after the ladder table's duration in the band — tenure and yards: the holding fragments or consolidates without its front changing; growing poor, the yard becomes a back court of rear plots reached by a new passage (densify … back_court) where §4.6's passage choice allows and the manifested band's row carries a rear-plot or hidden share — a middle-floored plot's yard is infilled, not cut into tenements; growing rich, a back court cleared and re-gardened (thin … back_court: uses relocated by the use step, households re-homed — item 17's relocation, or a relet up in a standing shell within capacity — buildings vacated, then rear buildings cleared (clear) and the passage sealed, item 30; a court whose households cannot be re-homed within the churn cap waits); big houses change class keeping shells (mansion → tenement, inn, workshop, chapel) by mutate (item 18)
items.note: restated §4.6 (0289)

items.statement: Rung 2 keeps every frontage and every main shell; its one plot-line change is densify … back_court, which splits the yard off the plot into rear plots and a passage face by S10 (7)'s incremental re-cut — the front plot (the child keeping the frontage anchor) keeps its address and builtBand, every child's lineage continued by §6.3's SPLIT rule (the parent's key with its child index), rear plots taking their new stock's band as builtBand — admitted only as above, never on a middle-floored plot; a court thin has emptied and cleared is vacant, so its rear row returns to the front plot's garden by rung 3's amalgamate (J-A31.40)

Rung 3, on vacancy, ruin, a destructive circumstance event or redevelopment only — the geometry follows: a vacant or ruined plot's ring is re-cut to the band: growing poor, an abandoned or ruined mansion's plot split into row houses or tenements (subdivide), or the fallen house's plot re-cut and rebuilt as lodgings; growing rich, a buyer joins two or three worn small plots and replaces their houses with one large building (amalgamate, then rebuild or build); redevelopment is a composite the engine issues in order — purchase (the plots' uses closed or relocated by the use step under item 17's rules — a dossier-backed use relocated, never closed; a pinned assignment or lock stops it), vacancy (vacate), then the re-cut and new stock — so the invariant holds at every step (J-A31.47)

Rung 3 re-cut is S10 (7)'s law in incremental form: the due block re-cut with its neighbours fixed (§7.3: the block is the effective scope with its seam exception), under the band's granularity target, fusing by S10 (7)'s orderings and splitting by them, every survivor's plot byte-identical, the new plots' buildings by S11's mutator from the empty design, their residential classes by S10b's class mix at the new stock's value (item 71); slums arise where stock was small and cheap, or from rungs 1 and 2 inside big shells; a mansion district grows poor as tenements behind grand fronts, never as a cleared slum (owner quote)

Asymmetry (owner: "much easier for a poor neighborhood to grow rich and merge plots"): rung durations are rows of the ladder table (WealthLadderTable in @plat/tables, §7.6, §14; our own rows, calibratable §13.9; tendencies per region and era, item 23), keyed by direction and by the stock's replaceability — a column of the template rows of the class table (§10.2) read at the plot's builtBand row: immediate (tents, sheds, hovels), short (cottages and poorer-band row houses), long (prosperous-band row and detached houses), ruin_only (manors, halls, institutions) (J-A31.42); default rows — years in the band before rung 2 rich/poor: immediate 0/0, short 0/10, long 10/20, ruin_only 10/30; rung 3 growing rich fusion after purchase and vacancy: immediate in the due epoch, short after 10 years in band, long after 30 years, ruin_only on vacancy, ruin, destructive event or redevelopment only; rung 3 growing poor splitting: every row on vacancy, ruin, destructive event or redevelopment
Every duration in years is read on the weekly clock: the years a block has spent in its band = (the epoch's week − the week of the epoch that marked it, from its EpochRecord) ÷ 52

Churn (J-A31.46; J-A76.44): the table's churn cap rows bound every epoch per kind — geometry (rung-3 re-cuts and rebuilds), fabric (the decline lottery's strikes), use (the use step's relocations) — as a share of a district's plots (or uses) per decade scaled by the epoch's years (a fraction of a year allowed; the scaled cap's fractional part the chance of one more, drawn on epoch.transform keyed by district, kind and epoch; no new concern) and a maximum per block per epoch; defaults 0.05/0.10/0.10 per decade and 2 plots per block (the former "10 % of a district's plots per decade" is the fabric row); candidates beyond a cap wait in address order; item 17's cap and the lottery's bound are rows of this one table

Geometry floor (owner quote on middle-class floor): each plot persists builtBand and builtProsperity — the band and field value its present stock was built for (§2.5; in the model digest §6.2; never recomputed from the field, J-DET-12) — and derives, never stores, geometryFloor = min(builtBand, FieldBands.middle) by the band order (the settlement's middle band for stock built at or above it, the stock's own band below it — a hovel cannot read poorer than a hovel; only replaced upward); the plot's manifested band = max(field band, geometryFloor), manifested value = max(field value, floor value), floor value = middle band's lower cut or builtProsperity when the floor is the built band

Block-level read (S10 (2)'s granularity rows, II.3's dispatch) takes the block's manifested band as max(block band, the floor of its standing plots' area-weighted median): plots ordered by geometryFloor in band order (ties by address), the floor at which their cumulative area first reaches half their total; a plot-level read takes the plot's own (J-A31.43)

Every change other than a rung-3 event reads the manifested band and value for what is BUILT — S10 (2)'s granularity rows, S11's template geometry columns (size budget, structures, storeys, heights, frontage, court and garden; J-A19.43), the yard partition (§4.9), II.3's block dispatch — and the field band and value for who is there and how it fares — households, condition, specialisation, room programme, labels and descriptions (J-P1: "the rich quarter" still a description of the field); the interior has no floor (item 28 (f)) — shell keeps its floor while rooms follow occupants down §2.6's interior ladder to single rooms off a corridor at the poorest; between the rich and the middle manifestation it cycles freely and reversibly through rungs 1 and 2 with no frontage change and no shell falling toward a poorer band (renovation may extend a shell, item 18); the middle band is each settlement's own (J-A31.43)

What writes builtBand (J-A31.44): generation (the plot's band at S10); a rung-3 event, to the band of the new stock (an amalgamate that builds nothing — a thinned rear row or cleared plot returned to its neighbour — keeps the builtBand and builtProsperity of the member whose frontage anchor the joined plot keeps, §6.3 JOIN); rung 2's densify … back_court for the rear plots it creates only; the hand edits of rung 3's kind (rebuild, demolish then build, amalgamate, subdivide, fill, a replace close-up (II.4), a New random of the block); the authorial re-derivations that re-derive the stock (a field brush's or FieldBands setAttr's re-derivation and Adjust, §7.2, §7.4); and a completed upward refurbishment — a mutate whose result meets a higher band's shape template raises builtBand to that band; nothing else lowers it: rungs 1 and 2 never lower a standing plot's builtBand; wealth change over epochs lowers it only through rung 3
items.note: producer list (wiring) for builtBand

items.statement: builtBand lifecycle: Regenerate (keep settings) keeps it (a recorded input, §2.8); a member a split resurrects takes it from the rung-3 event that re-cut it, not from its tombstone (§6.3); a document written before the attribute existed gets builtBand = its plot's DerivationRecord.band and builtProsperity = its recorded sample, exact for every document without an epoch (§7.5 migration); the floor draws no random numbers; with no epoch the manifested band equals the field band everywhere
items.note: lifecycle rows (regenerate, migrate) defined

items.statement: Lineage survives, so the seed survives (J-A31.48): fusion and splitting continue lineage by §6.3's JOIN and SPLIT rule (J-A31.73), so one seed with one history gives one town; an undo returns the former plots exactly from the undo record's rings and records (§7.4); every ladder event is a mutation continuing lineage; only a re-derivation takes fresh lineage (§6.3 succession rule; owner: "It's not new rerolls its modifications and variations to the original seed")

The epoch's order (engine's loop on the base's path): before S2 — rung profile read at the epoch's population target (The rung at an epoch), dials' applied standings and shares move past their hysteresis (The dials' inputs over epochs), TradeFlow re-read from the epoch's trade slice on current geometry (§4.3; item 77); after S2's delta demand: (a) S6 re-evaluates drivers and bands, re-bands every live plot's fieldBand against its own column by §4.5's rule (§2.5; J-A28.29) — before any rung reads the field band, former values in the epoch's undo record — and marks due blocks; (b) the use step (item 17) closes, opens and relocates uses; (c) when the target fell, the roster's suffix leaves in reverse ordinal order — a building whose household count falls but not to zero takes a relet down (unstored plan stale, stored plan re-cut in the event), vacate only when its last household leaves; the decline lottery draws per building, deciding whose households leave first, and strikes fabric by exposure (item 28 (f) with item 8; J-A28.45); (d) the ladder runs its rungs on due blocks under the churn cap; (e) dossier events arriving with the epoch's inputs (EpochInputs.dossier, in host order) applied as mutations at that epoch — S10b's dossier request and S11's mutator (§4.7, §7.7; item 22 (e)), never a re-roll (J-A22.42); (f) siting places the delta in the regrowth-first order from its step (0) — a relet up in a standing shell before reoccupy of a vacant one (J-A28.45); (g) a residual grows a stage (S5); (h) every live placement rejection (§7.7, item 20) re-checked by §7.7's lapse rule (J-A20.74, J-A20.41), the epoch writing lapsedAt inside its touched set; a lapsed site eligible from the next placement on; (i) the character step (item 72): §4.5's S12c on the grown town — character vector, identity (past hysteresis, re-typing a kind its identity row names), band range re-derived, clamped excess added to pressure, a district whose identity changed renamed by §6.3's epoch case — and TradeFlow re-derived on grown geometry; (j) every physical change of (a)–(g) shown on the ground by a Works started inside the epoch's span, and every Works finished more than works.retainWeeks before the epoch's week retired (item 67)

wiring.read_by: epoch event fold §7.4; V06; V08 dossier events

items.statement: Each epoch step's events cite the epoch; the whole is one epoch event's fold (§7.4); a dossier event between epochs is applied at its own log position by the same request and mutator (§7.7); a dated one — between epochs or carried by an epoch — keeps its dossierChange (§7.1, item 75) and starts its Works at the change's week

Regenerate, Adjust and the derivation record: a transformed entity's DerivationRecord is updated; every other plot keeps its record, so Regenerate (keep settings) on an untouched block reproduces it byte for byte; re-deriving it with the new field is the explicit Adjust (authorial); siting across epochs places only delta demand in the regrowth-first order

Test (M4): on a town with walled, ribbon and suburb regimes, adding a stage re-rolls 0 survivors, adds ≥ 1 primary when its gate law asks for one, and replays from the log to the session hash; the ladder's, floor's and epoch order's hook tests are §13.2's (item 31), as are the Works', the clock's and the character step's (items 67, 72, 76)

ConversionOp is defined here once as one union: the base's own kinds (wallToWay {enceinte, widthCm?}; gateToJunction {gate, square?}; outskirtToDistrict {region {ring, key}} — no stored slots §2.2 rule 5; demolish {id}; rebuild {building, cls} — whole replacement a ruin or redevelopment calls for (rung 3), never a designation change; build {plot, cls, footprint?} — as §7.1's build event; carve {kind canal|moat|harbour_basin, polygon}; abandon|decay|ruin|robStone|clear {building} (clear: removed to a footprint trace); plotToGarden {plot}; contractWall {enceinte, trace}) plus LadderOp (item 31), DeclineOp (item 8), UseConversionOp (item 17), TerrainWaterOp (item 25), HiddenOp (item 30 (e)) and the underground's own kinds (item 65: RaiseGrade II.7.6, ClearUndercity II.7.5, declared there); §7.1's convert event carries it; build is §7.1's build event

wiring.read_by: §7.1 convert event; §7.4 undo; V06 engine; V04 (RaiseGrade, ClearUndercity)

items.statement: LadderOp = relet {building, households: rung 1, the household count the roster fills within §2.6's capacity (J-A28.23); stored plan re-cut inside the event, unstored goes stale and re-cut on click, along §2.6's interior ladder} | densify {plot, as: infill (rung 1: sheds, hovels, a workshop in the yard, garden built over) | back_court (rung 2: rear plots reached by a new passage)} | thin {plot, what: infill|back_court — inverse: infill cleared and re-gardened (§4.9) after uses relocate and households re-homed (item 17's relocation or a relet up within capacity) and buildings vacated; back court likewise, passage sealed} | subdivide|amalgamate {plots: rung 3 only, on vacated plots: S10 (7)'s incremental law; §7.1's plot split and join are the hand forms}; each a mutation with an undo record (§7.4), usable by hand (§7.1)

wiring.read_by: §7.1 convert event; §7.4 undo; V06; V09 tools

items.statement: wallToWay(enceinte) = retypeEdges(ChainRef('wall', enceinte), add ('way', the new ring road), remove 'wall'): the wall chain becomes the spine of a primary way with a ring-road width on the same edges; the wall strips' setback and glacis lines removed, strips merge into the faces beside them, band, tower and gatehouse faces cleared with the rest of their finer content; S9's corridorUnion re-derives the ring road's corridor there; towers removed; gates become junctions with a square option

wallToWay clearance (GEO-38): the new corridor needs half its width on each side of the old wall line; where the half-band plus setback on a side is narrower, plots meeting the new corridor are clipped along its edge — a plot keeps its id when its frontage anchor survives (O8 g) — and footprints that no longer fit are demolished with lifecycle events (cause convert:wallToWay)

carve — a canal, moat or basin added by an edit, or an outer moat by S5a (§4.4): the dry run decides every way's fate and the carve's one footprint before any batch runs; S = channel ⊕ its bank setback; every way whose corridor meets S takes a fate by class (J-P30), recorded as lifecycle events with cause convert:carve

Carve fate kept with a pinned deck: every through and primary way, and any other way that is the only connection of the streets on its far side to a gate or the plaza; its deck (S1 (5)'s form, perpendicular to the channel) and its re-route solved in the dry run by §7.3's S4 local operator — between the way's nearest pinned nodes on either side of S, on S3's lattice with existingFabricCost (keeps near its old line), through the deck as a fixed graph edge; a way already meeting the channel within ±10° of its normal keeps its line and only its stretch across the channel changes; the old stretch between the re-route's ends is the way's replaced stretch; S7's rules give the deck its Bridge (events: altered on the way, built on the bridge)

Carve fate cut: every other secondary, lane, alley, cul_de_sac, track and path: its stretch inside the channel ⊕ max(bank setback, 1 m) removed, so every cut end lies ≥ 1 m from the channel, and a remainder that now dangles shorter than one block depth is pruned (events: altered, demolished); quay and pier ways cut the same way and, where they met the new water at ≥ 30°, extended from the cut end to the new bank as a quay or landing

Other crossings (J-I13): a wall trace S crosses has its run (trace between the nearest unaffected towers on either side) re-traced as data in the dry run with a water gate where the channel crosses (as §7.3 (b) 2 re-traces a run a moved river crosses); the run's strip-line stretches alongside it (inner setback line, glacis line or the moat's inner bank which stays, and the intervallum where the era row has one) between the feet of the perpendiculars from the run's two end towers leave with the old run and S7's operator re-cuts them along the re-traced run from those feet (batch (3)); every way the re-traced run's new strips (new run ⊕ (half band + setback, + glacis or berm on the field side)) will meet — other than a kept way through a gate of the run — takes the cut fate at the strip's boundary (as drawWall cuts ways its new strips meet, §5.2, §7.4), and every plot inside the new strips is re-derived with the rest of R; a locked or pinned way, wall or finer entity, or a reservation, inside S or a new strip returns to the dry run as an F-EDIT conflict (lock > drawn geometry; Re-derive from S3 offered for a reservation, §5.2), as for S1's water operator

The footprint (J-P34): C = the set of L1 cells that (a) the channel ⊕ (attractCm + bank setback) meets; (b) border a removed stretch, a pruned remainder or a stretch the new strips' cuts remove; (c) border a kept way's replaced stretch or are crossed by its new route; (d) where the channel crosses a wall, border the old run or the strip-line stretches batch (1) removes with it, or meet the re-traced run ⊕ (half band + setback, + glacis or berm on the field side); R = ⋃ C exactly; R is the carve's one clear region: batches (1) and (2) declare it as KernelTx.clearRegion, step (4) re-derives exactly its cells, the fate report lists exactly the protected entities inside it; locality checks (§3.3 clear-region confirmation, §7.3's carve row, §13.1 and §16 M3a fixtures, the O18 (g)/O2 (c) perturbation test) require byte identity outside it, less the seam exception at its boundary

By (b)–(d) no plot outside R loses its access (a plot's access edge lies on a kerb of a way it fronts) and batch (1) removes no edge a kept face uses (no E_KEPT); inside R S10 gives every plot an access edge by construction (O5 a), and S8's deep-interior rule and F-PLOT's alley rung act as in any block; wall-crossing fixtures are §13.1's and §13.2's

Carve batch (1) L1, clear region R: clearFiner on R's cells; cut stretches, pruned remainders and kept ways' replaced stretches removed, each through its StretchRef (§3.4) — a way cut in two first hands its far part to a new way by retypeEdges' rekey on that part's StretchRef; each kept way's new route inserted whole across the line the channel will take with its deck's two bank vertices placed at the new bank points (deck_end, pinned) and the span carrying structural deck beside way (every kept way one connected chain through every batch); each crossed wall run replaced by its re-traced run with its water gate's two bank vertices carrying ('gate_end', gate, 0|1) under a fresh Gate (§2.2 rule 7), the old run leaving with its strip-line stretches (each through its StretchRef, ends placed by splitThrough at the feet of the end towers' perpendiculars); ways the new strips will meet cut at the strips' boundaries; every other L1 edge the channel's banks will cross that is no way (settlement-perimeter or other district-boundary stretch, a wall strip's setback or glacis line outside a re-traced run) split at its two bank points by splitThrough, each carrying an anchor contact name (§2.2 rule 7: the entity of the edge's first own-level row, smallest free ordinal — from 2 on an enceinte), the stretch between removed through its StretchRef; the map's border line split at its bank points the same way but kept whole across the channel (§3.3 clear regions rule 2; the arena's outer ring is L0); those deck_end, gate_end and contact-name vertices are the carve's prepared vertices; every cut end ≥ 1 m from the channel, so no way is prepared except at its deck

Carve batch (2) L0, clear region R, KernelTx.prepared = the deck_end, gate_end and contact-name vertices of (1) (J-P40): the channel's ring inserted, attracts onto and promotes the prepared vertices, stripping the contact names (§3.3 rule 3, §3.6); each deck span now crosses the water as the Bridge's deck (§2.2 rule 7); no L0 edge crosses the channel, water body stays one L0 face; any other contact with finer geometry is E_LEVEL or E_KEPT and returns to the dry run

Carve batch (3) L1: each kept quay or pier extended from its cut end to the new bank (end a Steiner vertex on the L0 bank line, §2.2 rule 3); S7's operator re-cuts the wall strips' setback, glacis and intervallum lines along each re-traced run from the feet (1) left, closing them on the new banks, and builds its towers and the water gate's Gate record whose banks name its two gate_end vertices (§7.3's S7 row)

Carve step (4) re-derivation of R (J-P43): S6's operator restricted to R's cells after the L0 batch: each land face of R takes the district — or hinterland pseudo-district, or wall_strip typing — of the pre-edit L1 cell that held the larger part of its area (ties by id); a boundary stretch removed under the water lies between its two bank anchors, so the L0 batch re-separates the land on either bank along the remaining boundary and no land face spans it (a canal across the settlement perimeter leaves the land outside it with the hinterland on both banks — 0 district faces outside the perimeter; fixture §13.2); a block part beside a crossed glacis line keeps its own block's typing; the same rule settles a boundary stretch removed on land (a cut way that carried a district boundary) by the larger part; new strips (3) cut are typed wall_strip and take their district as S7's strips do; channel water faces leave the district face sets they were cut from; then S8–S12b re-derive R's cells by tree scoping (§7.3 item 2) — S8 first — with S10's step (0) for R's faces beside a wall trace, the perimeter or a shared reservation boundary

Where a carve batch adds or removes a junction vertex on a spine that bounds R, the far side takes II.1 (3)'s neighbour step or its reversal; those steps and the Seam records of R's districts are the carve's seam exception, the same set a district's reroll has (§7.3 item 1), which the locality oracle computes from the commit records; a carve costs its footprint, not the town

At S5a nothing finer than L1 exists and the channel meets only the arterials through the stage's gates: every way kept with a deck, nothing cut, R clears nothing (§4.4); every touched entity's lifecycle records the event with its cause
items.note: restates §4.4 (0159)

items.statement: A cut way's far part — records that name a way (J-Fpipe-2): when carve batch (1) hands a cut way's far part to a new way by rekey — and S1's water operator likewise (§7.3 (b) 3) — the rekey moves role rows, knot rows and vertex role rows and no record (§3.4), so the same batch re-points every record naming the way by id along the far part to the new way: Frontage.way (§2.5), Bridge.way of a built deck, Gate.way of a gate (§2.7), Greenery.along.way of avenue and street-tree rows (§4.9; §2.7), Junction.arms at its junctions (§2.4), Tunnel.follows of a main beneath (§2.7), and SeamEdge.chain, Portal.wayId, SeamAmendment.spine of Seam records naming it (II.1); those records lie outside R and change only by that id: the carve's identity exception, admitted by the locality oracle beside the seam exception (§7.3 item 1, item 7 (ii)); every such record equals its prior except the new way's id; every other entity outside R byte-identical
items.note: narration: "from Fable's review of 27 September 2026" in heading

items.statement: Which part keeps the old address is §6.3's anchor rule (the part keeping the old anchor, §7.3 (b)); the far part keyed by §6.3's SPLIT rule as a split plot's or tunnel's part is (J-A31.73, J-A11.43), continues lineage and keeps the parent's name and naming record without a draw — a street a canal severs is one street on both banks, so S13a draws nothing and label candidates for the new way built inside the carve's S13a delta (§7.3 item 2); a Frontage's class and lengthCm unchanged; the carve's undo restores the one way and every re-pointed record (§7.4)

Carve far-part test (§13.2, with §13.1's carve fixtures): after a canal that cuts a lane and a secondary, §5.3's reference-integrity row holds on every record that named either way, 0 records outside R differ from their prior other than by the new way id, and both parts of each cut way carry one name

Coherence from one seed (owner): epoch N+1 derived from epoch N's persisted state, the inputs and the seed's epoch sub-stream …/epoch=<n>: same town under different inputs has different histories, under the same inputs the same history; nothing that survives is re-rolled (survivor keeps lineage and derivation record, §6.3, §7.3)

The evolution engine is the owner's later stage (DEF-8); its hooks are concrete now: the owner's history (growth, regression, growth again: houses emptied and robbed for stone, plots turned to gardens, a shorter wall ring inside the old one, ruins left standing) expressed with the base's records: the transformation and conversion kinds (abandon, decay, ruin, robStone, plotToGarden, contractWall, LadderOp, DeclineOp), which a user can also apply by hand (§7.1); the lifecycle history on every entity; the epoch streams; the circumstances timeline (§7.7); the sequential roster (a population fall selects its suffix in reverse ordinal order; the decline table's exposure lottery chooses which buildings empty); a ruined building keeps its footprint and heights and draws with the ruin program and the none roof kind (§2.6, §8.2); when and where the engine applies these kinds is its own rule table over …/epoch=e streams
items.note: hook with V06 other end

items.statement: interface EpochInputs {week?: number (item 76: absolute week at the epoch — a dossier-bound map's is SettlementForge's calendar.elapsedWeeks; absent on a standalone call, then previous week + round(52 × years)); years: number (derived from weeks: (week − previous epoch's week, or the creation week) ÷ 52, a fraction allowed); populationTarget: number; circumstances: CircumstanceSlice (§7.7 layer 2); events: {kind; params: Record<string, number>}[]; dossier?: EditEvent[] (host's dossier events, author 'host', EditBase.dossier set, in host order, applied at step (e) (§7.7 item 6); each keeps its EditBase.dossierChange (§7.1, item 75))}
items.note: events[].kind — no enumeration of kinds in the base

items.statement: interface EvolutionStrategy {plan(doc: Document, inputs: EpochInputs, tables: TableView, rng: Stream): KernelResult<(ConversionOp | EditEvent)[]>} registered by name (§4.12); base registration 'grow-by-stage' — the path above; the owner-staged engine registers its own strategy and reuses every event kind

wiring.read_by: V06 engine registers its own; §14 registry

items.statement: The base builds and tests exactly one path — add a growth stage to an existing town — at M4 (G-P13), because it is the same path "regenerate this area" uses

The clock — weeks (item 76, with item 67's Works; owner: "our simulator advances by units of one week"): "our simulator" is the clock that changes the map's inputs — the host's (SettlementForge's) or the staged evolution engine's — never @plat/sim's time view key, which changes nothing (§10.3; J-A76.41)
items.note: TERM: the clock vs the sim time view key

items.statement: (1) The week: the map's time is an integer week; for a dossier-bound map SettlementForge's calendar.elapsedWeeks (no conversion; never elapsedMonths, never history.age); creation week the port's HostContext.week (§14) or 0; a standalone map starts at week 0; EpochInputs.week the absolute week at the epoch, years derived from it; a standalone grow call giving years only takes the previous week + round(52 × years) and re-derives years from whole weeks (one clock); a dossier event carries its week in dossierChange.week (§7.1, item 75); the document's current week is derived — the week of the last folded event carrying one — never a stored counter (§2.9); each epoch's week is its EpochRecord's

wiring.reads_or_produced_by: calendar.elapsedWeeks (SF dossier via port V08); HostContext.week (§14)
wiring.read_by: Works; season; ladder durations; V08; V06

items.statement: (2) Dating a dossier change: the port (§14) dates each change it finds by the first rung giving a week: an explicit tick on the change's receipt (foundedAt.tick; lifecycle institutionHistory[].tick; populationHistory[].tick; activeConditions[].triggeredAt.tick; campaign-era historicalEvents[].tick; decrees[].tickRef; calamityHistory[].tick; previousGovernments[].tick; a news tick; the provenance ledger's tick), then the week suffix of the change's outcome id, then HostContext.week, then none: a change with no week applies finished with no Works (§7.7 item 1 reads these rungs; the port counts an undated change in its report)
items.note: DOSSIER wiring: names ten dossier tick fields consumed by the port

items.statement: (3) The season — one calendar (J-A76.42): CalendarRow gives the week of the year (week mod 52) + 1 and its season: a dossier-bound map reads row sf445 (52 weeks; four seasons of 13 weeks from spring; month ends at weeks 4, 8, 13, 17, 21, 26, 30, 34, 39, 43, 47, 52), a standalone map our own default row shaped alike (month ends 4, 9, 13, 17, 22, 26, 30, 35, 39, 43, 48, 52); Works' pauses, §8.2's season rows for a campaign week and the module read it; no second calendar exists (tables/dossier/calendar, §14)

(4) The cadence: the port folds a dossier's discrete changes as standalone dossier events at their weeks, in SettlementForge's order (decrees first), and an epoch at each 52-week boundary crossed — or sooner, when the dossier's population has moved from the last epoch's populationTarget by more than the roster tolerance ± 5 % (J-A76.43; the one number §7.7 item 3's lapse reads too) — carrying the target, circumstance slices, event kinds and that week's dossier events in EpochInputs.dossier; a catch-up batch follows the same rule, gaps allowed; no epoch folded per tick (Works stages derived from the week at any drawing); a standalone map's epochs are its circumstance timeline's (§7.7, dated in weeks) or a user's grow calls

(5) Rates per year (J-A76.45): every chance stated per unit of time is per year, applied over an epoch's span as 1 − (1 − p)^years through dmath (§6.5 (3)); dwell bands and ladder durations in years read as weeks ÷ 52; churn caps scale by years — so epochs a few weeks apart and one a decade long change the town at the same rate; II.6's island slots follow the same rule
items.note: one pattern for per-year chances

items.statement: interface CalendarRow {id: 'sf445' (dossier's) | 'plat-default' (ours); weeksPerYear: 52; seasons: {season: spring|summer|autumn|winter; fromWeek (week of year, 1-based)}[]; monthEnds: number[] (twelve week-of-year ends)}

The rung at an epoch (item 81 (b); J-A81.41): at each epoch the rung profile is read at the epoch's populationTarget (§1.1's ladder): a crossing of one of §1.1's bands changes the rung's row — its granularity, greenery, layer and budget rows — for everything the epoch builds from then on; standing fabric survives exactly as it survives a growth stage (§6.3)

wiring.read_by: S10 granularity; S12b; II.6 island gate; V06
