items.statement: Frame growth at an epoch (J-A81.31): a crossing upward whose town the frame no longer holds grows the frame to the one §3.2 (9) gives the new target: S1 derives terrain, water and the hinterland's ground on the ring between the old margin and its successor (same terrain field continued; each water body continued across the old margin with inner reaches fixed); the kernel grows the frame by §3.2 (9)'s single-level batches over one clear region — an L1 batch clearing finer content of whole L1 faces beside a lapsing stretch of the old chains or under the new rectangle, an L0 batch replacing the margin chain, an L1 batch replacing the border chain — each raster growing by whole cells, every stored height unchanged, flow fields recomputed over the grown grid; then S4 continues every through-road from its old end to the new margin, S12a sites the hinterland on the ring; the stages owning the cleared faces re-derive them (hinterland unit for the hinterland's; a district's S8–S12b for a district's; on each underground part §3.2 (9) grows, that part's stages for its cleared faces — part 0's network stage its bands by corridorUnion (II.7.2), II.7.3's stage its plots, each other system's stage (catacomb, cavern, quarry, vaults) its own part's bands (II.7.6), II.7.5's stage the undercity's plots; on the buried and dug parts, which no stage re-derives at an epoch, their cleared bands re-laid from kept gallery chains by corridorUnion (§3.7), drawing nothing); every face outside the region, off a deleted stretch and off the ring keeps its ring, owner and nested faces; the frame never shrinks (a declining town keeps its frame and hinterland)

wiring.read_by: S1, S4, S12a; underground stages (V04); V06

items.note: long combined edge rule

items.statement: II.6's island gate is one reader of the rung; a dossier outside the ladder — below 1 500, or above the 120 000 cap — is refused by the port (§7.7 item 15, item 81; §1.1; J-A81.01) and never reaches an epoch, so §3.2 (9)'s clamp of the frame's target at the cap serves only growth that carries no dossier
items.note: edge: population outside ladder defined

items.statement: The dials' inputs over epochs (items 72, 78, 79): at each epoch, before S6 re-evaluates the drivers, a power's applied standing (PowerStanding.appliedStanding, §7.7 layer 2) moves to the epoch's standing, and a sector's applied share to the epoch's share, only when they differ by more than dial.hysteresis (0.05, a dial-table row); both are folds over the epochs' slices in log order, so a replay reproduces them and §4.5 (6)'s dials follow the dossier's powers and economy without flickering

Uses across epochs (item 17): a use (shop, workshop, inn, institution) is its own record (Use, §2.7), separate from the buildings that house it: a building references its current use or none (vacant) and keeps formerUses, so a use can close in one building and open in another while the building persists; the base builds the hand path: openUse on a vacant plot or building (the building mutates to the designation by §4.7 S11's operator), closeUse (building stays vacant — first state of the decline hooks — or converts to a named designation), relocateUse (a closeUse here and an openUse there under one event, detail.from and to on the use's lifecycle event §2.8; swapUse is two relocations) and mutate (§4.7 S11) — each with its undo record (§7.4) and reported to a host (§11.3)

The staged engine's use step runs at each epoch after the roster's delta demand and before siting, as the same events: (1) re-score — for every use §4.7 S10b's solver scores its present plot and the best alternative within its catchment (the district and neighbours, serviceRadiusM of §10.2's useRules) against the current field, distribution and supply graph; (2) inertia — a use moves only when the alternative beats the present plot by more than the row's inertia and the row's moveChance draw falls (use.relocate concern on the use's …/epoch=e stream, §6.1); closes only when its catchment's demand (households within its radius against the roster's ratio) has been below closeShare for closeAfterEpochs, or a hard supply edge had no provider in reach for starveAfterEpochs; a dossier-backed use never closes by this rule; new demand opens uses where the solver scores best; (3) cap — at most the churn cap's share of a district's uses relocates per epoch; (4) assignments — a host or owner assignment moves with its use unless pinned (§7.7, item 20 (g)), then it stays and the town adapts; every change reported; (5) traces — a vacated building keeps its former use in formerUses, which a later opening prefers (former inn reopens as an inn first; a dossier element whose assignment returns to active reopens in its former building first, repaired by a Works when dated — item 80) and the naming engine may read (§10.4); (6) concealed uses relocate by these rules like any use, front stays an ordinary business; uses visited in address order; households and postings follow (§10.3)

The epoch-spread mutation (item 18 (c)): across epochs a designation change is issued as a sequence of mutate events over the ladder's rung durations (item 31) — first occupy when the present design is compatible (every kept part, nothing added), then adapt, then extend (the adds), and rebuild only parts that cannot be adapted — same steps and draws spread in time; each event decides and records its step at once (§4.7 S11 step 6) and a Works shows it over the weeks it takes (J-A67.49); the model never changes between events
items.note: restates mutator step 6 (0352)

items.statement: Dossier content across epochs (item 20; J-A20.75, J-A20.43): no step of an epoch closes a dossier-backed use (assignment existence 'dossier', §7.7 item 2) or leaves one without a building; only a dossier event at step (e) removes, adds or re-designates one; the use step never closes one: where its catchment or supply fails the use relocates to (1)'s best alternative by the solver's dossier request (first closest option where no plot passes the hard rows, J-A20.71) or, where its catchment holds no candidate plot, stays in its building; its moves by (2)'s inertia rule are any use's

Before any other step would empty or remove the building housing an unpinned dossier-backed use — a redevelopment's purchase, step (c)'s vacate, the decline lottery's strike, the growth step's declared demolish or corridor re-cut, a carve, wallToWay's clearance, contractWall, a terrain-and-water repair, fallIsland, a tunnel's closing (II.7.3) or a passage's sealing — the use is first relocated the same way inside the epoch, a relocateUse citing the epoch and counted outside the use cap, the request's scope its catchment less the plots that step empties or removes, widened to the town where that scope holds no candidate plot; a pinned one keeps its building, which the step treats as any pinned entity (§7.2); so the dossier element is live and placed at every step (§5.3's row); a dossier-listed ruin (Assignment.state ruined, §7.7, item 80) is present as its ruin — its use closed, its building ruined — and no step repairs or clears it but a dossier event; a reopening returns its use to its former building first
items.note: enumerated list of removing steps (edge coverage)

items.statement: UseConversionOp = openUse {plot, to: Designation, building?, assignment?} | closeUse {use, leave: vacant|convert, to?: Designation} | relocateUse {use, to (destination plot: a closeUse here and an openUse there under one event)} | mutate {plot, to: Designation, spread?: now|epochs (§4.7 S11's operator; epochs issues steps over the ladder's durations)}; joins ConversionOp
items.note: swapUse named in prose (two relocations) but not a union member

items.statement: Decline and regrowth (owner 2026-09-25; AM-8): regression is growth read the other way: the population target falls, the roster's manifest shrinks by its suffix (§10.2), the fabric the suffix leaves steps down a ladder of states over epochs — never re-rolled, never removed by arithmetic — until regrowth reoccupies it; steps scheduled by the owner's staged engine (DEF-8); the base carries now, stated once: ladders, decline table with exposure function, salvage ledger, lag rule, regrowth-first siting order (binds the built grow-by-stage path today) and conversion kinds, each applicable by hand (§7.1) and undoable (§7.4); states §2.8's, style classes §8.2's; §6.3 identity rules, §13.2 hook tests, §16 price at M4

The ladders (§2.8 Existence in brackets; every step one conversion, a lifecycle event with its cause): Buildings — occupied → vacant (abandoned: use left, fabric stands) → derelict (decayed: roofless, RoofSpec.kind 'none') → ruin (ruined: walls part-standing, the ruin program) → robbed or cleared (cleared: a footprint trace, material in the ledger) → reused (reused: the trace drawn as the garden, orchard or field it became — Building.reusedAs §2.6 — or a successor building on the old foundations taking the trace's address, §6.3); upward steps at every rung (reoccupy, repair, rebuild, reuse), regrowth uses them first · Walls and gates — in use → neglected (abandoned) → breached or partly dismantled (decayed; gap a StretchRef) → superseded by a shorter inner ring: contractWall traces and builds the new ring inside the old one through S5a's trace step and S7's operator, old ring's record live with Enceinte.supersededBy naming the new one, its line a trace — or becomes the ring road by wallToWay · Tunnels (II.6's condition table) and the underground's galleries and chambers at the same persistence rate (II.7.5, II.7.6; item 65): in use → neglected, silted (abandoned) → partly caved in (decayed) → collapsed or sealed (ruined; Tunnel.closure), never demolished by the engine · Islands (II.6): floating → waning → settled → fallen · Plots — a plot whose last building is cleared or reused merges into a garden, orchard or field (plotToGarden) or its occupied neighbour (amalgamate; §4.7 S10), the plan coarsening where people are few; fields their own layer: a struck farmstead's fields stay worked, LandUse.owner passing to the nearest farmstead or the commons
items.note: "II.6's condition table" for tunnels — tunnels are II.6/II.7 hooks

items.statement: Decline table (DeclineTable in @plat/tables: editable, versioned rule table with provenance, §7.6; our own rows, calibratable §13.9; rows are tendencies — weights and chance, no fixed order, AM-23): persistence rate per fabric layer use 1.0 · building 0.6 · plotBoundary 0.3 · street 0.08 · wall 0.05 · underground 0.03 · terrainWater 0.005; exposure drivers — kernels over the context vector (§2.5) with weights, §4.5's construction: extramural + ; terrainClass low, damp or flood + ; downwind + ; near noxious kernels of field pass 2 + ; intramural periphery (dist.wall small inside the enceinte, dist.centre and dist.market large) + ; low prosperity + ; resilient core (dist.market and dist.plaza small; attractors at churches, precinct, castle) −; chance share 0.25 of the exposure field (prosperity field's 0.15); dwell bands (years; each drawn once as its step's decay Works duration) vacant → derelict [10, 30]; derelict → ruin [20, 60]; ruin → cleared on salvage demand only; walls one band slower, tunnels two; haul radius 250 m; exemptions: a locked or pinned entity never struck; an assigned entity only through the use-relocation rule (AM-17); the building of a dossier-backed use only after that use is relocated

wiring.read_by: strike lottery; Works decay durations; salvage; V06

items.statement: Strike lottery (the engine's step; the exposure function and table are the base's): for an epoch whose target lies below the manifest, the suffix leaves in reverse ordinal order as step (c) states (relet down while households remain, vacate at the last household; J-A28.45); which standing fabric steps down is drawn without replacement from a lottery over candidates whose dwell band has run (for a building, whose decay Works has run its span; J-A67.46) with weight w = E(x)·rate(layer)·u: E(x) = clamp(Σ_j v_j·kernel_j(x) + ε_E(x), 0, 1) the exposure field computed per epoch on §4.5's 32 m cells from current context vectors and prosperity field with its chance share; rate the layer's persistence row; u a draw from epoch.transform keyed by entity lineage and epoch (§6.1; no new concern); bounded by the churn cap per district per epoch; a weighted tendency, not a law (J-A8.41)

Salvage — the material ledger: robStone, clear, dismantle and demolish credit the town's MaterialLedger (§2.7) by the building's class-table yield (salvageM3 per material, §10.2); build, rebuild, reuse … build and a repair (reoccupy from derelict) debit it by the new class's row from sources within the haul radius; a flow record, never a hard constraint: a debit it cannot cover is built anyway and the shortfall reported (J-A8.45); the lottery's weight for robStone and clear is multiplied by the salvage demand within the haul radius (standing debits of planned building, repairs and a new stage's footprints), so cleared zones appear beside active building and a ruin beyond any demand is left standing

Lag and memory: built extent follows population with a lag on the way down and none on the way up: a fall's households leave at once (step (c)) and standing stock decays by the dwell bands over later epochs; a rise met in the epoch it arrives by the regrowth-first order without a dwell (J-A8.47); memory is the persistence order itself: plot, street, wall lines and traces outlast buildings, so the old plan is there for regrowth to refill

Regrowth-first — built now on the one path: in grow-by-stage S2's delta demand placed in this order, only the residual grows a stage: (0) standing shells whose household count fell below what their occupants' band row houses relet up within §2.6's capacity (relet; J-A28.45); (1) vacant buildings reoccupied (reoccupy); (2) derelict ones repaired (reoccupy, ledger debit); (3) ruins and cleared traces rebuilt or reused on their foundations (rebuild, reuse … build); (4) vacant plots of the old plan beyond the band's vacancy-run share (S10 (8) keeps the share; design's own runs never filled below it); (5) plots S10 cuts on faces the old plan left unbuilt along its street lines inside the last boundary; (6) new faces of a new stage — where Features.sewers is on, the underground crowding hook first sends crowdingShare of the residual's poorest-band households underground (II.7.3 (c), II.7.4, §4.5 S7b (6)); S5a grows the boundary for the residual only; an epoch whose residual ≤ 0 grows no stage and adds no face; S7b allocates the delta first to (0)–(5) as each district's old-plan capacity, only the remainder to new faces (replacing the rule that an epoch placed delta only on new or transformed plots; J-A8.44)
items.note: narration: "this replaces the rule that…"

items.statement: Regrowth-first test: §13.2's T8-2 (M4)

The prosperity field under decline: drivers re-evaluated per epoch (§4.5); under decline the market, harbour and main-street kernels shrink with their activity (§7.7's circumstance slice), and where plots merge the density field falls, so the field contracts toward the survivors' core and may concentrate there — the ladder's amalgamations its footprint on the plan
items.note: restates §4.5 LC-12 (0206)

items.statement: Islands and the underground over epochs (laws II.6's): each epoch re-reads the rung from its population target and re-evaluates II.6's supply law: an island whose supported area shrinks past the hysteresis is resized (rim plots cleared with lifecycle events, cause convert:resizeIsland); one whose supply falls to zero — or whose settlement has left the CITY band (AM-13) — wanes, settles after its dwell band and falls: fallIsland archives its arena and lays a ruin decoration face (§2.7) over its projected outline on the ground through the carve path's clear-region protocol, every entity under it demolished with that cause; regrowth re-floats a settled island before it raises a new one (J-A10.42); a tunnel silts, caves in and is sealed by the same lottery at the underground's rate, never demolished by the engine (J-A11.41), reopened before a new one is dug

Identity and determinism (decline): a vacant, derelict, ruined, cleared or reused building is a live record with its address and lineage (§6.3); it becomes a tombstone only by demolish or when a reuse … build successor takes its address (supersede, §2.8) (J-A8.42); every draw comes from epoch.transform or, for islands, island.place, keyed by lineage and epoch, so same seed + same timeline → same history of decline and regrowth (§6.2, §7.7)
Emulation note: neither reference has time; with no epoch the static baseline is unchanged byte for byte (§13.3's goldens), every rate a table value (AM-23)
items.note: restated several times in §4.11 (Survivors, Works (10), terrain note)

items.statement: DeclineOp = vacate|reoccupy {building} (occupied ⇄ vacant; reoccupy from derelict a repair: roof restored, ledger debited) | reuse {building, as: garden|orchard|field | {build: BuildingClass}} (Building.reusedAs or a successor on old foundations, Building.predecessor §2.6) | neglect|breach|dismantle {enceinte, stretch?} (old line persists as a trace; contractWall and wallToWay supersede a ring) | silt|caveIn|seal|reopen|flood {element: tunnel, gallery or chamber (II.6's condition table); flood only on a gallery or chamber whose floor lies below the water table; stretch?} (a stretch splits the record first; no engine plan contains demolish on a tunnel; J-A65.48) | resizeIsland {island, areaHa, elevationCm} (outline re-drawn by §4.2's routine from the island's own stream; rim plots cleared or new rim faces grown by the grow path on the island's arena) | settleIsland|fallIsland|refloatIsland {island} (waning → settled (elevation at the floor of its band, districts declined) → fallen (arena archived, ruin face on the ground); a settled island re-floats first) | raiseIsland {allocation} (regrowth: a new island for a sky allocation the count law opened, placed by SkyStrategy, II.6)

Terrain and water change slowly (item 25; engine owner-staged, kinds and hand path the base's): reclamation, silting and river-course shifts are conversions on the one list, the slowest layer of the persistence order, never immutable, applied by hand through §7.1's convert event and in the staged engine drawn at the decline table's terrainWater rate by their own trigger rows; each a typed operation whose repair is an operator the base already has (J-A25.41)

TerrainWaterOp = reclaim {kind: marsh|foreshore, region} (marsh: LandUse faces of kind marsh or a damp or flood band re-typed as land; foreshore: a shallow water margin filled) | siltReach {water, stretch?} (width and depth profiles fall by the row's share; a basin below the harbour's draught loses its harbour use) | shiftCourse {water, from, to} (control-knot ordinals §2.3; the reach between re-traced — a meander cut-off or avulsion) | digCanal {polygon} (the carve, kind canal)

Terrain/water repair: reclaim runs S1's terrain operator (§7.3 (a)) — region raised to the flood line plus the row's margin (reclaim.raiseCm 60), drained by a ditch water body and its LandUse faces re-typed with reclaimed set, as §2.3 states — and for a foreshore S1's water operator (§7.3 (b)) with the filled margin as new shore; siltReach and shiftCourse are S1's water operator on the changed reach (width and depth profiles, shores as buffer, crossings re-sited, kept ways re-routed, F-RIVER's re-trace confined to the reach, §7.3 (b) 1–2), so their footprint, fates and locality are the carve's and byte identity holds outside it; digCanal is carve; every touched entity's lifecycle records the cause (convert:reclaim …); record changes are §2.3's

Terrain/water trigger rows (the engine's step; rows the decline table's terrainWater rows, §7.6): candidates and chance per year — applied over the epoch's span as 1 − (1 − p)^years (J-A76.45) — each × the layer's persistence rate (0.005), drawn from epoch.transform keyed by the water body's or face's lineage and epoch (§6.1; J-A25.42): siltReach — a reach whose accumulation has fallen or a basin whose harbour use closed, 0.02/yr; reclaim — a marsh or foreshore face beside built land whose band's plot demand is short (S5d's shortfall record) and whose district's band is modest or above, 0.03/yr; shiftCourse — a reach whose sinuosity exceeds river.cutoffSinuosity (1.8) or whose flood cells beside it exceed the row's share, 0.01/yr; digCanal only by demand (a canal row of the roster's institutions, a dossier element or a user's edit); each fires at most once per body per epoch; AM-23 tendency; emulation: neither reference has time; MFCG's warp and FTG's water drawing kept as §7.1's edits; nothing runs without an epoch
items.note: BROKEN REF: "(The clock, below)" at l.6614 — The clock is above (l.6369)

items.statement: Hidden plots over epochs (item 30 (e)): a passage can be sealed — sealPassage sets Passage.sealed (§2.5), so the access edges on its face read as sealed; every plot whose only reach passes it takes exposure sealed (§4.6) and its buildings enter the decline ladder as vacant (vacate, cause convert:sealPassage) — and later reopened (openPassage: exposure returns to hidden, buildings reoccupy by the regrowth-first order); both hand edits in the base and the engine's kinds later; hidden plots arise by densification (densify … back_court, rung 2) and vanish by thin … back_court (item 31)
items.note: restates §4.6 back courts (0289) and rung 2

items.statement: HiddenOp = {op: sealPassage | openPassage; passage: Id (the L3 passage face, §2.5)}; the last kinds of this section the union admits (… | TerrainWaterOp | HiddenOp)
items.note: "last kinds" but RaiseGrade and ClearUndercity also join the union (declared in II.7) — wording tension, see conflicts

items.statement: Works (1) decided at once, shown over weeks (item 67; J-A67.41): every physical change (build, extension, demolition, repair, conversion, decay step, clearance) is decided and recorded by the event that makes it (mutator record, conversion, ladder or decline op; §4.7 S11 step 6, J-A67.49), so the log alone determines the model; when that event carries a week (an epoch, a dated dossier change §7.7 item 1, a hand edit scheduled by startWorks §7.1) and works.enabled holds, the event also creates a Works record (§2.7): kind, target (a building, whose added or subtracted wings and storeys are the parts of the MutationRecord its cause.mutation names; or the plots of a join or split — Works.target), start week, duration in working weeks, WorksTable row read, the event and mutation it shows, and what the ground held before that the model no longer holds (removed parts' rings with heights and roof kinds; removed plot lines with treatments); the drawn state at any week derived, never stored per week; an event with no week, an unscheduled hand edit, generation (creation week shows a finished town; J-A67.47) and the parity presets create no Works; a user's build, demolish or convert stays instant unless scheduled; an engine's demolish makes its tombstone at once while its Works draws the demolition from the kept shell; aborting a change is its undo (§7.4), which removes its Works; cancelWorks (§7.1) ends a running Works at once (change stands, drawn finished); a setAttr on a Works moves its start or duration

wiring.read_by: Works (§2.7); §8.2 states; §7.1 startWorks/cancelWorks; §7.4 undo; V06; V08

items.statement: Works (2) stage at a week: stageAt(works, w): e = the working weeks in [start, w) — weeks the calendar row does not pause for the Works' material in the town's climate (WorksTable.pauses: masonry, stone and brick pause in winter in temperate and cold climates; our own rows) — f = min(1, e ÷ duration); the stage is the kind's latest scheduled stage whose start fraction ≤ f, before for w before the start and finished at f = 1; weeks integers (a stage shorter than a week never drawn); a tent's zero-week duration applies finished in its week; at most one Works runs on a target: a new change on it ends the running one at the stage reached, which the new one takes as its before (a repair begun on a decaying house runs back from DECAYING)

Works (3) durations (item 67 (b); J-A67.43): WorksTable rows keyed by kind × class (or the template's works key §10.2) × size (storeys, footprint) × material give a range of working weeks; duration drawn once uniform in the range × the labour factor of the plot's band (richer, faster), on the works concern (key §6.1; J-A67.61; J-A67.42); defaults (own, calibratable §13.9): hovel or shed 1–2 weeks; small timber house 2–6; town house 8–17; stone house 17–52; manor 52–156; church 520 or more; a cathedral built part by part (choir, transept, nave, towers, each its own Works in programme order; choir in use under a temporary roof while the nave rises); demolition a quarter of its build's range; clearance 1–4; a decay Works the decline table's dwell band for its step × 0.6 for timber and thatch; material a duration row only — time, never shape (§2.6; J-A31.42 stands for replaceability)

Works (4) stages (item 67 (c)–(f)); start fractions per class row; what each draws is §8.2's states rows: build (and each wing or storey an extension or adaptation adds) — STAKED 0 · GROUND BROKEN 0.05 · FOUNDATIONS 0.15 · WALLS RISING 0.25 · ROOF FRAMED 0.75 · ROOFED 0.85 · FINISHED 1; extension — kept building in use throughout; added wing through build stages; at ROOF FRAMED old roof opened where the two join; at FINISHED joint wall opened and wings united; demolition — EMPTIED 0 · STRIPPED 0.2 · ROOFLESS SHELL 0.4 · RUBBLE 0.7 · CLEARED 1; decay (§2.8's ruin ladder downward) — toward decayed: ABANDONED 0 · DECAYING 0.5; then decayed is ROOFLESS, ruined COLLAPSED, cleared or reused OVERGROWN; repair — decay stages backwards under a scaffold to the former state; fire — an instant destructive event (rung 3's trigger): building decayed in its week, drawn CHARRED until a clearance or repair starts; conversion with no geometry step — REFIT 0 · FINISHED 1; ruin stages are the existing ladder's drawn stages (J-A8.46; no new Existence value); target keeps its ladder state from the event on and carries its running Works by Building.works (§2.6)

Works (5) decay Works carries the dwell band (J-A67.46): a vacate (building abandoned) starts a decay Works toward decayed whose duration is its dwell band drawn once; the lottery's decay candidates are buildings whose decay Works has run its span; the strike's decay event (building decayed) starts the next toward ruined the same way; a reoccupy ends it and starts a repair; a building left abandoned or decayed by an undated event (hand edit) gets its decay Works from the next epoch, starting at that epoch's week

Works (6) mutation steps (J-A67.49): a Works shows its event's MutationRecord in the record's order — subtracted parts by the demolition stages first, then adapted parts, then added parts by the build stages — each part's span a share of the duration by its footprint area; kept parts stand; a rebuild is a demolition then a build, one Works; the epoch-spread mutation's events each start their own

Works (7) plots in transition (item 67 (g); J-A67.44): a join or split decided when its event lands (plot rings change then — ownership) and the ground follows the work: each removed boundary line drawn from the Works' kept lines, dashed as pending removal, until the joined plot's build reaches GROUND BROKEN (or a demolition reaches RUBBLE); a new dividing line drawn as stakes, dashed, from STAKED and as its fence or wall from WALLS RISING; item 31's subdivide and amalgamate run through the same stages; access is the event's, so a Works never leaves a plot without access

Works (8) what reads the stage: heights at a stage derived, heightsAt(works, w): WALLS RISING raises the eave storey by storey (eave × storeys reached ÷ floors), no roof before ROOF FRAMED (drawn as a framed roof), finished roof from ROOFED, a demolition lowering them in reverse; stored heights stay the finished building's, so §8.4's shadows and §11.1's 3-D export follow the stage; households an event placed are housed at a week only from FINISHED, and a demolition's have left before EMPTIED (item 17's relocation, J-A17.41): the module's occupancy, lit windows (§10.3) and light sources (§4.7, §8.4) read that; the plan rung of a building in progress draws walls without doors or furniture, of a ruin its fallen walls and open rooms (§2.6); the stage counts among the plan rung's recorded inputs, so a stage change marks a derived plan stale and §8.5's change marker shows it (item 67 (j)); descriptions say "being built", "being demolished", "ruined since …" (§10.4); the city band draws the stage glyph on the footprint, the neighbourhood band walls, scaffolds, frames and rubble (§8.5, §8.2)

Works (9) which week is drawn (J-A67.45): every drawing, export and reader draws the document's current week unless the per-viewer view key week (§2.9) names another — a host setting its campaign week, or a user scrubbing — outside every digest; scrubbing draws every live Works and every Works finished within works.retainWeeks (52) at that week over the current model, forward and back, byte for byte; the full history at an earlier week is the log's replay (§7.4); an epoch retires Works finished more than works.retainWeeks before its week: the record leaves the model, its target's lifecycle event keeps the weeks

Works (10) restraint (item 67 (i); J-A67.48): an epoch's Works start at weeks spread uniformly over its span (the offset the works concern's draw before the duration's, §6.1), so the share of stock under works follows the growth or decline rate by construction; a ConditionOverlay (§2.7; staged, empty in the base; item 88) scales the share of an epoch's changes it starts as Works once the port fills it (a siege stops building); with no epoch and no scheduled edit nothing runs; static baseline byte-identical (item 23)

type WorksStage = before|staked|groundBroken|foundations|wallsRising|roofFramed|roofed|finished | emptied|stripped|rooflessShell|rubble|cleared | abandoned|decaying|roofless|collapsed|overgrown | charred|refit

interface WorksRow {key (class id or template's works key §10.2); kind: build|extend|demolish|repair|convert|decay|clear; storeys?: [n, n]; footprintM2?: [n, n]; material? (duration row only; never a shape input); weeks?: [n, n] (working weeks drawn once; absent on a decay row, whose span is the decline table's dwell band × 52); factor? (decay row's material factor: timber and thatch 0.6); stages: {stage: WorksStage; from: fraction}[]}; interface WorksTable {rows; labour: {band; factor}[]; pauses: {material; climate; seasons[]}[]; retainWeeks: 52; enabled: boolean (false in the parity presets)}; WorksTable lives in @plat/tables (works.json, §14), editable with provenance (§7.6); its decay rows read the decline table's dwell bands, never a second number
items.note: WorksRow.kind uses 'extend'/'demolish'/'convert' while the stages table names 'extension'/'demolition'/'conversion' — naming variance (minor)

items.statement: Markets over epochs (item 24): a secondary market the roster's suffix adds is claimed by the epoch's S7b in the new stage or in a due district by §4.5 S7b (3)'s rule; a market whose institution closes (the use step) keeps its square — a plaza or market_green — until a clear or a claim reuses it, so no market moves by wealth change alone
items.note: restates S2 (0076)

items.statement: Informal clusters over epochs (item 70 (e); J-A70.48): a cluster grows by accretion — delta households of its band placed on an informal plot add structures by §4.7's packing on the plot's free path sites, each a build Works of days (a shack) or less than a week (a tent, finished in its week); rung 1's densify … infill on an informal plot adds structures that way too; a destructive circumstance event (rung 3's trigger) burns a cluster fast — structures decayed and drawn CHARRED in one week, then cleared; when its district's band rises past the hysteresis a cluster is cleared or formalised by rung 3 in the due epoch (replaceability immediate): households re-homed by item 17's relocation or re-let, plot cleared, re-cut by S10 (7) into row-house plots and built by S11 at the new band; in decline, a vacant, cleared or ruined plot of a district whose value fell past the hysteresis takes tenure informal and may take a cluster; each step an event of this section's kinds; the engine scheduling them is the staged one
items.note: "Works of days" vs integer-week rule (Works (2)) — see conflicts

items.statement: Lights, deposits and conditions over epochs (items 68, 88): a light follows its host (§4.7 Light sources); an epoch re-runs the light rows on its new and changed faces only; a DepositSite (§2.7; staged, empty in the base) whose state changes converts the land use it anchors: depleted or removed — its quarry, mine or claypit abandoned and drawn worked out (a deposit depleted at creation drawn so from the start); discovered — a new outside site sited by S12a's rows at that epoch; a ConditionOverlay is read as Works (10) states
items.note: restates §4.7 lights (5) (0385)

items.statement: Strategy registry (§14): every layout stage runs behind a strategy: TerrainStrategy, CoastStrategy, RiverStrategy, ManifestStrategy, NetworkStrategy (the fused base; american/ringed; a village would add a tracker walk), EnceinteStrategy (the base's S5a pull-and-simplify; a village's palisade), FabricStrategy (BentCutFabric now; NG's templates at stage 2), PlotStrategy, SitePlanStrategy, BuildingGenerator (§2.6), EvolutionStrategy (§4.11)
items.note: TerrainStrategy, CoastStrategy, RiverStrategy, ManifestStrategy, PlotStrategy, SitePlanStrategy: no interface signature in this unit (named only)

items.statement: interface StageDecl {id: StageId; inputs: DataKey[]; outputs: DataKey[]; streamKeys: string[]; invariants: Invariant[] (each with its scope, §5.3); ladder: Ladder; workLimits: WorkLimits (laws over the batch scope's population-derived counts, §5.1 (5)); budgetMs: Record<Rung, number> (reporting only); batch: BatchScope; lineageUnit: EntityKind (§6.3); lazy: boolean (only under the §4.1 contract); txForm: 'declared'|'callback' (§3.3; op form per stage §4.1)}; §14's Stage extends it

wiring.read_by: §4.1 DAG sort; §14 Stage; §5.3 invariants; §5.1 work limits; V07 village stages; V04/V05 stages

items.note: earlier CF-PIPE-02 resolved (§4.1 now points here)

items.statement: interface NetworkStrategy {grow(site: Site, destinations: Destination[], terrain: Terrain, water: WaterSet, enceintes: Enceinte[] (traced before growth; the strategy consults them at every step and places gates where it meets them), existing: Network | null, stage: number, ctx: StageContext, k: Kernel): KernelResult<Network>}

interface EnceinteStrategy {trace(boundary: Polygon, gateSites: GateSite[], reservations: Reservation[], terrain: Terrain, water: WaterSet, policy: {waterfront: 'open'|'quay_wall'|'sea_wall'; placement: 'aroundAll'|'aroundStage'}, ctx: StageContext, k: Kernel): KernelResult<Enceinte>}

The pipeline order is the topological order of the registered StageDecls (§4.1), so a product may add a stage by registration alone (PART III); every district's SeamContract is complete from milestone 1 (G-P1): the view over the Seam records it shares with its neighbours plus its own boundary plot lines and alleys and interior field samples (II.1); shared geometry is owned by the base; PART II's district → neighbourhood interface reads the contract; nothing in PART II needs a base change; what the base must already carry is listed in II.5 and is a base requirement here
items.note: restates §4.1 registration (0003)

items.statement: The one placement solver (PlacementSolver, §4.7 S10b) and the designation mutator (DesignationMutator, §4.7 S11) are registry strategies too (§14 StrategyRegistry): a product may register another implementation by name, and S10b, S11, every assignment path (§7.7) and the use step (§4.11) resolve the registered one

The owner-staged layers register the same way — SkyStrategy after S7b, SewerStrategy after S11, and after the network stage UndergroundSystemStrategy (the void systems), UndergroundStrategy (the sewer-front neighbourhoods), UndercityStrategy and last UndergroundLinkStrategy, each by declared I/O (II.6, II.7.3–II.7.6) — and the base registers none of them
items.note: hooks with volume other ends

items.statement: §10 plain words: as in FTG every building has a purpose and people: the town starts from how many people live there and what such a town needs (our own tables), places needs onto plots by rules, derives households and people on demand; what drawing and editing need is in the base; hourly schedules, calendar, factions' meetings and events are an optional module over the same ids, so the one-click map never waits for a simulation
items.note: plain-words summary

items.statement: Base must-haves (J-9; J-S adopted): the sequential roster (S2) with its need propagation over the supply edges (§4.2 S2, §10.2), the per-plot context vector, the eager allocation (S7b, S10a), the one placement solver with the relation templates (S10b, §4.7), the designation templates and mutator (S11, §4.7), the Use record with its hand relocation path (§2.7, §4.11), households and people derived lazily from their keys, typed open spaces, rule-placed landmarks and furniture, a gazetteer via query
items.note: list restates §4 mechanisms

items.statement: Base schema from M1, materialised by the module: the relation store (family units, relations, memberships, postings), sub-locations, factions with roles and goals, religions, the government's offices (§2.7), and the economy and personality schema stubs of D-32 (§10.3); the supply edges that place a workshop near its suppliers are base placement data (item 16), while prices, stock and trade volumes remain the module's (D-32)

Optional module @plat/sim (delivered at M4b §16; never gating milestone 1, never in the one-click path): professions ↔ workplace matching, occupancy and schedules as a query, the calendar and clock with external time sync, factions' and religions' meetings, events as templates, relations by the family-unit model; schedules and the calendar are not in the base (J-9); restraint: the map stays a clean plan, content in data, hover, the gazetteer and export; one click never asks a questionnaire
items.note: TERM conflict risk: "calendar and clock with external time sync" (module) vs §4.11 "The clock — weeks" and "no second calendar exists" (see conflicts)

items.statement: The content locality contract (FTG-9; J-P21): content is global and relational while regeneration is spatial: (1) the allocation is persisted and a scoped regeneration re-places only its own scope's allocation — global rebalancing is a separate, reported action; (2) once the module has materialised the relation store, a scoped regeneration changes no relation outside the scope: relations of people whose households were superseded are carried over by the household's address (§6.3) or dropped and reported; (3) the locality oracle and O2 (c) cover content and relation hashes as well as geometry; the relation store's schema is in the base, its data materialised once by the module and then persisted; the one-click path never pays for it

interface RosterTables {classes: BuildingClassRow[]; districtKinds: DistrictKindRow[] (relation templates of the neighbourhood kinds, item 16 (a)); resources: ResourceRow[] ({id, kind: site|made|import} — resource ids the supply edges name); institutions: InstitutionRow[]; government: GovernmentRow[] (offices and seat classes per government kind); religions: ReligionRow[]; households: HouseholdRow[] (size distributions by class); professions: ProfessionRow[]; farm: FarmTable (§4.9); roomProgram: RoomProgramRow[] (item 28); basementGate: BasementGateRow (item 29 (b)); covers: CoverRow[] (item 63); classMix: ClassMixRow[] (item 71); clusters: ClusterRow[]; tenure: TenureRow[] (item 70); quarterIdentities: QuarterIdentityRow[]; powerLinks: PowerLinkRow[]; sectorLinks: SectorLinkRow[]; bandRanges: BandRangeRow[] (item 72); sectors: SectorRow[] (item 78: sector set the economy slice is keyed by); portRows: PortRows (item 88: staged rows the port fills — schema-complete, empty, extension); names: NamePack; provenance: Provenance}; row types of items 70–72, 78, 79, 82, 88 declared with defaults in the closing paragraphs
items.note: WIRING: InstitutionRow, ReligionRow (read by religion rule), ProfessionRow (module), HouseholdRow, ResourceRow, sectorLinks — check readers; sectorLinks vs BuildingClassRow.sectors duplicate?

items.statement: interface BuildingClassRow {id; use; perCapita: [n, n]; perOther?: {class; ratio}; min; max; firstAtPopulation; requires: (water|coast|route|farmland|ore|stone|timber|fish|clay)[] (site-resource gates S2 reads from SiteResources); outside; liveIn; cluster?; noxious; lifestyleBand; shopProb; priority; relations: RelationRule[] (item 16 (a)); produces: string[]; supply: SupplyEdge[] (item 16 (b)); template: DesignationTemplateRow[] (one row per band; item 19); useRules: UseRuleRow (item 17); secondaryChance? (market rows, TOWN chance of a secondary market); salvageM3: Record<string, number> (item 8); drain: none|pit|channel; underground: never|allowed|preferred; undercity: never|allowed|preferred (item 65); undergroundAccess: {prob: Record<string, number> (item 64: per band row, the chance a basement within reach of an underground element holds an access, II.7.3)}; concealment?: ConcealmentRow[] (item 63); distribution: district-defining|dispersed|singular; significance; powers: {kind; weight}[]; sectors: {sector; weight}[] (items 72, 78, 79; weights summing to 1 per column); subLocations: SubLocationRow[]; openingHours: OpeningRow[]; tags: string[]}

items.statement: interface RelationRule {kind: adjacent|near|far|sameStreet|clustered|avoid (to another class, cluster tag or feature class) | upwind|downwind|upstream|downstream|nearWater|highGround|lowGround|dry (environmental: ContextVector.upwind, upstream, terrainClass, dist.water §2.5) | frontage|nearGate|nearMarket|nearHarbour|nearCentre|extramural|intramural (access: roadClass, dist.*; nearest of N markets, item 24) | plotArea|plotShape|frontageM (capacity against the template's size budget) | band|exposure (prosperity band; Plot.exposure and knownTo, item 30); to?; withinM?; beyondM?; min?; max?; values?; falloff?: step|linear|smoothstep; strength: hard|soft; weight (soft rows: score at full satisfaction; hard rows 0); extension: boolean (a row the references lack, scaled by placement.extensionWeight)} — read by the placement solver (§4.7 S10a, S10b) and, for district kinds, §4.5's typing scorer

(item 67: WorksTable row key); households {built; max} (item 31); entrances {side; rear; service; capSide; capRear; yardDoorMinM2} (item 29); cellar {prob; kinds {full; half; walkout}; slopeCm; rockCost; depthCm (default 220); insetCm (default 60)} (item 29 (b))}

interface ConcealmentRow (item 63; our own rows, extension) {band? (absent: every band; interpolate like every band row); districtKind? (absent: every kind); weights {none; front; hidden; underground} (non-none weights extension, scaled by placement.extensionWeight, 0 in parity presets); hiddenWithFront (share of hidden and undercity placements that also take a front, drawn on siting); accessMultiplier (item 64: × the access probability of a surface building carrying this concealed use, II.7.3; default 6)}

The sequential roster (FTG-14; J-P20): FTG's documented shape, none of its 209 types, 80 nodes, 299 professions or 323 items; a virtual population advances on a fixed grid of Δ = 10 people up to the rung's maximum; at each grid point every class's target count is a monotone step function of the virtual population — perCapita or perOther ratios converted to per-person ratios, core versus shop pools, lifestyle-banded pools with rare outliers (weights ours), hard min/max, size gates (firstAtPopulation), resource gates from SiteResources (no farmland → no farms, shops instead) — every class below its target receives its next building in class-priority then class-id order; every draw keyed by the building's ordinal (roster/<class>/<ordinal>: shop or core, lifestyle outlier), so the n-th chandler is the same at any population; the run records each building's appearance population; manifest(P) = every (class, ordinal) appearing at or below P

wiring.read_by: S2 manifest; delta demand §4.11; need propagation

items.statement: Roster prefix stability: manifest(P₂) ⊇ manifest(P₁) whenever P₂ > P₁ (property test on 1 000 seeds, §13.2); an epoch's delta demand is exactly the suffix; a population fall selects the suffix in reverse order; negative deltas arise only from declared circumstance events; §7.8's population control is monotone by construction

Roster mode (COV-FTG-B06): rosterMode 'minimiseUnemployment' (default: at each grid point, when the unemployed share of the virtual population exceeds a table threshold, the workplace class with the largest weighted job deficit receives one extra building) or 'matchRatios' (configured ratios only, FTG's alternative); both grid-sequential, both prefix-stable
items.note: threshold value not given

items.statement: Roster output: demand per class with area/frontage requirement classes, district affinities, cluster tags, live-in flags, outside flags and wealth bands; the town-level character shifts the ratios — read from the economy slice's sector shares (circumstances.economy, §7.7 layer 2) through each class's sectors weights, so one input drives both the roster and the neighbourhoods' economy dial (items 72, 78; an even mix, the neutral default, shifts nothing)
items.note: restates S2 (0078, 0084)

items.statement: Government (COV-FTG-B13): the blueprint's government circumstance selects a GovernmentRow whose offices force seats — a crown seat a royal castle or palace; a seigneurial lordship a lord's castle or keep; an ecclesiastical lordship a bishop's palace beside the cathedral; a chartered commune a town hall and guild halls; a merchant oligarchy a merchants' hall — plus a military share (guard posts per 1 000 inhabitants; barracks at CITY and above near the castle or gates); the castle toggle auto reads it
items.note: guard post rate value not given

items.statement: Religion (COV-FTG-B14): religions from ReligionRows with worshipper shares (shifted by the town-level character), a practice share and clergy per 1 000; temples per religion proportional to its practising worshippers; each religion has a faction (§2.7)

S7b then allocates the demand and S10b places it (§4.5, §4.7); where capacity is short, placement's reconcile and F-SITING's ladder decide, surplus capacity typed as yards, greens or vacant plots (§4.7 S10b); population honoured within tolerance and reported (O7 a, e)
items.note: restates §4.7 S10b reconcile (0323); earlier CF-PIPE-04 now consistent

items.statement: Relation templates, supply edges, designation templates, use rules (items 16, 17, 19; rows are data §7.6, re-signed by the corpus phase §13.9): a class's relations are the rows the solver filters and scores by (§4.7 S10a, S10b); its produces and supply are the resource and dependency graph S2's need propagation walks and the solver measures distance on; a neighbourhood kind's rows serve §4.5's typing scorer and a whole-neighbourhood assignment (§7.7); default rows are the references' placement rules where a reference has one and soft tendencies where it has none (item 23; extension: true, scaled by placement.extensionWeight)

Default relation and supply rows (examples): a tannery downstream hard, nearWater hard, extramural soft, supply hides 800 m by street and bark 2 000 m by road; a brewery supply malt 1 000 m by street (hard) and nearWater soft; a maltings supply grain 3 000 m by road; a bakery supply flour 600 m by street; a warehouse nearHarbour 150 m hard with supply import by sea; an inn frontage primary or through hard and nearGate 150 m soft; a market hall nearMarket 60 m hard; a trade group's shops sameStreet and clustered soft; a mill nearWater hard with a fall (its outside row, §4.9)

The template rows are S11's (§4.7); useRules §4.11's use step's; the produces of the outside classes — grain, timber, fuel, stone, ore, fish — are the hinterland's food, fuel and timber rows (§4.9, item 26); no row of this table names a material: a material is a rendering attribute (§2.6), and §4.11's WorksTable alone reads it, for durations — time, never shape (item 67)
items.note: CONFLICT candidate: "no row of this table names a material" vs DesignationTemplateRow? (materials in MaterialRow §2.6) — consistent; but WorksRow.material — WorksTable not a roster table: consistent

items.statement: Markets, wealth bands and countryside rows (items 24, 26, 27): the market class row demands markets by size — min 1 (principal), firstAtPopulation 10 000 and perCapita one per 12 000 for secondaries, secondaryChance 0.15 at TOWN (our own rows; §4.2 S2; §13.5's anchors MFCG's secondary plazas and FTG's two market squares) — and the market hall's and market trades' rows cite the market they serve by rank (nearMarket, principal by default); HouseholdRow.band and every class row's lifestyleBand name a band of §4.5's band set; household shares' default weights FTG's captured lifestyle distribution (provenance ref:FTG lifestyle distribution) shifted by the town-level character; every band-keyed row set may omit bands, which interpolate (item 27); farm table fuel and timber rows, farm modes and outside classes' seeding rows are §4.9's
items.note: restates S2 market numbers (0075)

items.statement: Under a fall (AM-8): a population fall selects the suffix in reverse ordinal order and its households leave by §4.11's step (c) — a relet down, vacate at the last household — never removing a building by arithmetic; standing stock follows with §4.11's dwell lag; a later rise reoccupies the same suffix first; BuildingClassRow.salvageM3 is the class's material yield when robbed, cleared or dismantled and the debit of a build or repair of that class, read by §4.11's ledger
items.note: restates §4.11 (0472 step (c), 0521)

items.statement: interface RoomProgramRow {for {cls; band; use?; era?}; rooms: RoomRuleRow[]; pattern: Record<basement|ground|upper|top, {weight; pattern: LayoutPattern}[]> (§2.6's layout patterns per storey class); circulation {num; den} (integers: the share of a storey given to halls and corridors — §2.6's capacity reads it exactly); stair {placement: by_entrance|rear|centre|tower; kind: StairCore['kind']}; basementAccess: core|trapdoor (derived into Basement.access for a non-walk-out cellar, read at builtBand — never external, which only a walk-out's fall derives; the plan rung reads Basement.access); furnish {density; wallBias}} (items 28, 29, 31; J-A28.43, J-A29.41)

interface RoomRuleRow {role: RoomRole (§2.6, data-defined); scope: unit|shared|service|circulation (item 28 (f)); count {n; law: const|perHousehold|perStorey|perCapacity|perSubLocation; capacity?; tag?}; area: [min, target, max] m²; storey: any|ground|upper|top|basement; exterior: none|some|max; door: door|arch|open; maxDoors?; adjacency: {kind hard|soft; to core|entrance:main|entrance:yard|RoomRole; via? direct|corridor|under}[]; priority: hard|soft; hearth?; concealed? (item 63: placed by the plan rung away from the main entrance, reached only through a service, yard or concealed door); furnish {density; wallBias; glyphs}}

interface BasementGateRow (item 29 (b); one row per table version) {waterTableM (default 40: within this distance of a shore the water table is the nearest water body's surface plus the freeboard); freeboardCm (default 50); drainageAccumCells (default 100: flowAccum at which a hydro cell is the drainage line elsewhere, §2.3; our own, calibratable)}

The room programme lists the rooms a building of that class, use and band must and may have — each with its size band in m², storey, openings, adjacencies and count (fixed, per storey, one per household of item 31's relet, or a sub-location's capacity) — which §2.6's plan rung writes first and then cuts the walls to fit (item 28), so rooms are never cut before the programme is known; programme rows follow §2.6's interior ladder (item 28 (f)): the ladder's row for the occupants' band gives the cross-class structure (households the shell holds, each unit's rooms, shared rooms, staff rooms and their size, circulation form, room size limits) and a class's programme row adds what a smithy, inn or chapel needs; programme read at the occupants' band (field band, J-A19.43) and the households column at builtBand (shell's capacity §2.6), so the interior has no floor while the shell keeps its own (§4.11)

LayoutPattern, StairCore and RoomRole are §2.6's; role names our own data rows (hall, chamber, solar, parlour, kitchen, buttery, common room, cooking place, staff chamber, corridor, stair hall, forge, shop, store, undercroft, chapel, nave, passage …); the plan rung's plan.program stream draws the fractional part of a count law (§6.1), as plot.join draws a join (§7.7)
items.note: "plot.join draws a join (§7.7)" — plot.join is S10 (7)'s/clusters' stream (§4.7); check §7.7 reference

items.statement: Households per building follow the roster's households — with a dossier, the households filling its population, map facts derived from its population and circumstances (§7.7 derivation table; item 20 (h)) — and item 17's relocation (§10.3); the households row and the shell's floor area bound the ladder's relet through §2.6's one capacity function, which the generation fill (§4.7: S10b's placement, S11's clamped write), relet and F-PLAN (§5.2) all read; with no epoch every residential building houses what §4.7's fill gives it — at least one household and never above its capacity — static baseline unchanged (item 23)

Every column is data with provenance, editable and calibratable (§7.6, §13.9); entrance rows default to one street entrance per building — the owner's rule (item 29; provenance owner): FTG's 2026-09-25 capture sends no door (its road-facing anchor a night light, item 50), MFCG's model carries no door record (an inference) — with side, rear and service doors as our tendencies (extension, 0 in parity presets, item 23); the cellar rows are item 29 (b)'s class rows whose extensions §2.6's emulation note names; the reference's basement share is a descriptive baseline only (§13.5)

drain, underground, undercity, undergroundAccess columns (II.7; items 12, 14, 64, 65): BuildingClassRow.drain is the drainage need: none (tents, sheds, hovels), pit (households and most workplaces: a cess pit or own street gutter), channel (trades and institutions discharging foul water: tanners, dyers, fullers, brewers, slaughterhouses, baths, hospitals, monasteries); underground names which classes a sewer-front underground neighbourhood may hold or prefers (II.7.3); undercity which classes the undercity may hold or prefers (II.7.5) — preferred for its microcosm: black market, fence's hall, criminal guild's seat, tavern, forbidden shrine, fighting pit, healer; allowed for dwellings of the squalid and poor bands and the small trades serving them; never for the rest

wiring.read_by: II.7.1 drain rule; II.7.3; II.7.5; V04

items.statement: undergroundAccess.prob per band row interpolated along the value: the chance a surface building of the class whose basement reaches an underground element holds an access down to it (II.7.3 Basement accesses) — higher for breweries, bathhouses, warehouses and inns (0.15–0.30 by band), low for houses (0.02, raised with the plot's age by II.7.3's age term), 0 for a barracks, courthouse and temple; a user adds an access to any building by item 66's edit (§7.3 item 9); which plots a network connects, what a class does when none exists and how the underground rows are used are II.7.1's, II.7.3's, II.7.5's rules; every non-never, non-zero cell an extension (no reference has an underground)

concealment column and cover table (item 63): BuildingClassRow.concealment gives, for a class our tables mark clandestine (thieves' den, assassins' house, smugglers' store, forbidden cult, black market, spy ring), its default-mode weights per band and district kind (ConcealmentRow: front, hidden, underground weighted against none; default rows weight front highest in every band, hidden next in the poor and squalid bands, underground where an underground allocation may exist), the share of hidden and undercity placements that also take a front, and the multiplier on the access lottery; RosterTables.covers gives each concealed class its weighted plausible fronts per band (assassins' house behind a tavern, fencing hall or apothecary; smugglers' store behind a warehouse or chandler's; thieves' den behind a tavern, pawnshop or bathhouse; forbidden cult behind an almshouse, bathhouse or bookbinder's …); RoomRuleRow.concealed marks concealed rooms; every row our own and an extension, so parity presets conceal nothing; how read is §4.7's Concealed institutions
items.note: restates §4.7 concealed (1), (3) partly

items.statement: Rows of items 70–72, 78, 79, 82, 88: every row our own, calibratable (§13.9) and an extension — zero, a step or empty in the parity presets (item 23) — unless it says otherwise; how each is read is the section named beside it

interface ClassMixRow (item 71; one row per band; a band without a row interpolates) {band; weights: {cls (residential class id); weight; wealthShift (× (wealthLevel − 0.5))}[]; prestige: {frontage: tier1|square|park|corner|water; weight}[]}

interface ClusterRow (item 70; by band × climate × era) {band; climate?; era?; kinds: {cls: shack|tent|lean_to_shelter; weight; footprintM2: [n, n]; depthM: [n, n] (drawn on siteplan; §4.7's footpath web spaces by the row's largest upper end)}[]; householdsPerStructure: {rung; range: [n, n] (drawn on siteplan)}[]; pathWidthM; fireGapM: {rung; m}[]; wholeBlock (share of eligible blocks S10 (7) joins into one informal plot); relations: RelationRule[]}
interface TenureRow {band; informal: boolean (this band's plots with no standing building but shacks, tents or lean-tos are informal)}

interface QuarterIdentityRow (item 72 (d′)) {id; families: {family (class tag); weight}[]; threshold; perHa?; bands?: [lo, hi]; priority; singular; power? (power kind its quarter dial follows); sector?; kind? (S6 kind an epoch re-types a district to past the hysteresis); definedBy? (a district-defining class: identity a dossier instance claims); targetShare?; magicOnly? (admitted only where the magic circumstance is not none or the dossier lists an arcane power); naming (the naming slice its names draw from, §10.4)}

interface PowerLinkRow {element: gate|wall|tower|bridge|road|quay|market|tollHouse|customsHouse; powers: {kind; weight}[]} (item 72 (d″): the infrastructure's powers); interface SectorLinkRow {element; sectors: {sector; weight}[]} (item 72 (d4): infrastructure's sectors)

interface BandRangeRow {band; lower: [floor, ceiling] (district in the band's lower half); upper: [floor, ceiling] (upper half)} (item 72 (d‴), §4.5 (5)); interface SectorRow {id; tags: string[] (class tags whose classes serve the sector by default)} (item 78: the sector set CircumstanceSlice.economy is keyed by, §7.7 layer 2)

interface PortRows (item 88; staged rows the dossier port fills §14 — schema-complete, empty in the base) {impairments: {type; physical; conditionSteps (a physical type's condition steps per severity band on the building, §7.7's F4 row; a non-physical type's steps per unit of severity on the impaired institution's own dial term, conditionSteps × severity × dial.conditionStep, §4.5 (6))}[]; hinterland: {importPct (0–1); foodChain: Record<string, boolean>; farmlandScale (§4.9's arable demand × max(0, 1 − importPct × farmlandScale))} | null; crime: number | null ([0, 1]; §4.6's staged crime term — factor of its hidden share, II.7.3's access, II.7.5's undercity demand); customKinds: {kind; criticality?; economicWeight?; defenseRoles?; powerAuthorities?; fallbackClass (class a custom kind is built as)}[]; legitimacy: number | null (on the government record: × the governing power's amplification in §4.5 (6)'s institution dial, 1 while empty)}
items.note: WIRING GAP: PortRows.customKinds (all fields) and hinterland.foodChain have no reader named in the base (0613 lists five readers, none for these)

items.statement: Class mix default weights (item 71): squalid hovel 0.8, row house 0.2; poor hovel 0.3, row house 0.6, cottage 0.1; modest row house 0.6, cottage 0.2, house 0.2; comfortable row house 0.3, house 0.6, town house 0.1; prosperous house 0.5, town house 0.35, manor 0.15; rich manor 1.0; wealthShift manor +1.0, town house +0.5, house 0, row house −0.3, hovel −0.6; prestige weights tier1 1.0, square 0.8, park 0.6, water 0.6, corner 0.4; parity presets make each band row one class (its class rows' lifestyleBand pool, a step at each cut); shack, tent and lean_to_shelter rows are the cluster's structure classes, never drawn by the class mix (J-A70.49)
items.note: wealthShift for cottage not listed (cottage appears in poor/modest rows) — missing value

items.statement: Clusters and tenure (item 70): squalid shacks 0.5, tents 0.4, lean-to shelters 0.1; poor shacks 0.7, lean-to shelters 0.2, tents 0.1; footprints shack 6–20 m² (depth 3–4 m), tent 6–15 m² (round or oblong, depth 3 m), lean-to shelter 4–12 m² (depth 2 m); households per structure 1 at TOWN, up to 2 at CITY, up to 3 at METROPOLIS in the squalid row; poor row 1, 1, up to 2; pathWidthM 1.2; fireGapM 1.0 (squalid row 0.8 at CITY and METROPOLIS); wholeBlock 0.2 in the squalid row, 0 otherwise; relations nearWater and the lee of walls and ruins, soft; the shack, tent, lean_to_shelter class rows (distinct from the lean_to frontage treatment): drain none, replaceability immediate, cellar 0, one floor, a programme of the one-room unit with no circulation, households from the cluster row; tenure squalid and poor informal: true
items.note: tent footprint 6–15 m² agrees with §4.7 tents row (0334)

items.statement: Distribution and significance (item 72): distribution singular for the cathedral, a great temple, the palace, the castle, the university and the principal market's hall; district-defining for the dossier kinds that are districts (red-light district's brothels, slums, foreign quarter, guild district); dispersed for every other class; significance cathedral, great temple, palace 30; castle 20; university 15; church 8; guildhall, town hall, market hall 5; chapel 3; inn 1.5; workshop 1; shop 0.5; lodging house 0.3; house 0.2; cottage 0.1; shack and tent 0.05
items.note: §4.5 (3) names singular "the great market" vs here "the principal market's hall" — see conflicts; lean_to_shelter significance not listed

items.statement: Quarter identities (item 72): religious quarter (families religion; chapels and churches 1, cathedral or great temple 3; threshold 3; power religion; kind temple); craftsmen's quarter (craft 1; 0.6 per hectare; power guild; kind craft); merchants' quarter (trade and warehouse 1; threshold 5; bands prosperous to rich; power company; sector trade); harbour quarter (harbour 1; threshold 4; kind docks); garrison quarter (military 2; threshold 4; power military); learned quarter (learning 2, a university 5; threshold 5); arcane quarter (arcane 1, a mage tower 3; threshold 3; power arcane; magicOnly — the row a Mages' Quarter naming claim biases toward, item 82); defined districts (red-light district definedBy its brothels, targetShare 0.15, no kind — §4.5 (3) scores its district by the brothel class row's soft nearHarbour within 300 m, nearGate within 200 m and near an inn within 100 m rows, our own and extension (J-A72.51); slums definedBy the dossier's slum kind, kind shanty, the squalid band's rows); plain residential identities one per band, lowest priority; each row's naming slice is our naming pack's (§10.4)
items.note: priorities per row not given (only "lowest" for plain)

items.statement: Powers and sectors (items 72, 78, 79): classes' powers column — guildhalls and workshops guild; merchant houses and warehouses company; churches, chapels, temples religion; castle, manors, keeps lordship; town hall and courthouse council; barracks and guard posts military (item 79's kind); mage towers and alchemists arcane (item 79's kind, only where the magic circumstance or a dossier arcane power admits it); clandestine classes criminal — each an association the dossier's Institution.powers overrides (§2.7); powerLinks: gates 0.5 military, 0.5 council; walls and towers military; bridges, roads, quays council; the market square council; toll and customs houses council; sector set: trade, taxes and tolls, crafts, agriculture, extraction, fishing, finance, religion, military, magic, crime; classes' sectors column and sectorLinks: markets, warehouses, quays → trade; gates, toll houses, bridges, roads, walls, customs house → taxes and tolls (0.7) with trade (0.3) on gates, bridges, roads; workshops and guildhalls → crafts; farms, mills, granaries → agriculture; quarries and mines → extraction; fisheries → fishing; moneylenders → finance; churches → religion; barracks → military; mage towers → magic; clandestine classes → crime
items.note: walls → taxes and tolls (0.7) with trade only on gates/bridges/roads: walls' remaining 0.3 unspecified (weights must sum to 1 per column) — possible gap

items.statement: Band ranges (item 72): squalid: squalid–poor in both halves; poor: squalid–modest; modest: poor–comfortable; comfortable: modest–prosperous; prosperous: comfortable–rich (middle band to rich, item 71's mix); rich: prosperous–rich in its lower half, rich alone in its upper half
items.note: consistent with §4.5 (5) examples

items.statement: Notice posts (item 82): a notice pin at the principal market and each gate plaza by default (§4.7's furniture step), at the main entrance of every class whose tags hold notice (a town hall, a market hall, a guildhall), and wherever a named-feature claim of the dossier names one (§7.7)
items.note: restates §4.7 notice posts (0399)

items.statement: The port's staged rows (item 88): portRows declared in full and empty; a row the port fills acts only through the reader its comment names (the hidden share of §4.6, the farmland of §4.9, the access of II.7.3, the undercity's demand of II.7.5 and the dials of §4.5 (6)); while empty every factor is 1 and every list empty
items.note: customKinds and foodChain name no reader → one-ended (wiring defect)

items.statement: Households and people: a person is a pure function derivePerson(seed, key, tableVersion) of its key (household address, member ordinal, birth epoch) — the address is what survives a re-derivation of the household's plot (§6.3), whereas the household's lineage changes on New random — and of the person tables current when its household was created (Household.tableVersion); yields name, age, status, role, ancestry, height and appearance

Pinning is an explicit edit, never a view (LC-16, FTG-10; J-P22): opening a person in the gazetteer writes nothing to the document, the hash or the undo stack; which people a viewer has seen is per-user view state (§2.9); a table edit applies to households created afterwards; existing people change only through a diffed "re-derive people" action (§7.5 pattern)
items.note: "re-derive people" action: its edit kind/tool not named here (§7.1?)

items.statement: An epoch ages everyone by its years through the key's birth epoch; births and deaths are epoch events of the owner-staged evolution engine; when regeneration supersedes a household, its pinned or edited people are fixed inputs re-homed by rule to the household that inherits its address (§6.3), or reported as orphans (their edit-lifecycle row is §7.4's)
items.note: births/deaths event kinds: base declares none (V06 other end)

items.statement: Storage: aggregates plus explicitly pinned people — kilobytes for a 50 000-person metropolis (FTG PERF-1; R14) — until the module materialises the relation store, after which relations and postings persisted (≈12 bytes per relation in the binary block; ≈1.8 MB raw for 50 000 people at ≈3 relations each, reported per 10 k population as the O7 module metric)

People model (COV-FTG-C01, COV-FTG-C08): AncestryRow {id, lifeStages: {name, fromAge}[], maxAge, heightCmBand, nameGrammar, appearanceTemplates} and a partnering matrix (pair weights and the child's ancestry rule) are data; the realism base ships one human ancestry; further ancestries only through setting packs (§10.4); Person.status ∈ worker, unemployed, retired, student, dependent; a dependent has a carer whose schedule it follows; when a carer is removed the household (then the family unit) supplies the next carer by rule and the change is reported — a dangling carer is a reference-integrity violation (§5.3)

Appearance (COV-FTG-C02): appearance text from the §10.4 engine — weighted option tables per ancestry, line templates with substitution, conditional lines (by gender, age or a value predicate), fallback lines and article agreement — our own templates

The module @plat/sim: Relations (FTG-9, COV-FTG-C04) — first run materialises the relation store by one global pass on its own stream (content/relations) in person-key order (family units, partnerships, parent/child, siblings, carer/caree, friends, rivals, business and religious ties, affairs), persisted with lifecycle and reference integrity (§10.1 locality contract); Work (COV-FTG-B11) — professions ↔ workplaces by greedy matching with id tie-breaks, persisted as Posting records; after an edit only postings of changed workplaces and the unemployed pool re-matched in person-key order; unfilled postings tracked and reported

Sub-locations and occupancy (FTG-11): occupancy(dayType, hour) resolves the whole population in person-key order in two passes — primary behaviours (home, work, study, care, following carers) from profession templates, then occupancy criteria (leisure, guest workers, temporary residence) filling SubLocation capacities with their relax options — cached per (day type, hour), invalidated by edits touching the people or buildings involved; whereIs(person, day, hour) reads the cache; resource provides/uses edges on roster rows are data the schedules may read; budget §12.7's
items.note: "provides/uses edges" naming vs BuildingClassRow.produces/supply

items.statement: Calendar (module): a configurable calendar (hours/day, days/week, rest days, weekday names); the time is the view key time, set by view.set {time} and advanced by the module's sim.advance {hours} over the bridge (§11.3); occupancy recomputed for the new hour; neither changes the model or logs an event
items.note: TERM: module "calendar" vs §4.11 CalendarRow "no second calendar exists" (see conflicts)

items.statement: Factions (COV-FTG-B12): seats on plots, an influence field over districts (used by the prosperity drivers and the grammar), named roles with member criteria (predicates over person fields) and counts, goals with methods and progress, a secret flag; role headcounts reconciled with the seat building's working capacity (excess roles filled by members housed elsewhere; reconciliation reported); government offices and religions are §10.2's
items.note: CONFLICT candidate: "influence field used by the prosperity drivers" (module) vs §4.5 dials needing no module and §10.1 "never in the one-click path"

items.statement: Events (COV-FTG-C05): EventTemplate {id, preconditions (predicates over relations, factions, buildings), weight, effects: EditEvent[]} rank candidate events per building; starting one applies its effects as logged, undoable edit events; data dictionaries (ages, genders, ancestries) append-only and id-referenced (renaming never re-colours; FTG DAT-3 avoided); the relation store answers the family-tree query (§11.2)

Economy, personality and stat-block schema stubs (D-32; COV-FTG-B10, COV-FTG-C03, COV-FTG-C11): in the base registry from M1, empty until @plat/sim materialises them; every table our own: ItemRow {id, category, unit, basePrice (setting pack's coin unit), providedBy? (roster class ids)}; ServiceRow {id, providedBy, basePrice}; Stock {building, item, qty}; PriceTable {multiplier, overrides} (global price edits are editTable events §7.6); PersonTraits {traits, motivation, mannerism, hobbies, education} (derived from the person key); StatBlockPack {id, attributes, base, professionModifiers} (a named game-system pack, off by default, D-3)
items.note: stubs empty in base: consumers are the module only (intentional one-ended, WIRED-BY module)

items.statement: Uses that move (item 17): when a use relocates (§4.11) its live-in household (Building.dwelling) moves with it when the destination's designation template has a residential slot (a structure with houses, §10.2; §4.7 S11) and otherwise stays in the vacated building as an ordinary household, reported; its people keep their keys, the household address surviving (§6.3); the module re-matches only the postings of the closed and opened workplaces and carries business ties over by the use's address; a household re-homed by item 31's re-letting takes the same path

Lit windows (item 68): at the view's hour (time key) the module's occupancy selects lit windows — a building lit while its sub-locations hold anyone awake at that hour; without the module a dwelling is lit in the lighting row's evening hours (lights.windowHours, 17–22 h default; our own row, extension) while its households live there at the drawn week (§4.11's Works), and a workplace during its openingHours rows (§10.2); window lights derived per view — §8.4's derived sources, never records; the FTG preset lights each lit building at its main entrance only (§4.7 Light sources)
Cluster households (item 70): a cluster structure houses the cluster row's households per structure (§4.7, §10.2); their people derive as any household's
items.note: restates §4.7 clusters (4)

items.statement: Standings (item 79): the module's faction influence field takes its weights from the base's power standings (CircumstanceSlice.powers, §7.7 layer 2) — the inputs the base's dials read (§4.5 (6)), which need no module; a dossier-backed Person (§2.7; staged with the port, item 88) is pinned, housed by rule in the district of its institution or its power's seat, and never derived away
items.note: "housed by rule" — the rule is not stated here

items.statement: Hours are not weeks (item 76): the module's calendar counts hours for the time view key; it is never the map's week (§4.11's clock) and never compared with it
items.note: restates §4.11 (0500); resolves the calendar/clock term collision

items.statement: The naming engine: an original English-fantasy grammar (D-6) in a Tracery-class engine of our own (rules with modifiers, feature guards, weighted decks, conditional lines, article agreement) plus syllable and Markov generators over corpora of our own authoring; folk-contraction as an EVO event (FTG's erosion idea; "≤ 3 syllables" a parameter); names drawn from the naming concerns only (§6.1) and only in §6.3's cases, a successor keeping its predecessor's name and naming record; names never move geometry; uniqueness follows §9.6
items.note: "EVO event" — event kind name not defined elsewhere in the unit (folk-contraction)

items.statement: The same engine writes descriptions — a district's one-line summary of its mix and features (e.g. a waterfront quarter that also holds workshops and a green; COV-FTG-E10), each building's description (§2.6) — and people's appearance lines (§10.3); descriptions regenerated when their inputs change unless edited

Per-culture generators and user lists (COV-FTG-L06): every AncestryRow and culture row names its own grammar and corpora (personal and place names differ by culture); a user-uploaded list (plain text, one entry per line) becomes a user corpus: a syllable and a Markov model trained at load, stored in the document as pack data with author user, selectable wherever a corpus is; selecting it is an adjust of the recipe's pack list entering it as user:<content hash> with shipped: false (§2.9, §7.6), so a town whose history selects it never emits a link (§6.4); the pack holds the corpus and the keyed row operation setting the chosen corpus field of the chosen culture or ancestry row; selecting it re-draws exactly the unedited names drawn from that field, listed for confirmation (§6.3 case (4)), never the row's other names (each corpus field its own naming slice, §7.6); deselecting is a second adjust; how long its content stays is §2.9's pack-set rule
items.note: earlier CF-PIPE-06 and NP5-3 now resolved in text

items.statement: Setting packs (DEF-10): interface SettingPack {id; version; author; date; licence; provides: {grammars?: GrammarDef[]; corpora?: {id; kind: personal|place|word; entries}[]; ancestries?: AncestryRow[]; religions?: ReligionRow[]; appearance?: TemplateDef[]; rosterPatch?: {table: RosterTableId (classes, districtKinds, resources, institutions, government, religions, households, professions, farm, roomProgram, basementGate, covers, classMix, clusters, tenure, quarterIdentities, powerLinks, sectorLinks, bandRanges, sectors; never portRows, which only the dossier port fills); baseVersion; ops: RowOp[] (§7.1)}[]; tablePatch?: {table: TableId (naming, culture and ancestry tables); baseVersion; ops: RowOp[]}[]; styleHints?: Partial<StyleSheet>}}
items.note: RosterTableId list omits names (NamePack) and provenance of RosterTables — intended (names via tablePatch)

items.statement: A pack is data, never code: schema-validated (zod), every entry carrying author and date (clean-room rule §17), loaded as one layer of the override chain between the shipped defaults and the preset (§7.6), recorded in the recipe or in the adjust that adds it by id, version and content hash; the content of every pack of the document's pack set not shipped with the output version is copied into the document's packs block and retained by §2.9's pack-set rule, so a replay never depends on what is installed; a link emitted only when every pack of the pack set is shipped (§6.4)

A pack's roster patch and table patch are keyed row operations, never positional — the RowOps of §7.1, each set carrying the hash of the base row it was written against (baseRowHash) and the table version it targets (baseVersion), orphaned and reported exactly as a user override is (§7.6; LC-22) — so a newer table version never silently misapplies a pack; a user corpus pack is {corpora: [the uploaded list], tablePatch: [one set on the chosen culture or ancestry row's corpus field]}; the base ships exactly one pack, our original English-fantasy set; further packs are the owner's adopted default "setting packs later" (D-6); adding one is a file, not a code change
items.note: "setting packs later" — deferral-like wording quoting D-6 (adopted default, not an open choice)
