items.statement: The allocation (S7b (7), §4.5): where an undercity exists — predicted at S7b, when every void source is predictable: caverns from S1's geology flag, catacombs from the religious rows and their sources' ages, quarries from the stone resource and the roster's predicted stone stock, vaults from the arterials and bridges S4 laid, a buried town from the log or at generation from the history scar II.7.6 reads — S7b creates its Allocation after (6) and before (1): H households (squalid first, then poor), the undercity 'preferred' classes, and the clandestine institutions whose mode is underground (preferring the undercity over a sewer dwelling where both exist); capped by the predicted capacity; ground districts receive the remainder (population whole — nobody added by the underground, c′ (1)); a miss between prediction and built voids absorbed by S10b's plan–fit–reconcile and F-SITING's ladder, reported, never re-rolled

wiring.reads_or_produced_by: geology; religious rows; stone; S4 ways; history scar

items.note: restated §4.5 S7b (7)

items.statement: A shadow, not a second city (item 65 (c′); owner quote; J-A65.44): (1) its people and institutions are the settlement's own (the dossier's where one exists); population totals include them; (2) each neighbourhood shadows a surface district: a pseudo-district (District.kind = 'undercity', §2.5) in its void's part, with a parent link to the surface district above the largest share of its main chamber in plan (ties by address) — the district that feeds it; joins §9.1's quarter tree under its parent's quarter node, named as the underside of that quarter by §10.4's undercity naming (J-A65.40), never a rival town; prosperity = the parent's field sampled at each plot shifted by undercityOffset (−0.35), banded by the town's FieldBands (II.7.3's pattern); (3) its economy is the surface's shadow: black market trades the town's goods; S10b's supply edges run to the surface markets, docks and outfalls, measured from each undercity plot along its walkways to its nearest lifeline and on from the lifeline's ground point (the solver's street mode through the lifeline); (4) nothing of its own to govern it — no government, walls, gates, rung or identity of its own; settlement circumstances (disorder, crime, government) drive it; (5) it changes as the settlement changes: at each epoch its size law re-read, a change taking effect only past hysteresis (0.1 of H), a new neighbourhood opening only in its void's free capacity; its blocks follow their parent's due marks through §4.11's wealth ladder (item 31); chambers and galleries flood, collapse or are sealed by II.6's condition table, a chamber's plots following it as II.7.3's follow their tunnel; clearUndercity (the authorities' clearance, by an epoch or by hand) vacates one neighbourhood's plots — households leaving by §4.11's step (c), institutions relocating by the use step — while its chambers stay
items.note: "no identity of its own" vs District.identity (item 72) for kind 'undercity' — S12c on pseudo-districts undefined (see edges)

items.statement: Where it lives (item 65 (e); J-A65.44): an undercity neighbourhood lives in the arena part of its void source (a cavern, quarry, catacomb, vaults or buried-town part, II.7.6) — never in the sewer's part 0 (U1–U3 hold there), never in a part of its own (its chambers are its source's; nothing copied between parts, J-A12.43; J-A65.31); the undercity stage runs S9–S11 on that part by the kernel's one cut (J-A65.32): its streets are gallery chains of its own — walkways laid across a chamber's floor and the source's galleries it adopts — banded by corridorUnion; a chamber's floor cut by S10's frontage-first machinery on those walkways' kerbs and on the chamber wall (plots may end on the chamber_wall); the main chamber stays unplotted as its plaza, the black market's stalls its pins (§4.7's market pins); S11 admits row, hovel, cluster (item 70) and institution (UndercityRule.arrangements), carved rooms and repurposed vaults being row cells against the chamber wall; heights ceiling-capped: eaveCm = min(class storey height × floors, chamber's ceilingCm − ceilingClearCm (30)), one floor or more where the ceiling allows, roof kind flat, no sky; every district, plot and building an ordinary record on its part, editable by every edit kind of §7
items.note: ceiling cap formula differs from II.7.3's (0738: min(class storey height, headroom + vaultAllowance)) — two cap shapes (elegance candidate)

items.statement: Its outskirts: the sewer-front blocks of II.7.3 whose tunnel runs lead into the undercity — within outskirtsReachM (150 m) along open tunnels from a link that joins it — belong to its neighbourhoods: each undercity district lists them (District.outskirts §2.5), a link between records in two parts (J-A65.31); their plots, geometry and allocation stay part 0's under U1–U3, and they are named, described and counted with the neighbourhood
items.note: restates II.7.3 (0742)

items.statement: Lifelines: the connection stage (II.7.6) realises the undercity's lifelines before any lottery: the nearest candidate access, air shaft and water link are made (open, or secret by the row) first; a neighbourhood left without one fails condition 4 and is dropped, its allocation re-placed by the reconcile, and with none left there is no undercity — each drop reported
items.note: edge defined (all dropped → none)

items.statement: Undercity light (item 68 (d′); owner quote: a lot of light sources, no sun or moon): the underground layer has no global light and near-zero ambient; the undercity's rows of §4.7's light table (LightRule, arena underground, system undercity) are the densest of the layer — a light at every door (windows lit by §8.4's derived window lights), along walkways (gallery rows, arena underground) at a spacing tighter than any surface street, clustered in the market chamber and around its institutions, braziers and fire pits in the larger chambers — the fuel by the settlement's circumstances (tallow and pitch, lamp oil; magical lights only where the magic circumstance admits them); every lifeline breaking the surface is a light shaft (§8.4), so its brightest spots at noon lie under its shafts
Undercity emulation (item 65 (f)): no reference generator has an underground: every row here is an extension; the parity presets set maxNeighbourhoods to 0

Undercity order, seed and locality: UndercityStrategy registers after the void systems and the sewer-front neighbourhoods and before the connection stage, by declared I/O — inputs the void systems' parts, the ground plat (read), the three field rasters, the undercity Allocation and the rows; outputs its districts, blocks, plots, buildings and walkways — runs eagerly on the generation worker after the pool's merge (J-A12.46); existence and size draws on sewer keyed by the settlement's lineage; each neighbourhood's streams derive from its district's lineage, itself from its parent's (§6.3), through ordinary concerns (plot.*, siting, siteplan, heights; §6.1); writes only its void's part, so a New random of an undercity neighbourhood leaves the ground and every other part byte-identical, but for the far link_end vertices of its links, which the connection stage re-derives by one transaction on each such part (§3.4)
interface UndercityExistenceRow {existence: never|law; maxNeighbourhoods: 0|1|2|3; minPopulation?; chance? (TOWN 0.2)} — RungProfile.layers.undercity (§1.1)

interface UndercityRule (one editable rule record §7.6; own, calibratable, extension; parity presets maxNeighbourhoods 0) {share: Partial<Record<Rung, number>> (u: TOWN 0.01, CITY 0.02, METROPOLIS 0.03); povertyRef 0.022; maxBandShare 0.6; disorderGain 1; householdsPerNeighbourhood 120; minHouseholds 20; m2PerHousehold 40; mainChamberM2 400; minInstitutions 2; undercityOffset −0.35; ceilingClearCm 30; outskirtsReachM 150; hysteresis 0.1 of H; arrangements default [row, hovel, cluster, institution]; presets: Record<historical|navigable, {maxNeighbourhoods (a cap on the rung row: 1 and 3); sources: UndergroundSystem['kind'][] (historical: vaults, catacomb, quarry, buried; navigable: all); shareScale (0.5 and 1)}>}
items.note: values restated from prose

items.statement: interface ClearUndercity {op: 'clearUndercity'; district: Id (one undercity neighbourhood)} — a conversion kind (§4.11's union names it): its plots vacated, households leaving by step (c), institutions relocating by the use step; chambers kept

interface UndercityStrategy {derive(doc, systems: UndergroundSystem[], allocation: Allocation (S7b (7)'s), rules: UndercityRule, ctx, k): KernelResult<{districts; blocks; plots; buildings; walkways: Gallery[]}>} — a Stage registered after the void systems and II.7.3's stage by declared I/O; runs S9 → S10 → S10b → S11 on each neighbourhood's void part; the StrategyRegistry's underground map (§14)

One layer, several systems (item 65 (a); J-A65.31, J-A65.42): the underground layer holds the derived sewer network (system kind sewer, part 0) and beside it systems each an UndergroundSystem record (§2.7) with kind, source, arena part and depth range: catacomb, cavern, quarry (quarries and mine voids), vaults (cisterns, street and bridge vaults), buried (a buried old town), dug (private passages an access edit or an undercity lifeline's closure digs, item 66); each its own arena part of the underground layer (§3.4): sewer keeps part 0, every further system takes the next unused part number when first created — at generation in the stage order, one system per kind; a buried system when a raiseGrade first makes one or at generation from a history scar; a dug system at the first closure needing one (§7.3 item 9 (d)) — stored on the record (UndergroundSystem.part), counted by the document's nextUndergroundPart (§2.9), never renumbered or reused (the number is part of its entities' keys and addresses, §6.3)

One system per kind: two catacomb complexes that meet join, as galleries of one kind may; what passes over or under without meeting belongs to another kind and so another part; inside one part every plan crossing is a junction (§3.4), so no rule lays an element across another of its part without meeting it: a catacomb or quarry laid beside a complex of its kind joins it at a common depth band; a dug connector's path search treats every other building's dug passage as a foundation (step 3); a drawn gallery or chamber that would cross one of its system's at another depth band is refused by its dry run naming the crossing (F-EDIT, §5.2; J-A65.47)

System elements: galleries (Gallery §2.7: a chain at the part's L1 with widthCm, wallCm, headroomCm from its system row, banded by corridorUnion as a tunnel is, §3.7) and chambers (Chamber §2.7: a void wider than a band — ossuary, cavern hall, quarry room, cistern — a closed outline chain carrying the chamber_wall role, its floor an L1 face; J-A65.32), each with its floor elevationCm and its ceilingCm

Depth bands: every gallery and chamber keeps its own depth inside its system row's depthM range (catacombs 3–10 m, vaults 3–8 m, quarries 10–30 m, caverns 5–60 m following the rock, a buried town at its old grade, dug passages 2.5–6 m) and never above the ground less its system's coverM; inside one part depth is per entity (J-A12.45); systems in different parts pass over and under one another; the view groups every part's items into the depth bands of depthBandCm (II.7.3), so the layer draws and exports as one (§8.4, §11.1), a crossing of two parts drawn over and under
items.note: coverM values per system not given

items.statement: The derivations: each system is a registered stage with declared I/O (§4.12; UndergroundSystemStrategy) running after the network stage in the order catacombs, caverns, quarries, vaults — then at generation a buried old town where a history scar makes one — each reading the ground and part 0 through the services only (J-A12.32) and writing its own part; every draw on sewer keyed by the system's lineage and the element's source (§6.1; no new concern); every system gated to TOWN and above (PART III) and by its row's chance per rung — a history scar's buried town by the buried row's scarSeverity instead, drawing nothing; the chances 0 and the scar rule off in the parity presets

Catacombs: from cemeteries' and churchyards' sources: churchyard parts of church and temple plots (§4.9 churchyard row), crypted classes (underground 'preferred': crypts, §10.2) and religious precincts and monasteries; a source qualifies when its ground is not damp or flood (water table of §2.6's gate values) and its age reaches minAgeYears (100) — at generation (K − k + 1) × yearsPerStage for a source built in growth stage k of K (§4.4; yearsPerStage 50, §4.2 S2), replaced by the staged HistoryHint.ageYears when the port fills it (item 88) and by the log's years since its use opened after epochs — and holds a catacomb with the row's chance by source kind and rung (crypted church 0.6; churchyard 0.25 at TOWN, 0.4 at CITY, 0.5 at METROPOLIS; precinct 0.4)
items.note: "replaced by HistoryHint.ageYears" — which source's age (all sources get the settlement age?) ambiguous

items.statement: Catacomb extent = ossuary need A = Σ_years servedPopulation × burialRate ÷ 1 000 × ossuaryShare × m2PerBurial — population its source serves (town's population history × the source's share of its religion's temples, §10.2; at generation each growth stage's population at its built share), burialRate 30 per 1 000 a year, ossuaryShare 0.1, m2PerBurial 0.05 — laid as galleries on a grid of gridM (6 m) under and beside the source within reachM (80 m), an ossuary chamber at every fourth crossing, and an entrance stair from the source's building (an AccessPoint of source system); a catacomb as large as its town's dead and as old as its church

Caverns: from geology: where S1's geology flag (Terrain.geology, §2.3) is soluble or volcanic, over the frame's rock (S1's rock, high and mid terrain classes), a cavern system exists with the row's chance (soluble 0.7, volcanic 0.4); soluble rock: galleries along the terrain's drainage lines beneath the rock (§2.3 hydro cells whose flowAccum passes the row's threshold) at the local water table — a gallery below it carries water (Gallery.water) — with a hall where two galleries meet under high relief; volcanic rock: one to three tubes descending from high ground along steepest descent with breakdown chambers; extent capped at maxRockShare (0.1) of the rock area; a gallery meeting a slope's face or a bank opens there as a cave mouth (AccessPoint kind mouth)
items.note: closes wiring of the geology flag (only reader)

items.statement: Quarries and mine voids: from S1's stone resource and the town's stone stock: volume taken = the wall volume of the stock whose material is stone (§2.6's material rule read as a quantity of stone, never a shape; J-A65.45) and of the enceinte's walls and towers × wasteFactor (1.6); workings laid on the frame's stone cells (SiteResources.stone ≥ 0.5) ranked by stone value, then nearness to the town, within reachM (2 km), under the town first where its own ground holds the stone (as the old quarries under Paris), as room-and-pillar galleries on a roomM (5 m) grid leaving pillarShare (0.35) of the rock; area = volume ÷ headroomCm (250); a working whose cover would be under minCoverM (6 m) is left to the hinterland's surface quarry (§4.9) and laid nowhere underground; a shaft opens at each working's centre (AccessPoint kind shaft); mine voids read SiteResources.ore the same way, only where the roster holds a mining class
items.note: "area = volume ÷ headroomCm (250)" mixes units (m³ ÷ cm) — must read headroom in metres (2.5 m): unit ambiguity

items.statement: Vaults: cisterns and street and bridge vaults: under every bridge approach whose way rises over the ground beyond the banks, under way segments on slopes steeper than vaultSlope (0.12) where a street is carried on arches, and a cistern under the oldest precincts and the castle where dist.water exceeds cisternDistM (400 m) — each a chamber or a short run of vaults under its way or precinct, under public ground only (II.7.3's surface constraint applies)

A buried old town (item 65 ruling 5; J-A65.46): the conversion kind raiseGrade (§4.11's union names it) applied by an epoch (staged engine) or by hand (convert, §7.1): S1's terrain operator raises the region's ground by raiseCm (≥ 200 cm, a storey); the region's ways, plots and buildings at the old grade end on the ground (existence cleared, §2.8) and fresh records of the buried part are the system's elements — each old way's centreline a gallery, each old building's ground storey a chamber, each new record a fresh entity of the buried part minted from the conversion event's seq and ordinal (§6.3), the cleared records keeping their addresses on the ground (an address names its part; no batch writes two, §3.4) — while the ground above is re-derived on the new grade from the old centrelines (regrowth-first §4.11: streets keep their lines, buildings rise on their plots); the conversion records the system it created or extended in RaiseGrade.system, so a replay after a log truncation reads its part number there, as a closure's ClosureRecord.created does (§2.9); an undercity in it walks the old town's streets under the new

Buried town at generation: none exists unless the port fills the staged HistoryHint (item 88) with a fire or flood scar (the RaiseGrade.cause types §4.2 S2 routes here) of severity ≥ the buried row's scarSeverity (0.5): the most severe such scar (ties: the oldest, by yearsAgo) makes one buried system, in the systems' stage order after vaults, gated to TOWN and above — its region the districts whose growthStage is 1 (its sources, §2.7), its galleries that region's way centrelines and its chambers their buildings' ground storeys, fresh records of the buried part (system's lineage children, §6.3), floors laid at scarBaseCm + scarGainCm × severity (200 + 200 × severity) cm below the present grade; the town above generated on the present grade as it stands, no raiseGrade event recorded, nothing cleared, the rule draws nothing (our own rows, calibratable, extension the parity presets turn off); with the hint empty, none

The connection graph (item 65 (d); J-A65.47): a link (UndergroundLink §2.7) joins two elements of different parts — each end one vertex in its part carrying the link_end role (§2.2 rule 7), never a vertex two parts share (J-A65.31) — with a kind (open, gated, secret, collapsed, flooded), a via (breach, stair, shaft, door) and a knownTo; surface links are AccessPoints (II.7.4); the connection stage (UndergroundLinkStrategy) runs last, after the undercity: (1) the undercity's lifelines (II.7.5) first; (2) for every pair of elements of different systems within linkReachM (10 m) in plan and linkDepthM (8 m) in depth — found by reads across parts — one link per pair within linkSpacingM (60 m), existing with the row's chance for the pair of kinds (sewer–vaults 0.6, catacomb–quarry 0.5, any–buried 0.5, sewer–catacomb 0.3, sewer–quarry 0.3, cavern–quarry 0.3, sewer–cavern 0.2, others 0.2; our own); (3) its kind drawn by the row's weights (open 0.3, gated 0.25, secret 0.25, collapsed 0.15, flooded 0.05 — flooded only below the water table); (4) its knownTo secret for a secret link or a link into a building with a concealed use, else local; (5) II.7.3's basement accesses (item 64); a link's kind follows the elements it joins (II.6); every link an edit target (add, delete, setAttr on kind and knownTo, §7.1)
items.note: link "kind follows the elements" (derived reading) vs drawn kind collapsed/flooded stored — two ways a link reads collapsed

items.statement: The same engine (item 65 (e)): every system laid by the kernel's one cut (J-A65.32): galleries as chains banded by corridorUnion, chambers as closed outline chains; plots and buildings exist only where a system hosts people — the sewer's frontage (II.7.3) and the undercity (II.7.5); a catacomb's, cavern's, quarry's or vault's chambers carry none unless the undercity takes them; every element an edit target (draw, move, delete, setAttr on kind, depth, width, state and knownTo; II.6's conversions and flood); every rule a data row (§7.6); the seed survives edits (§6.3); the dossier stays the authority for institutions (item 20); every element fades by II.6's condition table

Underground systems' light (item 68 (d′)): catacombs dark but for shrine and ossuary lamps at the chamber altars; caverns dark but where lived in (a glowing-fungus row only where the magic circumstance or the biome allows); quarries and vaults dark but at their shafts and where lived in — §4.7's light table, arena underground and the system kind; every access or cave mouth breaking the surface a light shaft (§8.4)

The pieces an access edit generates (item 66; owner quote; the closure rule — one event whose batches commit together, the record of what it created, exact undo, shared pieces kept — is §7.3 item 9's; J-A66.41): addUndergroundAccess(building, target?) (§7.1) calls generators in dependency order at its dry run, each drawing on sewer keyed by the building's lineage, the target's and the event's seq (§6.1; minted as J-A18.43 mints), so the same edit on the same seed gives the same pieces: (1) the basement — §2.6's basement decision with its probability forced (the request overrides the chance, never the terrain gate): a full cellar where the gate allows, else a half cellar or walk-out on a slope, else a hatch to a crawl space under a raised floor (§2.6's requested-mode ladder), else a refusal naming the gate (F-EDIT §5.2), never silent (J-A29.22); (2) the target — the named element, else the most plausible reachable: an open navigable sewer tunnel or an underground building's wall within accessReachM, then within digReachM (60 m) the nearest open gallery or chamber of a catacomb, cavern, quarry or vaults, or an undercity walkway — ties by plan distance then address

wiring.read_by: closure record; V09 tool; V10 clerk

items.statement: (3) The connector — when the target lies beyond accessReachM: a dug passage, a gallery chain in the dug system's part, routed by the kernel's path search (§3.1) on the frame's grid from the basement ring to the target — cost infinite within foundationClearM (0.5 m) of every other building's footprint, basement ring and dug passage and wherever the water table (§2.6's gate values) lies above the passage's floor, rising with the rock class — inside the dug row's depth range, below the street's services (network coverCm, II.7.2) and above the water table; a route longer than 2 × digReachM is a refusal with the reason
items.note: edge: target beyond digReachM but route ≤ 2 × digReachM allowed?

items.statement: (4) The system itself — where no underground element lies within digReachM (a town without sewers, a village): the minimal private underground, the dug system with one passage to the most plausible outlet by the building's outlet row (default: another cellar of the same owner within reach, a catacomb or cave the site has, the riverbank, the shore, beyond the outermost enceinte; with a concealed use: beyond the walls, the riverbank, the shore, a catacomb or cave) — its outer end an AccessPoint of kind mouth, or a door into the other cellar; the settlement's sewer rows unchanged (a dug passage is no network, Features.sewers untouched) while Features.underground turns true (II.7.4); (5) the access point — II.7.4's record, its kind by the drop (II.7.3 Basement accesses (3)), state open, knownTo by (4), source edit; (6) the plan — the plan rung reserves the stair, ladder or hatch in the basement plan (§2.6, item 28), building's plan rung marked stale; (7) the links — the connection graph gains the new links, typed (open at a dug passage's two ends)
items.note: "(a town without sewers, a village)" — villages: PART III says every system gated to TOWN and above; a dug passage at a village allowed by edit (edge: village rungs admit dug by edit only)

PART III plain words: the village generator is a separate product staged after the town, with its own ladder (thorp → hamlet → village); this page lists what it would take from the base, the hooks the base carries now, and confirms nothing stands in its way; the base does not pay for it

What the village would reuse unchanged: the kernel and plat (§2–§3); the site model — descent-traced rivers with a carved field, level-set ponds, the coast routine (§4.2) — and, for VG's own order, a RiverStrategy that lays a terrain-independent spline course first (VG's live course runs through 6–7 control points laid before its terrain; COV-VG-WC2) and asks S1 to carve the field to it, which S1's carve step already does; the sequential roster and lazy people (§10); the frontage-first plot machinery and the designation templates (§4.7 S11, §10.2), which already contain cottage, farmstead and detached-in-yard classes; the hinterland presets incl. the VG sector look, orchards and commons (§4.9); the palisade enceinte kind (§2.7); the display list, style sheets, the base's relief tier (hillshade, contour, hachure marks) and the reserved painterly preset slot (§8.2); the document, edits, exports and the API (§7, §11)
items.note: hook list; RiverStrategy has no signature in the base (named only)

items.statement: Village hook (1) (DEF-15): a density stage before its network (COV-VG-VN-002): the pipeline is the topological order of declared stage I/O (§4.1, §4.12), so a VillageStrategy registers a density StageDecl whose output the network stage declares as an input; VG computes its density before its roads, and the base's S6 order does not bind it
items.note: VillageStrategy: named only (no interface in base)

items.statement: Village hook (2): a palisade before its roads (MN-4, COV-VG-VN-003): on VG 1.6.9 the palisade is built before the roads — the hull of the populated points of a 10 × 10 lattice over the density field, cleaned and smoothed — and the road trackers consult it at every step (steering: a per-type terrain weight plus terms for water, the destination's pull and the wall's push — reader-tier, for the village rung's calibration; provenance row D5, item 61), gates falling where they meet it (profile-village.md N2, P1); the village registers an EnceinteStrategy that builds exactly that from its density stage, and its tracker-steered NetworkStrategy receives the result through the enceintes input every network strategy takes (§4.12)
Village hook (3): a tracker-steered network (VG's roads are steered trackers, not A*) with one through-road and partial driveways, and a "houses along ways" FabricStrategy with no block cutting

Village hook (4) One district (COV-VG-WC4): a village is modelled as one district of kind village (one quarter) covering the settlement; its blocks are the large faces between ways and its plots line the ways, so the containment invariant building ⊂ plot ⊂ block ⊂ district holds unchanged and nothing in §2–§4 needs a village exception

Village hook (5) a size ladder below TOWN: rung rows THORP ≈ 20–80, HAMLET ≈ 80–400, VILLAGE ≈ 400 up to (not including) 1 500 inhabitants (our own rows, calibratable; VG spans ≈ 130–1 700); a request of 1 500 or more is a base TOWN and below 1 500 LadderRouter routes to the village product (§1.1, D-33); a village request's default is not a walled circle (walls a rule keyed on rung); VG's independent tree stream is a keyed sub-stream (already the design); VG's spotlight vignette and grass-tuft look are painterly programs — the hillshade, contour and hachure marks are the base's relief tier (§8.2), built at M2b (§16), so the village adds none (COV-VG-VN-029)
items.note: canonical rung bounds live in §1.1 (check agreement: THORP/HAMLET/VILLAGE bounds)

items.statement: Not-precluded checks (the parity judge's 44/44): the strategy registry admits every strategy above; the level model tolerates nearly empty L2/L3; model time is near-linear in building count; every VG rendering row has a program or a preset slot; terrain-and-water-as-one-picture is the base's own model; what the base does not pay for: tracker steering, the palisade construction, VG's spotlight and painterly look, the palisade look, VG's grammar and its tag vocabulary

Placement and designation (items 16–19): the village reuses the one placement solver with the relation templates and supply edges, the designation templates and mutator (§4.7 S10b, S11; §10.2), whose rows already carry the village classes — cottage, farmstead, mill, smithy, chapel, inn — and the Use record with its relocation path (§2.7, §4.11); a village adds rows, not code

Village rung rows (items 24–27, 30): hidden-share target 0 and reach weights of open only (§4.6; VG's and MFCG's every-house-on-a-way); a market row of min 0 with at most one market — a green or a widened street, sited by §4.2 S3 (12)'s score with the plaza kind absent; farm mode fill (§4.9); band set's cuts computed per village from its own roster shares over its one district (§4.5); §4.11's terrain and water conversions apply unchanged; a concealed institution at a village rung takes the front mode (hidden share 0, no sewer: its fallback chain ends at a front — a working business on an ordinary plot); each is a table row a village supplies, not code
items.note: restates §4.6 and §4.9 village values

items.statement: Layers at the village rungs (AM-13): the village ladder's RungProfile rows carry layers.islands = 'none' (§1.1), so II.6's island rule admits no island below TOWN whatever the prosperity or model setting; a village request never creates a sky allocation
items.note: restates II.6 (2)

items.statement: No sewers below TOWN (item 14; II.7.1): the village rung rows carry layers.sewers.existence = 'never': a village registers neither the network stage nor the underground stage; a request's toggles.sewers is reported as not applicable in requestedVsBuilt; drainage is gutters and pits — the class table's drain column is read by nothing there
items.note: restates II.7.1 row

items.statement: No derived underground below TOWN (items 65, 66; II.7.5, II.7.6): village rows carry layers.undercity.existence = 'never' and derive no catacomb, cavern, quarry, vaults or buried-town system (every II.7.6 system row gated to TOWN and above), so a village's underground layer is empty unless a user asks for an access: addUndergroundAccess (§7.3 item 9's closure, item 66) digs a private passage of kind dug from the building's basement to the most plausible outlet (II.7.6) — the one underground a village can hold, making the layer present without a network (sewers stay never); nothing in II.7 stands in a village's way: every hook is a rung row or a field it leaves empty
items.note: resolves edge in 0787 (village dug passage by edit)

items.statement: A dossier below the town floor (item 81; owner's ruling J80 Q3): a dossier whose population lies below 1 500 is refused by the port (§7.7, item 81: E_RUNG_UNAVAILABLE, naming the village product) while no village product is registered — the dossier's population is a dossier fact and a clamped town would contradict it — so a village-sized SettlementForge settlement waits for the village product's own port path, which registers its rung rows behind the same port (§14) rather than a second one; §1.1's clamp to a 1 500-person TOWN stays for a request that carries no dossier
items.note: restates §4.11 (0509); J80 is an owner-decision id (J80 Q3) — check it resolves in rationale

internal_conflicts.what: Duration of an informal cluster's shack Works. §4.11 'Informal clusters over epochs' makes each added structure 'a build Works of days (a shack)'; §4.11 Works (2) says weeks are integers and a stage shorter than a week is never drawn, and Works (3)'s duration rows give a hovel or shed 1–2 weeks.
internal_conflicts.resolution: State the shack's Works duration by its WorksTable row (the hovel-or-shed row, 1–2 working weeks, or a shack row of its own) and keep only the tent's zero-week, finished-in-its-week case; drop 'of days'.

internal_conflicts.what: Whether an undercity always exists at CITY and METROPOLIS. II.7.5's first sentence says 'an undercity exists in cities and metropolises, and in a large town only where a void source exists'; the same paragraph's rung row gives CITY and METROPOLIS existence 'law', under which it exists only when conditions (ii)–(iv) hold (a void source, H ≥ minHouseholds, conditions 2–4).
internal_conflicts.resolution: Reword the lead sentence: 'an undercity may exist in cities and metropolises under the law, rarely in a large town, never below TOWN'.

internal_conflicts.what: Whether the optional module feeds the prosperity field. §10.3 Factions says the module's influence field over districts is 'used by the prosperity drivers and the grammar'; §10.1 says @plat/sim is never in the one-click path, and §10.3 Standings says the base's own dials read the standings 'which need no module'; §4.5's driver list has no module term.
internal_conflicts.resolution: State that the module's influence field is read by the module's own queries and the naming grammar only; the prosperity field's power terms are §4.5 (6)'s dials over CircumstanceSlice.powers, which need no module.

internal_conflicts.what: 'No second calendar exists'. §4.11 clock (3) says CalendarRow is the one calendar and 'no second calendar exists'; §10.1 and §10.3 give the module 'the calendar and clock with external time sync' and 'a configurable calendar (hours / day, days / week, rest days, weekday names)'. §10.3's last bullet separates them (hours vs weeks) but the two sentences contradict as written.
internal_conflicts.home: §4.11 clock (the week) with §10.3 (the module's hour view clock)
internal_conflicts.resolution: Rename the module's pieces (for example 'the day-schedule table' and 'the hour view key') or qualify §4.11's sentence to 'no second calendar of weeks and seasons'.

internal_conflicts.what: Islands after a rung change. II.6 (2) and §4.11 say a settlement 'that leaves the CITY band' can no longer sustain islands / wanes (AM-13), but METROPOLIS also admits islands (RungProfile.layers.islands possible at CITY and METROPOLIS). Read literally, a CITY growing into a METROPOLIS loses its islands.
internal_conflicts.resolution: Say 'falls below the CITY band (to TOWN or a village rung)' in both places.

internal_conflicts.what: Identity of an undercity neighbourhood. II.7.5 (4) says it has 'no government, walls, gates, rung or identity of its own'; S12c (§4.1, §4.5 (2), (4)) writes every district's character vector and identity, and an undercity neighbourhood is a District (kind 'undercity'). Whether S12c runs on pseudo-districts (hinterland, sky, underground, undercity) is not stated anywhere.
internal_conflicts.home: §4.5 (item 72: the one statement of character and identity) with II.7.5 (J-A65.44)
internal_conflicts.resolution: State in §4.5 which districts S12c covers: the ground districts; an undercity neighbourhood reads its parent's identity (named as its underside by §10.4); the hinterland, sky and underground pseudo-districts take no identity (or state what they take).

internal_conflicts.what: Where an underground-mode clandestine institution is allocated when both an underground (sewer-front) and an undercity allocation exist. II.7.3 (b) lists them in S7b (6)'s allocation 'where an undercity exists they go to it first'; II.7.5's allocation lists them in S7b (7) and says they 'prefer the undercity over a sewer dwelling'; S7b runs (6) before (7). Neither step says (6) excludes them when (7) will exist, so the text admits double allocation.
internal_conflicts.resolution: In S7b (6): 'the clandestine institutions whose mode is underground, except where S7b predicts an undercity, which takes them at (7)'.

internal_conflicts.what: Works kinds. The stages table has a 'fire' kind (CHARRED) and 'conversion with no geometry step' (REFIT); WorksRow.kind is build|extend|demolish|repair|convert|decay|clear — no 'fire', and 'clear' has a duration (1–4 weeks) but no stages row; the prose kind names (extension, demolition, conversion) differ from the enum (extend, demolish, convert).
internal_conflicts.resolution: Add 'fire' to WorksRow.kind (or state that fire is an event with a CHARRED state, not a Works kind), give 'clear' its stages row, and use the enum names in the table.

internal_conflicts.what: The singular classes. §4.5 (3) names 'a cathedral, the palace, the university, the great market'; §10.2's default rows name 'the cathedral, a great temple, the palace, the castle, the university and the principal market's hall'. 'The great market' (a Reservation) vs 'the principal market's hall' (a class); castle and great temple absent from §4.5.
internal_conflicts.resolution: §4.5 (3) cites §10.2's rows ('e.g. the cathedral, the palace, the principal market's hall') rather than its own list.

internal_conflicts.what: Sector weights of walls, toll houses and the customs house. §10.2 gives 'gates, toll houses, bridges, roads, walls and the customs house → taxes and tolls (0.7) with trade (0.3) on gates, bridges and roads', so walls, toll houses and the customs house carry 0.7 in total, while the classes' sectors column is declared 'weights summing to 1 per column'.
internal_conflicts.resolution: Give walls, toll houses and the customs house taxes and tolls 1.0, or state that a link row's weights are renormalised to one.

internal_conflicts.what: S7b's step numbers do not follow its execution order: (4) is drawn 'before (3) cuts the claims', and (5), (6), (7) run 'before (1)'. The numbered list reads as an order it is not.
internal_conflicts.resolution: Renumber S7b's steps in execution order (sky, underground, undercity, town → districts, sub-districts, edge greens, claims) or state the order explicitly at the head of the list.

internal_conflicts.what: Stage words. §4.10 and §4.11 Works (8) list 'being built', 'being demolished', 'ruined since …'; §10.4 lists 'being built', 'being extended', 'being demolished', 'under repair', 'ruined since'. Same fact, three lists.
Unit in the quarry area law: 'the area = volume ÷ headroomCm (250)' divides m³ by centimetres.
